# Tapir

> Tapir is a free, open-source (MIT) add-on for Graphisoft Archicad 25–30, by
> ENZYME-APD and its community. It adds 789 JSON commands to Archicad's own JSON API, a palette
> that runs Python scripts in one click and a Grasshopper plugin (package `tapir` on the Rhino Package
> Manager); community MCP servers let AI assistants drive Archicad through it. A new release ships
> every Monday.

- Site: https://archicad-api.com/
- Source, issues and releases: https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation
- Download (Tapir Installer for Windows and macOS): https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest
- Community (Discord): https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY
- Tapir started in 2022 as R&D at Enzyme, an architecture practice; the add-on is built on Tibor
  Lorántfy's archicad-additional-json-commands template.

## How a Tapir command is sent

Archicad (with a project open) answers JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:19723`. Tapir's commands go
through Archicad's own `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`, in the namespace `TapirCommand`:

```json
{"command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
 "parameters": {"addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": "GetAddOnVersion"},
                "addOnCommandParameters": {}}}
```

The answer is `{"succeeded": true, "result": {"addOnCommandResponse": {...}}}`. Python's standard
library is enough (`urllib.request`); the official `archicad` package and the Tapir Grasshopper
plugin send the same JSON. Every command, with its parameters and an example, is in
[commands.md](https://archicad-api.com/commands.md) and [commands.json](https://archicad-api.com/commands.json).

## Archicad, on *autopilot.*

Number every door along a line. Colour the model by any property. Check a project before it goes out. Tapir adds hundreds of commands to Archicad and a palette that runs scripts in one click.

[Download WINDOWS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Win.exe) [Download MACOS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Mac.zip)

100% free Open source (MIT) [Watch the tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) [All downloads](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest)

**Mon** [A new release every week](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases)

### Start where you *already work.*

Two of the three need no programming. All of them use the same commands.

For architects

#### Scripts in the palette

Open the Tapir palette, pick a script and press Run Script. The built-in scripts are there from the start, and more are shared by the community.

[Browse scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/)

For computational designers

#### Grasshopper

The tapir package in Rhino's Package Manager. Walls, doors, windows and more as components that read and change the model, with the names of Archicad's settings dialogs.

[Grasshopper guide](https://archicad-api.com/grasshopper/)

For developers

#### Python and the JSON API

Every command answers on port 19723, each with a schema and an example. Python's standard library is enough.

[Command reference](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/)

### Six jobs it *already does.*

Five built-in scripts of the Tapir palette and one workflow script, each a short Python file you can read and change.

- Built-in script

#### Number elements along a line

Select a polyline and the doors, zones or objects to number. Each one gets its Element ID in the order the polyline passes it.

Changes the model `SetPropertyValuesOfElements`

[Automatic Numbering Based on Polyline](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline.py)
- Built-in script

#### Colour the model by a property

Pick a property; every element gets a colour for its value, with a legend of the values and how many elements have each. Number values can be grouped into ranges.

Read only `HighlightElements`

[Property Highlighter](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyHighlighter.py)
- Built-in script

#### Check a project before it goes out

Lists elements without an ID, zones with the same number, unclassified and duplicate elements, empty stories and unused layers. Export the list to Excel or turn it into Issues.

Read only `GetClassificationsOfElements`

[Project Health Check](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ProjectHealthCheck.py)
- Built-in script

#### Publish on a schedule

Publishes the chosen Publisher Sets now or on a schedule, every few hours or daily at a set time. It can receive the Teamwork changes and update the drawings first, and logs every run.

Writes files `PublishPublisherSet`

[Batch Publisher](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BatchPublisher.py)
- Built-in script

#### Tidy up the View Map

Finds the views that are neither placed on a layout nor published, and moves the ones you choose into a separate folder that keeps their folder structure.

Changes the model `API.MoveNavigatorItem`

[Unused View Cleaner](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/UnusedViewCleaner.py)
- Workflow

#### Export the model to OBJ

Writes the 3D model, or only the selected elements, to a Wavefront OBJ file, one object per element, for Blender and other tools.

Writes files `Get3DGeometryOfElements`

[export_obj.py](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Workflows/export_obj.py)

### What you can do *today.*

Twelve kinds of work offices automate with Tapir, from a palette script to a Grasshopper definition.

#### Property management

Read and update the properties of hundreds of elements in seconds.

#### Geometry generation

Create walls, slabs and beams from Python, with the settings you choose.

#### Quantity take-offs

Material and element quantities for reports, straight from the model.

#### AI assistants (MCP)

Let an AI assistant read and change your model through a Tapir MCP server.

#### BCF issue tracking

Create and track issues and exchange them as BCF files from Python.

#### Classification mapping

Classify elements by naming conventions or by rules on their geometry.

#### Views and layouts

Script views, sections and the Layout Book.

#### Model checking

Find missing values and elements that break the office's standards.

#### Office workflows

Python scripts made for your office's standards, run from the palette.

#### Grasshopper links

Connect Rhino and Grasshopper definitions to native Archicad elements.

#### Element filtering

Select elements by type, layer, classification or nested properties.

#### Bulk renaming

Rename views, layouts and Publisher Sets to match the project's standards.

### One file, *no packages.*

With a project open, Archicad answers JSON commands on `http://127.0.0.1:19723`. Tapir's commands go through Archicad's `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand`. Save this as `walls.py` and run it with any Python 3.

With several Archicads open, the next ones answer on 19724, 19725 and so on.

[Your first Python script, step by step](https://archicad-api.com/start/#python)

walls.pyport 19723

```
import json
import urllib.request

def run_tapir_command(command, parameters=None):
    body = json.dumps({
        'command': 'API.ExecuteAddOnCommand',
        'parameters': {
            'addOnCommandId': {'commandNamespace': 'TapirCommand', 'commandName': command},
            'addOnCommandParameters': parameters or {}
        }
    }).encode('utf-8')
    request = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:19723', body, {'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
        result = json.loads(response.read())
    if not result['succeeded']:
        raise RuntimeError(result['error'])
    return result['result']['addOnCommandResponse']

print(run_tapir_command('GetAddOnVersion'))
walls = run_tapir_command('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
print(len(walls), 'walls')
```

## Get *started.*

From download to your first script in about ten minutes. Steps 1 to 3 need no programming.

**Video** Prefer watching? The [Tapir video tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) walk through installing Tapir and using it.

**Tutorials** Written tutorials, step by step: [properties to Excel](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/export-properties-to-excel/), [Grasshopper](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/connect-grasshopper-to-archicad/), [renaming views](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/batch-rename-views/), [numbering doors and windows](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/number-doors-and-windows-by-zone/) and [your first Python script](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/first-python-script/).

### Install Tapir

**With the installer (recommended).** It finds every Archicad version on the computer and installs the matching add-on into each, so Archicad loads it on its next start.

[Download WINDOWS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Win.exe) [Download MACOS](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest/download/TapirInstaller_Mac.zip)

  - **Windows:** the installer asks for administrator rights, because it copies the add-on into the Archicad folder under Program Files.
  - **macOS:** unzip the download and open the app.

**Prefer to install by hand?** Download the `TapirAddOn_AC<version>_Win.apx` or `TapirAddOn_AC<version>_Mac.zip` file for your Archicad version from the [latest release](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases/latest), then in Archicad: *Options > Add-On Manager > Edit List of Available Add-Ons > Add*, browse to the file and click *OK*.

Tapir keeps itself up to date: it tells you when a new version is out and installs it for you.

### Run your first script

Tapir adds a *Tapir* menu to Archicad. Choose *Tapir Palette* from it, pick a script in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. The built-in scripts are there from the start: try *ProjectHealthCheck*, which lists elements without an ID, zones with the same number, unclassified elements and more. It only reads the model.

Tapir runs the scripts with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which brings the Python and the packages each script needs. If uv is not installed yet, Tapir offers to install it the first time you run a script.

*Manage Shortcuts* on the palette puts up to six scripts in the Tapir menu, as *Run Script Shortcut 1* to *6*.

### Add more scripts

The [Scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/) page collects scripts shared by the community, each one reviewed before it is listed. The Tapir palette is getting a window to find and install them in one click.

**Until then** If your palette has no such window yet, add a script by hand, as below.

Download the scripts you want into a folder, then tell Tapir about that folder in its configuration file, `Documents/Tapir/config.json` in your user folder (Tapir writes it the first time it runs). Add the folder to its `localFolders` list, keeping the rest of the file as it is:

Documents/Tapir/config.jsonJSON

```
{
    "repositories": [ ... ],
    "localFolders": [
        {
            "displayName": "My scripts",
            "path": "C:\\Users\\me\\Documents\\Tapir scripts"
        }
    ],
    ...
}
```

  - `path` is the folder (on macOS for example `/Users/me/Documents/Tapir scripts`). In JSON, a Windows path's backslashes are doubled.
  - `displayName` is the name the palette shows for the folder's scripts; without it, the folder's name is used.
  - Optionally, `includePattern` and `excludePattern` are regular expressions that choose which files of the folder the palette lists.

The palette lists the folder's scripts next to the built-in ones the next time it loads its scripts.

### Write a script of your own

Archicad answers JSON commands on `http://127.0.0.1:19723` while a project is open (with several Archicads open, the next ones use 19724, 19725 and so on). Tapir's commands are called through Archicad's `API.ExecuteAddOnCommand` command, in the `TapirCommand` namespace. Python's standard library is enough; there are no packages to install.

version.pyport 19723

```
import json
import urllib.request

def run_tapir_command(command, parameters=None):
    request = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:19723')
    request.add_header('Content-Type', 'application/json')
    body = json.dumps({
        'command': 'API.ExecuteAddOnCommand',
        'parameters': {
            'addOnCommandId': {'commandNamespace': 'TapirCommand', 'commandName': command},
            'addOnCommandParameters': parameters or {}
        }
    }).encode('utf-8')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, body) as response:
        result = json.loads(response.read())
    if not result['succeeded']:
        raise RuntimeError(result['error'])
    return result['result']['addOnCommandResponse']

print(run_tapir_command('GetAddOnVersion'))
## prints the version of the add-on Archicad has loaded, e.g. {'version': '1.8.0'}
```

Graphisoft's [`archicad` package](https://pypi.org/project/archicad/) sends the same commands and finds the port by itself, if you prefer it. Put your script in a [local folder](https://archicad-api.com/start/#marketplace) to run it from the Tapir palette.

[All commands, with schemas and examples](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/)

### Use it from Grasshopper

In Rhino, open the Package Manager (the `PackageManager` command, or *Tools > Package Manager*), search for tapir, install it and restart Rhino. Its components are on the *Tapir* tab in Grasshopper and work with the Archicad that runs Tapir. The Walls, Doors, Windows and Railings components read and change Archicad elements with the names you know from Archicad's settings dialogs.

[The Grasshopper guide](https://archicad-api.com/grasshopper/)

### How it *works.*

Tapir is an Archicad add-on that turns native API functions into a stateless JSON server on port 19723. Anything that can send an HTTP request can drive Archicad.

**Grasshopper**The tapir components

**Python scripts**The palette, or your own

**AI and MCP**Assistants and MCP servers

**Tapir Add-On**A stateless JSON layer: one command per request

**Archicad**The BIM model and its C++ API

### Anatomy of a call

requestPOST 127.0.0.1:19723

```
{"command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
 "parameters": {
   "addOnCommandId": {
     "commandNamespace": "TapirCommand",
     "commandName": "GetElementsByType"},
   "addOnCommandParameters": {
     "elementType": "Wall"}}}
```

response200

```
{"succeeded": true,
 "result": {
   "addOnCommandResponse": {
     "elements": [
       {"elementId": {"guid": "3F2A…"}},
       …
     ]}}}
```

Every Tapir command is sent the same way; only `commandName` and `addOnCommandParameters` change. [Your first Python script](https://archicad-api.com/start/#python)

## Share a script *from Archicad.*

No GitHub account, no setup. Your name stays on it, and everyone who uses Tapir can install it.

### What happens

1. **Send it**Post the script in `#share-a-script` on Discord, with a few words on what it does. The Tapir palette is getting a Share button that does the same: you see the whole file before anything is sent. It arrives as a GitHub issue labelled `script-share`.
2. **Adapted for any office**Tapir's bot, an AI, opens a pull request: hard-coded layers, properties and paths become settings, risky code is removed, and it works in every Archicad language, in metric and imperial.
3. **You confirm, it's listed**Try the adapted version and say it still does what you meant. Once the pull request is reviewed and merged, it appears on the [Scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/) page with your name.

### Three ways to send it

Coming to the palette

#### From the Tapir palette

Right-click your script and choose Share: add a few words about it and send. Until your palette has it, use Discord.

Easiest today

#### On Discord

Post the script in the `#share-a-script` channel, with a few words on what it does and which Archicad version you use.

[Join Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY)

If you use GitHub

#### As a pull request

Add a folder `marketplace/<name>/` with the script, a `listing.json` and a README, as the marketplace README describes.

[The marketplace folder](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/tree/main/marketplace)

What is sent

#### Only the script

The file, your one-line description, the name to credit, and your Archicad and Tapir versions. Nothing from the open project.

Licence

#### Free for everyone

Every shared script is free and open source. Unless you choose another open-source licence, yours is published under the [MIT licence](https://opensource.org/license/mit): anyone may use, change and share it, as long as they keep your name and the licence with it. It comes without warranty. You stay its author, and its page credits you.

Only share a script you wrote, or one whose author agreed to share it.

### What the AI *changes.*

It keeps what your script does. It changes how, so the script is safe and works in other offices, and lists every change in plain words in the pull request.

Made safe

#### Removed, or flagged for a maintainer

- connections to anything other than Archicad on your own computer;
- running other programs or code built from text (`subprocess`, `os.system`, `eval`, `exec`);
- installing packages while it runs (`pip install`);
- deleting or overwriting files, and writing anywhere but the project's folder and `Documents/Tapir`;
- passwords, tokens and keys;
- user names, `C:\Users\…` paths, and project, client and office names, in the code and its comments.

Made to fit other offices

#### Settings instead of your names

- Property names, layers, stories, paths and classification codes you typed in become settings at the top of the script, or fields of its window.
- Built-in properties are found by their ID, so the script works in every language of Archicad.
- Lengths and areas work in metric and imperial units; paths work on Windows and macOS.

Made safe to run

#### No surprises

- It says what it is about to change, and does nothing, saying so, when nothing fits.
- It makes its changes in one Undo step where it can.
- When a property or element type it needs is missing, it shows a clear message instead of crashing.

Described

#### A README in plain words

- What it does, how to use it, its settings, what it changes, its limits, and *Original by* you.
- Its category, the Archicad and Tapir versions it works with, and whether it changes the model, writes files or only reads.

Before it is merged

#### What the review checks

Every pull request is reviewed before it is merged, like any other code in Tapir. The review checks that:

- nothing on the *Made safe* list is left in, unless a maintainer agreed to it;
- the script still does what you wrote it for, and you confirmed that;
- the folder has the files and fields the [marketplace format](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/marketplace/README.md) asks for;
- the README is accurate, and the screenshots show no client, project or people.

Next step

#### Post your script

Share it in `#share-a-script` on Discord, and we take it from there.

[Join Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY) [Browse scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/)

Source: https://archicad-api.com/grasshopper/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Docs](https://archicad-api.com/docs/) / Grasshopper

## Grasshopper, *visually.*

The Tapir plugin connects Grasshopper to a running Archicad: read elements and their settings, change them, and create new ones from Rhino geometry, without writing code.

### What the components *do.*

Each component sends a Tapir command to Archicad and gives you the answer as Grasshopper data. You find them on the **Tapir** tab, grouped as in Archicad.

**READ** **Elements and their data**Elements by type, story or selection; their properties, classifications, settings and geometry.

**CHANGE** **What you pass in**Property values, classifications, layers, IDs and tool settings of the elements you pass in.

**CREATE** **From Rhino geometry**Walls, doors, windows, railings, level dimensions and more, from points and curves.

**PROJECT** **The rest of the file**Stories, attributes, navigator views, layouts, issues, favorites and libraries.

Which Tapir commands have a component, and which settings each covers, is on the [Grasshopper coverage](https://archicad-api.com/gh-coverage/) page.

### One per Archicad *tool.*

A tool component works like the Archicad tool of the same name. One JSON input and one JSON output per panel of its settings dialog, keyed by the labels you see there, such as `Wall Height`.

Design Tools

#### Walls

Placed by `StartPoint` and `EndPoint`.

Refresh Execute Create

Design Tools

#### Doors

Placed in an `OwnerWall` at a `CenterOffset`.

Refresh Execute Create

Design Tools

#### Windows

Placed in an `OwnerWall` at a `CenterOffset`.

Refresh Execute Create

Design Tools

#### Railings

Placed along a `ReferenceLine`.

Refresh Create

Document Tools

#### LevelDimensions

Placed at a `Position`, optionally on a parent element.

Refresh Create

**REFRESH** **Reads**Reads the elements in `ElementGuid` and fills every output.

**EXECUTE** **Writes**Writes the given settings to those elements. Only the keys you give are written.

**CREATE** **Makes new elements**From the geometry inputs, starting from the tool's defaults or from a `FavoriteName`.

Nothing is written to Archicad until you press Execute or Create. A JSON output read by Refresh can be fed straight back into the same input. Archicad has no command to change railings or level dimensions after they are placed, so for those Execute only writes the ID, layer and draw order.

**Note** Walls remembers the walls its Create made, in the `.gh` file. The next Create updates them instead of making new ones. Turn this off, or forget them, in the component's menu.

### Install

#### Install the Tapir Add-On in Archicad

The components talk to Archicad through the Add-On. [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows how.

#### Install the tapir package in Rhino

In Rhino 7 or 8, open *Tools > Package Manager* (or type `PackageManager`), search for **tapir** and click Install. Restart Rhino.

#### Open Archicad, then Grasshopper

With a project open in Archicad, start Grasshopper. The **Tapir** tab appears in its toolbar. With more than one Archicad open, give the port of the one you want to the **ConnectArchicad** component (*Tapir > General*); the first Archicad uses 19723.

### One *wall.*

Build this in an empty Grasshopper canvas, with a project open in Archicad:

1. Place two **Point** parameters and set them to 0,0,0 and 5,0,0. Archicad reads the numbers as metres.
2. Place the **Walls** component from *Tapir > Design Tools*. Connect the points to `StartPoint` and `EndPoint`.
3. Place a **Panel** with the text on the right and connect it to `GeometryAndPositioning_JSON`.
4. Press **Create**. A 5 m wall appears in Archicad, 3 m high and 30 cm thick.
5. Move a point and press Create again: the same wall moves. Change the panel and press Create: the same wall changes.

Press **Refresh** to see every setting of the wall in the JSON outputs. Copy a key from there to set it the next time.

Panel → GeometryAndPositioning_JSONJSON

```
{"Wall Height": 3.0, "Wall Thickness": 0.3}
```

#### [Install the Add-On](https://archicad-api.com/start/)

Install Tapir and the tapir package, then try the wall above.

Get started

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Docs](https://archicad-api.com/docs/) / AI

## Tapir and *AI.*

An AI assistant can read your Archicad project and change it through Tapir. You ask in plain words; it sends the commands to the Archicad running on your computer.

### Two ways to *connect.*

Both talk to the same Tapir commands on port 19723, on your own computer.

While you chat

#### An MCP server

The AI tool calls Tapir's commands itself, while you chat. Works with tools that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP), such as Claude Desktop.

[Tapir MCP servers](https://archicad-api.com/ai/#mcp-servers)

Any AI tool

#### A script the AI writes

Any AI tool can write a short Python script that sends Tapir commands. You read it, then run it from the Tapir palette or a terminal.

[How it works](https://archicad-api.com/ai/#scripts)

### Tapir MCP *servers.*

These are community projects, not part of Tapir. Each has its own install steps in its README. Which one Tapir recommends is still being decided in [issue #2070](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/2070), so they are listed here without a recommendation.

By SzamosiMate

#### tapir-archicad-MCP

The MCP server for Tapir that the others started from. It is also published on PyPI as the tapir-archicad-mcp package.

[Its repository](https://github.com/SzamosiMate/tapir-archicad-MCP) [The package on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/tapir-archicad-mcp/)

By the community

#### Its forks

Versions of it that others changed and published. Check when each was last updated.

[See the forks](https://github.com/SzamosiMate/tapir-archicad-MCP/forks)

**Careful** An MCP server can change your model. Try it on a copy of your project first, and read what the AI is about to do before you allow it.

### Start by *reading.*

Open a project in Archicad, with the Tapir Add-On loaded, and give your AI tool this prompt. It only reads, so it is safe to try on any project.

When the answer looks right, ask for a change in the same plain words, and say exactly which elements it may change: "Set the property X to Y on the selected walls only."

promptread only

```
Use Tapir to look at the Archicad project I have open.
Do not change anything; only read.
1. List the stories with their names and levels.
2. Count the walls, slabs, columns, doors and windows on each story.
3. Show the result as one table, one row per story.
Tell me which Tapir commands you used.
```

### Check names, *don't guess.*

Your words rarely match the names in the project: "fire rating" may be a property called FireRating in one template and Feuerwiderstand in another, and "level 2" may be the story "02 First Floor". An AI that guesses the name still gets an answer, only a wrong one: no values found, so "no doors have a fire rating".

**01** **Look the words up first**Before a command whose parameters come from your words (a story, property, classification, layer, building material, composite, surface, zone category or element type), the AI sends those words to [ResolveNames](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ResolveNames), with the kind of each when it knows it. It only reads.

**02** **Use what it returns**found: the item named exactly so, with the ids the other commands take (story index, attribute id, elementType, propertyId, classification ids). closeMatches: only similar names, best first; the AI asks you which one you meant instead of picking one itself.

**03** **Say "not in this project"**notFound: nothing in the project is close, so the project has no such item. The AI says "this project has no X" instead of guessing a name or reporting an empty result as the answer.

Add these lines to your prompt, or to the instructions of your MCP server, so the AI checks the names every time. They work the same when the AI writes a script: the script sends ResolveNames first and stops with a message on notFound.

Before a change, ask for a preview. The commands that delete or replace, such as [DeleteElements](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteElements), [DeleteAttributes](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteAttributes) and [DeleteAndReplaceAttributes](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#DeleteAndReplaceAttributes), take "dryRun": true: nothing changes, and the response lists what would. The command reference says which commands have it.

promptadd to any request

```
Before you use a name taken from my words (a story,
property, classification, layer, building material,
composite, surface, zone category or element type),
check it with the Tapir command ResolveNames.
- found: use the ids it returns.
- closeMatches: ask me which one I mean.
- notFound: tell me this project has no such item.
  Never guess a name.
Before a command that deletes or replaces, run it with
"dryRun": true if it has that input, and show me what
it would change.
```

### Describe it, *run it.*

Without an MCP server, describe the task, give the AI the command list, and run the script it writes.

**01** **Describe what you want**For example: "Extract all composite exterior walls on level 2 and calculate their net volume."

**02** **Share the command list**Give the AI the [command reference](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/) and the working example below. Ask for Python's standard library only, on port 19723.

**03** **Read it, then run it**Read the script before you run it, from the Tapir palette or a terminal. Try one that changes the model on a copy of your project first.

promptfor Claude or any AI tool

```
Write a Python script that uses only the standard
library and sends Tapir commands to Archicad on
http://127.0.0.1:19723, like the example I attach.
Use the Tapir command reference I attach.

Extract all composite exterior walls on level 2
and calculate their net volume.

Only read the model; change nothing.
```

tapir_example.pyport 19723

```
import json
import urllib.request

def run_tapir_command(name, parameters=None, port=19723):
    request = {
        "command": "API.ExecuteAddOnCommand",
        "parameters": {
            "addOnCommandId": {"commandNamespace": "TapirCommand", "commandName": name},
            "addOnCommandParameters": parameters or {},
        },
    }
    with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}", json.dumps(request).encode("utf-8")) as response:
        answer = json.loads(response.read())
    if not answer.get("succeeded"):
        raise RuntimeError(answer.get("error"))
    return answer["result"]["addOnCommandResponse"]

print(run_tapir_command("GetAddOnVersion"))
```

## Ask. Report. *Test.*

Architects, developers and the maintainers in one place. Bugs and ideas become fixes that someone with your Archicad version tests before they ship.

### Where to find us

Discord

#### Ask anything

Architects, developers and the maintainers, in one server. Show what you made and talk with the people who build Tapir.

[Join Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY)

YouTube

#### Learn the API

A video series from the first command to full workflows.

[Watch the tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/)

AI assistants

#### Talk to your model

MCP servers let Claude and other assistants read and change a project through Tapir.

[Tapir and AI](https://archicad-api.com/ai/)

### How the bots *work.*

Most fixes are written by bots and checked by people. The maintainers set the rules and can stop any change; you decide whether a fix works in your Archicad.

**01** **Post it**Describe the bug or idea on Discord or GitHub. A GitHub account is not needed on Discord.

**02** **An issue**Every half hour, Discord posts that read like a bug report or a feature request become GitHub issues, and the bot replies with the link.

**03** **A draft fix**The issue bot answers, asks for what it is missing, or writes the fix and opens a pull request. It is built for every Archicad version and reviewed.

**04** **You test**A comment on the pull request links the built add-on and asks the person who reported it to try it.

**05** **Released**Green and reviewed, it is merged three days later unless a maintainer stops it, and ships in Monday's [release](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases).

Report

#### How to report a bug

Post it on Discord or open an issue on GitHub; both reach the same place. A report that can be fixed in one go says:

- your Archicad version and build, and its language (for example 29.0.0 (3100) INT);
- your Tapir version (the *About Tapir* dialog shows it);
- what you did: the script or Grasshopper definition, or the command and the JSON you sent;
- what you expected and what happened instead, with the error message;
- whether the project is a Teamwork project, and which libraries are loaded, when it matters.

**Public** Issues and Discord channels are public. Leave out client names, project names and file paths you don't want to share.

[Open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/new) [Post on Discord](https://discord.gg/NAnSennmpY)

Test

#### How to test a fix

A fix is only known to work once someone has run it in Archicad. The bots can build Tapir but cannot run Archicad, so your test is what matters most.

1. Open the pull request linked from your issue. A comment on it lists the downloads, one per Archicad version and platform. Downloading needs a GitHub login.
2. Unzip the download for your Archicad version. On macOS it holds another zip with the `.bundle`.
3. In Archicad, open *Options > Add-On Manager > Edit List of Available Add-Ons*, remove or disable the installed Tapir, then *Add* the `.apx` (Windows) or `.bundle` (macOS) and click OK.
4. Do what went wrong before, in a copy of your project.
5. Say on the pull request whether it works and fixes your case. Afterwards, put your installed Tapir back the same way.

Testing often? The [community test runner](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/tools/community-test-runner/GUIDE.md) tests open pull requests on your own Archicad while it is closed, leaves your Tapir in place and posts the result. It runs on Windows and needs Python and a GitHub account.

## What's *next.*

Tapir grows from requests. Most new commands, components and fixes start as a message from someone who needed them in their own work.

### How to ask for a *feature.*

Four steps from "I need this" to a Monday release.

#### Say what you want to do

Post it on Discord or open an issue on GitHub. Describe the task in Archicad, not only the command: "number the doors along a line", "read the area of every zone". A Discord message that reads like a feature request becomes a GitHub issue by itself, labelled `enhancement`.

#### Asking for a part of the Archicad API?

The [API coverage](https://archicad-api.com/api-coverage/) page lists every function of the Archicad API and whether Tapir has a command for it. Use the *Archicad API request* issue form to ask for one that is missing.

#### The issue bot picks it up

A clear, wanted request is built like a fix: the bot writes it and opens a pull request, and you are asked to try it. A large one is split into parts. When the design is open, the bot describes the choices and a maintainer decides.

#### It ships on a Monday

Merged changes are released every Monday. The release notes list them, and the add-on offers to update itself.

### What is being asked for now

Requests

#### [Open feature requests](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aenhancement)

Every open issue labelled `enhancement`. Add a comment or a reaction to one you need too.

See the requests

Plan

#### [Project board](https://github.com/orgs/ENZYME-APD/projects/4/views/1)

The maintainers' board of planned and ongoing work.

Open the board

In progress

#### [Open pull requests](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/pulls)

Changes being built, reviewed and tested right now.

See the pull requests

Shipped

#### [Releases](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/releases)

Every release, with its notes and downloads. The command reference shows the version each command came in.

See the releases

### Already *here.*

Asked for on the old site's "What's cooking" list, and now part of Tapir.

#### Stairs, roofs and curtain walls

Read and change them: [`ModifyStairs`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyStairs), [`ModifyRoofs`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyRoofs) and [`ModifyCurtainWalls`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyCurtainWalls).

#### Building materials and composites

Create them from a script: [`CreateBuildingMaterials`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateBuildingMaterials) and [`CreateComposites`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateComposites).

#### Dialogs from Python

A script shows its own window in Archicad: [`ShowScriptUI`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ShowScriptUI) and [`GetScriptUIResult`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetScriptUIResult).

#### 2D detailing

Lines, fills and text: [`CreateLineElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateLineElements), [`CreateHatches`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHatches) and [`CreateTexts`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateTexts).

#### Your own properties

Add property definitions from a script: [`CreatePropertyDefinitions`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreatePropertyDefinitions).

#### Built-in scripts

Ready to run from the palette, from numbering to a project health check. [See them on GitHub](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/tree/main/builtin-scripts).

### Still *open.*

Two ideas from the old list that nobody has asked for in an issue yet. Want one? Open the issue.

Missing something in your work?

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / About

## About *Tapir.*

An open-source project that makes Archicad scriptable for architects, not only for programmers. Started in 2022, released every week since.

### Why it *exists.*

Archicad's own JSON API covers only part of what its add-on API can do. Tapir adds the missing commands as an add-on, then puts them within reach of people who don't code: a palette of ready scripts, Grasshopper components, and AI assistants.

### How it *started.*

Started as R&D at Enzyme, an architecture practice, then opened to everyone, in the spirit of ifc.js: practitioners shouldn't wait for a vendor to support their workflow.

Revisions · Tapir

| Rev | Date | Description | By |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 5 July 2022 | Born in Enzyme's R&D Archicad's JSON interface was a step forward, but Grasshopper users still needed C++ add-ons to reach native elements. The first commit, with the MIT licence. | Grzeg Wilk, Jorge Beneitez |
| B | 7 July 2022 | A place to talk The Discord server opens, where architects and developers say what they need and show what they made. | The first members |
| C | July 2024 | The template Tibor Lorántfy, whose archicad-additional-json-commands the add-on is built on, joins the project. Almost any function of the Archicad API can now become a JSON command. | Tibor Lorántfy |
| D | 2026 | Built by its community A release every Monday. Reports on Discord become GitHub issues, bots draft the fixes and people test them in their own Archicad. [See the growth](https://archicad-api.com/community/#activity). | Everyone who reports, tests and contributes |

### The people *behind it.*

ENZYME-APD runs the project and publishes Tapir under the MIT licence. Everyone below has written code for it, or tested it and given the feedback it is built on, in alphabetical order.

### Principles

**FREE** **No price, ever**MIT licence for the add-on, the plugin and every shared script.

**OPEN** **Built in public**Every issue, pull request and review is on GitHub.

Source: https://archicad-api.com/limits/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Docs](https://archicad-api.com/docs/) / API limits

## What the Archicad API *can't do.*

Tapir uses the Archicad API that Graphisoft publishes for add-ons, and covers all of it that can be a JSON command. What that API does not offer, Tapir cannot offer either. This page lists what people ask for that is not in it, with what to do instead.

### The *list.*

It is also what Tapir would like the Archicad API to offer, and the list Tapir sends to Graphisoft. Every row was checked in the headers of the Archicad API DevKits of Archicad 25 to 30, the versions Tapir is built for; the Evidence column names the headers and functions.

| What people want | Status | What to do instead | Evidence | Issue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Elements | | | | |
| Explode an element into its parts, as Edit > Reshape > Explode into Current View does | Not possible | Nothing yet | No explode function in `ACAPinc.h`, the `ACAPI_*.h` headers or the `ACAPI::` modules (AC25–AC30). `APIAttrCreationMethod_Explode` (`APIdefs_Attributes.h`) only tells how an attribute was created. | – |
| A camera with a name of its own, or an axonometric camera | Partly possible | Name the Camera Set the camera is in. For an axonometric view, set the 3D window with [Set3DProjectionSettings](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Set3DProjectionSettings). | `API_CameraType` holds only `head`, `camSetGuid` and `perspCam` (`API_PerspCamPars`); only `API_CamSetType` has a `name` (`APIdefs_Elements.h`, AC25–AC30). | [#2192](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/2192) |
| Remove one direction of a trim between two roofs or shells that trim each other | Workaround | Remove the trim with [RemoveElementTrims](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RemoveElementTrims), which removes both directions, then trim the other direction again with [TrimElements](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#TrimElements). | The only removal function, `ACAPI_Element_Trim_Remove (guid_Element1, guid_Element2)` (`ACAPinc.h`, AC25–AC30), “removes trimming connection between the elements” and takes no direction or trim type. | [#2365](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/2365) |
| Read which slab or stair edge a railing is linked to, or link a railing to one | Not possible | Read the slab's outline with [GetDetailsOfElements](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDetailsOfElements) and create a static railing along the edge with [CreateRailings](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateRailings). When the slab changes, delete the railing and create it again. | `API_RailingType`, `API_RailingSegmentType` and `API_RailingNodeType` hold no host element or edge; the node has only `isStatic` (`APIdefs_Elements.h`, AC25–AC30). `ACAPI_Grouping_GetConnectedElements` and `ACAPI_Element_GetRelations` (`ACAPinc.h`) list no railing connection, and the `ACAPI::` modules have no railing API. | [#2445](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/2445) |
| Navigator and views | | | | |
| Add an item to a publisher set | Not possible | Add the items in Archicad's Organizer, then publish the set with [PublishPublisherSet](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#PublishPublisherSet). | The `ACAPI_Navigator_*` functions (`ACAPI_Navigator.h`; `APINavigator_*ID` in AC25–AC26) create views and folders on the View Map (`ACAPI_Navigator_NewNavigatorView`, `ACAPI_Navigator_CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap`) and layouts (`ACAPI_Navigator_CreateLayout`); `ACAPI_Navigator_SetNavigatorItemPosition` moves items on the Layout Book and the View Maps only. None adds to a publisher set. | – |
| Change, rename or create a stored Model View Options combination | Partly possible | Read the combinations with [GetModelViewOptionDetails](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetModelViewOptionDetails); change the options of the current window with [SetViewOptions](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetViewOptions). | `ACAPinc.h` has only `ACAPI_Navigator_ModelViewOptions_Get`, `_GetNum` and `_Search` (AC27–AC30). In AC25–AC26 the combinations are attributes (`API_ModelViewOptionsID`); not checked there. | [#781](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/781) |
| Project and files | | | | |
| Undo or redo, as Edit > Undo does | Not possible | Most Tapir commands change the model in an undo step, so the user can undo them in Archicad; the command reference says which cannot be undone. Save the project with [SaveProject](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SaveProject) before a script that may need to be taken back. | `ACAPI_CallUndoableCommand` (`ACAPinc.h`) only opens an undo step; `APINotifyElement_Undo` and `APINotifyElement_Redo` (`APIdefs_Callback.h`) only notify. No function runs an undo or a redo (AC25–AC30). | [#1820](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/1820) |
| Copy and paste through the clipboard | Workaround | In a project, copy 2D elements to another view with [CopyElementsToDatabase](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CopyElementsToDatabase). Between projects, save the elements as a module with [SaveAsModuleFile](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SaveAsModuleFile), place it in the other project with [CreateHotlinkNodes](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHotlinkNodes) and [CreateHotlinkInstances](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHotlinkInstances), and, to keep plain elements, [BreakHotlinkNodes](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#BreakHotlinkNodes). | No clipboard, copy or paste function in `ACAPinc.h`, the `ACAPI_*.h` headers or the `ACAPI::` modules (AC25–AC30). | – |
| Merge a file into the project, as File > Interoperability > Merge does | Workaround | Place the file as a hotlink with [CreateHotlinkNodes](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHotlinkNodes) and [CreateHotlinkInstances](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateHotlinkInstances), then [BreakHotlinkNodes](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#BreakHotlinkNodes). | The project functions (`ACAPI_ProjectOperation_*`; `APIDo_*ID` in AC25–AC26) open, create, save, close, print and publish, but none merges. `ACAPI_Element_Merge_Elements` is the Merge of construction elements, not of files. | – |
| Documents and publishing | | | | |
| Read the rows of an Interactive Schedule | Not possible | Build the list yourself: find the elements with [GetElementsByType](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByType) and read their values with [GetPropertyValuesOfElements](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetPropertyValuesOfElements) or [GetQuantitiesOfElements](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetQuantitiesOfElements). The [built-in scripts](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/) Room Finishes Schedule and Material Take-Off build such lists. | A schedule appears only as a Project Map item (`API_ScheduleNavItem`, `APIdefs_Navigator.h`), a view node (`API_ViewNodeSchedule`) and a window type (`APIWind_IESCommonDrawingID`, `APIdefs_Database.h`). No function returns its rows (AC25–AC30). | – |
| Export an Interactive Schedule | Workaround | Put the schedule in a publisher set in Archicad once, then publish that set with [PublishPublisherSet](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#PublishPublisherSet). | No schedule export function (AC25–AC30); `ACAPI_ProjectOperation_Publish` (`APIDo_PublishID` in AC25–AC26) publishes a whole publisher set. | – |
| Archicad's interface | | | | |
| Read the text of the Session Report window | Not possible | Open the window for the user with [ChangeWindow](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ChangeWindow) and windowType 'Report' (from Archicad 26). | `ACAPI_WriteReport` (`ACAPinc.h`) writes to it and `ACAPI_Dialog_ActivateSessionReport` (`ACAPI_Goodies.h`, AC27–AC30; `APIAny_ActivateSessionReportID` in AC26) opens it; no function reads it (AC25–AC30). | [#1707](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/1707) |
| Get the outcome of an Action Center check | Partly possible | Run the check with [RunActionCenterChecks](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RunActionCenterChecks); Archicad shows the Action Center when it found an issue. For the hotlink check, read the state of each source with [GetHotlinkSourceStatus](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetHotlinkSourceStatus) (from Archicad 27). | `ACAPI_Window_Check` (`ACAPinc.h`, AC27–AC30; `ACAPI_ActionCenter_Check` in AC25–AC26) returns only an error code; `API_ActionCenterItemID` (`APIdefs_ActionCenter.hpp`) has only `APIActionCenterItem_Hotlinks`. | – |

Found something else the Archicad API cannot do? Say so in an issue, with the DevKit headers you checked, and it is added here. [Open an issue](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/issues/new/choose)

Source: https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/batch-rename-views/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) / Batch rename views

## Batch rename views in *Archicad.*

Bulk View Renamer, a script that comes with Tapir, renames the views of the View Map, or of one of its folders, in one go. You see every new name before anything is renamed.

### Open the script

Install the Tapir Add-On with the Tapir Installer, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows, and start Archicad with a project open. Choose *Tapir Palette* from the *Tapir* menu.

Bulk View Renamer is a built-in script: pick *BulkViewRenamer* in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. It lists the views of the View Map with their folder, ID and name. It is also on the Scripts page as [Bulk View Renamer](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/?s=bulk-view-renamer).

### Choose the views

In *Views in*, choose the whole View Map or one folder; its subfolders are included.

### Choose how the names change

  - *Find and replace*: *Find* and *Replace with*, optionally with *Match case* and *Regular expression*.
  - *Prefix and suffix*: *Add before* and *Add after*.
  - *Pattern with counter*: a *Pattern* in which `{name}` is the current name, `{id}` the view's ID and `{n}` the counter, with its *Start*, *Step* and *Digits*. The counter counts in View Map order. With the first settings, pattern `{name} {n}`, start 1 and 2 digits, a first view named *Ground Floor* becomes *Ground Floor 01*.

### Check the new names

The table shows the new names. A *clash* is a view that would get the same name as another view in its folder; an empty new name is skipped. Select rows to rename only those; *Clear selection* renames every listed view again.

### Rename

Press *Rename...*: the script lists the changes and asks first, then renames the views one at a time and reads the View Map again. Views that could not be renamed are named in the palette's output. Only the names change, not the view IDs or the views' settings.

### The commands *behind it.*

The script reads the View Map with Archicad's own `API.GetNavigatorItemTree` command and renames each view with the Tapir command [`RenameNavigatorItem`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#RenameNavigatorItem). Its code is [`builtin-scripts/BulkViewRenamer.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BulkViewRenamer.py). It works in Archicad 25 to 30 with Tapir 1.8.0 or later.

Elements

#### [Number doors and windows by room in Archicad](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/number-doors-and-windows-by-zone/)

Element IDs such as 1.04-D1, from the zone each door or window opens into.

Read it

Source: https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/connect-grasshopper-to-archicad/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) / Connect Grasshopper

## Connect Grasshopper to *Archicad.*

Grasshopper talks to Archicad through two parts of Tapir: the Tapir Add-On in Archicad and the tapir package in Rhino. Install both, then read a wall and change one of its settings, without writing code.

### Install the Tapir Add-On in Archicad

The Grasshopper components send their commands to the Add-On. Install it with the Tapir Installer, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows.

### Install the tapir package in Rhino

In Rhino 7 or 8, open *Tools > Package Manager* (or type `PackageManager`), search for tapir and click *Install*. Restart Rhino.

### Open Archicad, then Grasshopper

With a project open in Archicad, start Grasshopper. The *Tapir* tab appears in its toolbar. With more than one Archicad open, give the port of the one you want to the **ConnectArchicad** component (*Tapir > General*); the first Archicad uses 19723.

### Read a wall

  - In Archicad, select one wall.
  - In Grasshopper, place the **SelectedElements** component from *Tapir > Elements*. Its `ElementGuids` output holds the selected elements. After you change the selection in Archicad, recompute the canvas to read it again.
  - Place the **Walls** component from *Tapir > Design Tools* and connect `ElementGuids` to its `ElementGuid` input.
  - Press **Refresh** on Walls and connect a **Panel** to its `GeometryAndPositioning_JSON` output. It shows the settings of the wall's Geometry and Positioning panel, keyed by the labels of the Wall Settings dialog, such as `Wall Height`.

For every wall of the project instead of the selection, use **ElementsByType** (*Tapir > Elements*): it comes with a list of element types connected to its `ElementsType` input, set to `Wall`.

### Change one value

  - Place a second Panel with the text below and connect it to the `GeometryAndPositioning_JSON` input of Walls.
  - Press **Execute**. The wall in Archicad is now 3.5 m high; Archicad reads the numbers as metres.
  - Only the keys you give are written; the other settings stay as they are. One JSON for several walls is written to all of them. The `Errors` output has a message for each wall that could not be changed.

Panel → GeometryAndPositioning_JSONJSON

```
{"Wall Height": 3.5}
```

Nothing is written to Archicad until you press Execute, or Create, which makes new walls. [The Grasshopper guide](https://archicad-api.com/grasshopper/#sample) shows how to create a wall from two points.

### The commands *behind it.*

SelectedElements sends [`GetSelectedElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSelectedElements) and ElementsByType sends [`GetElementsByType`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByType). Refresh on Walls reads the walls with [`GetDetailsOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDetailsOfElements), Execute writes them with [`ModifyWalls`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#ModifyWalls) and Create makes them with [`CreateWalls`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#CreateWalls). Which other commands have a component is on the [Grasshopper coverage](https://archicad-api.com/gh-coverage/) page.

Navigator

Source: https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/export-properties-to-excel/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) / Export properties to Excel

## Export Archicad element properties to Excel with *Python.*

Tapir comes with a script for it: Property Value Exporter writes the values of the properties you choose into an Excel workbook or a CSV file, one row per element, without an Interactive Schedule. Property Value Importer reads the edited file back.

### Open the script

Install the Tapir Add-On with the Tapir Installer, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows, and start Archicad with a project open. Choose *Tapir Palette* from the *Tapir* menu.

Property Value Exporter is a built-in script, so it is in the palette from the start: pick *PropertyValueExporter* in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. It reads every property of the project and opens its window. It is also on the Scripts page as [Property Value Exporter](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/?s=property-value-exporter).

### Choose the elements and the properties

  - Under *Elements*, choose *Selection*, *Current story* or *Whole project*, and if you want *Only elements on visible layers*.
  - Tick the element types to export. *All types* and *No types* tick or untick every one.
  - Under *Properties*, find properties with *Search* and move them to the *Exported* list with *Add →* or a double-click. *Up* and *Down* set the order of the columns; *← Remove* takes one out again.
  - Tick *Precise numbers* to export numbers in SI units (m, m², m³, degrees) instead of the values as Archicad displays them. Leave it off for a file you want to read back in.

### Export

Press *Export...* and choose the file. Its default name is `Property values <date> <time>.xlsx`; give it a `.csv` name for a CSV file. Nothing in the project changes.

The file has the columns *GUID*, *Element ID*, *Type* and *Story*, then one column per property, headed `<group>: <name>`. Rows are sorted by type, story from the bottom up and Element ID. A property an element does not have gives an empty cell. The file cannot be written while it is open in Excel.

### Bring the edited values back

Edit the values in Excel, then run [Property Value Importer](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/?s=property-value-importer). It is not built in: download it from the Scripts page into a folder of your own, with copies of the `utilities/` and `aclib/` folders of [`builtin-scripts/`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/tree/main/builtin-scripts) next to it. Add that folder to `localFolders` in `Documents/Tapir/config.json`, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#marketplace) shows, then choose *Reload scripts...* at the bottom of the palette's script list.

  - Press *Open file...* and choose the `.xlsx` or `.csv` file. A row is matched to its element by its GUID, or by its Element ID when it has no GUID.
  - The list shows each value that would change as *Current* → *New*, and in red what cannot be written, with the reason. An empty cell leaves the value as it is.
  - Press *Write to Archicad* and confirm. The values are written in one Undo step, and the *Result* column says *Written* or why a value was refused, for example because the property is read-only for that element.

### The commands *behind it.*

Both scripts are Python that sends Tapir commands to Archicad. The exporter lists the properties with [`GetAllProperties`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetAllProperties), finds the elements with [`GetElementsByType`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByType) or [`GetSelectedElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSelectedElements), reads their ID, type and story with [`GetDetailsOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetDetailsOfElements) and their values with [`GetPropertyValuesOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetPropertyValuesOfElements). The importer writes the values with [`SetPropertyValuesOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetPropertyValuesOfElements).

Their code is [`builtin-scripts/PropertyValueExporter.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyValueExporter.py) and [`marketplace/property-value-importer/PropertyValueImporter.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/marketplace/property-value-importer/PropertyValueImporter.py). Both work in Archicad 25 to 30 with Tapir 1.8.0 or later.

Source: https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/first-python-script/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) / First Python script

## Your first Archicad *Python script.*

A Tapir script is a Python file that sends JSON commands to Archicad. This one asks Archicad how many elements are selected, and runs from the Tapir palette.

### Install Tapir

Install the Tapir Add-On with the Tapir Installer, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows, and start Archicad with a project open. The Tapir palette runs scripts with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), which brings the Python each script needs; if uv is not installed yet, Tapir offers to install it the first time you run a script.

### Make a folder with aclib

Make a folder for your scripts, for example `Documents/Tapir scripts`, and an `aclib` folder inside it. Download [`builtin-scripts/aclib/__init__.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/aclib/__init__.py) into that `aclib` folder. `aclib` is the small helper of the built-in scripts: it sends a Tapir command to Archicad and returns the answer.

Documents/Tapir scriptsfolder

```
FirstScript.py
aclib/
    __init__.py
```

### Write the script

Save this as `FirstScript.py` in the folder. The two headers are those of the built-in scripts, described in [`builtin-scripts/README.md`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/README.md): uv reads the first, and the palette shows `changes` as *Read only*. The last two lines are [`archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSelectedElements.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/archicad-addon/Examples/Element/GetSelectedElements.py), the example of [`GetSelectedElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetSelectedElements).

FirstScript.pyPython

```
## /// script
## requires-python = ">=3.11"
## dependencies = []
## ///

## /// tapir
## changes = "read-only"
## ///

"""
First Script

Prints how many elements are selected in Archicad.
"""
import aclib

selectedElements = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetSelectedElements', {})['elements']
print ('{} elements are selected.'.format (len (selectedElements)))
```

### Run it from the palette

Add the folder to `localFolders` in `Documents/Tapir/config.json`, with the `displayName` *My scripts*, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#marketplace) shows. Choose *Tapir Palette* from the *Tapir* menu, then *Reload scripts...* at the bottom of its script list.

Select a few elements in Archicad, pick *FirstScript (My scripts)* in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. The palette reports what the script prints, such as `3 elements are selected.` Edits to the file take effect the next time you run it.

The palette starts the script with `uv run --script FirstScript.py --port <port>`, and `aclib` reads `--port`, so the script talks to the Archicad whose palette started it. With Python installed, you can also run it yourself as `python FirstScript.py`; it then uses the first Archicad, on port 19723.

### Call another command

Every Tapir command is called the same way: its name and a dictionary of its parameters. These lines count the walls of the project with [`GetElementsByType`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetElementsByType):

FirstScript.pyPython

```
walls = aclib.RunTapirCommand ('GetElementsByType', {'elementType': 'Wall'})['elements']
print ('{} walls in the project.'.format (len (walls)))
```

[The command reference](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/) lists every command with its parameters, its response and an example like the one above. To send the commands without `aclib`, see [Write a script of your own](https://archicad-api.com/start/#python).

A script that does more: property values to Excel and back.

Read it

Source: https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/number-doors-and-windows-by-zone/

[Tapir](https://archicad-api.com/) / [Tutorials](https://archicad-api.com/tutorials/) / Number doors and windows

## Number doors and windows by room in *Archicad.*

Door and Window Numbering by Zone, a script that comes with Tapir, gives every door and window an Element ID built from the zone it opens into, such as `1.04-D1` or `1.04-W2`, numbered within each zone.

### Open the script

Install the Tapir Add-On with the Tapir Installer, as [Get started](https://archicad-api.com/start/#install) shows, and start Archicad with a project open. Choose *Tapir Palette* from the *Tapir* menu.

Door and Window Numbering by Zone is a built-in script: open the floor plan, pick *DoorWindowNumberingByZone* in the palette's list and click *Run Script*. It reads the doors and windows of the current story and shows the new IDs next to the current ones; nothing is changed yet. It is also on the Scripts page as [Door and Window Numbering by Zone](https://archicad-api.com/scripts/?s=door-window-numbering-by-zone).

### Choose the elements

In *Elements*, choose *Selection*, *Current story* or *Whole project*, then press *Read elements*.

### Set the patterns

The list of new IDs updates as you type.

  - *Doors* and *Windows* are the patterns of the IDs, `{zone}-D{n}` and `{zone}-W{n}` at first. `{zone}` is the zone number, `{name}` the zone name (also used for `{zone}` when the zone has no number) and `{n}` the running number within the zone.
  - *Start at* is the first number in each zone, 1 at first.
  - *Digits* is the least number of digits of `{n}`, padded with zeros: 2 gives `01`.

The script warns when new IDs repeat.

### Rename

Press *Rename* and confirm. The script changes the Element ID of each door and window whose new ID differs from the current one, and you can undo it in Archicad. The status column shows the elements that could not be changed and why. In a Teamwork project, an element you have not reserved may not be changed.

### How it finds the *zone.*

Each door or window belongs to the zone on its "to" side, or to the zone on its "from" side when there is none. Within a zone they are numbered clockwise around the zone stamp, starting from the north. Zones with the same number continue one count, from north to south. Doors and windows without a zone are listed separately, with the reason, and are not renamed. Skylights and curtain wall panels are not numbered.

The script reads the zones of the doors and windows with [`GetRelationsOfElements`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#GetRelationsOfElements) and their positions with [`Get3DBoundingBoxes`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#Get3DBoundingBoxes), and writes the IDs with [`SetElementInfoStrings`](https://archicad-api.com/archicad-addon/#SetElementInfoStrings). Its code is [`builtin-scripts/DoorWindowNumberingByZone.py`](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/DoorWindowNumberingByZone.py). It works in Archicad 26 to 30 with Tapir 1.8.0 or later; Archicad 25 cannot tell which zone a door or window opens into.
