## Scripts in the Tapir palette

- **Automatic Numbering Based on Polyline**: Select one polyline and the elements to number. The elements get their Element ID in the order they follow along the polyline, from its first point to its last one. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/AutomaticNumberingBasedOnPolyline.py))
- **Batch Publisher**: Publishes the chosen Publisher Sets in one go, now or on a schedule (every N minutes or hours, or daily at a given time on the chosen weekdays). Before publishing it can receive the Teamwork changes and update the drawings on the layouts. The schedule runs while this window is open. The settings are saved per project, the runs are logged in the window and in a CSV file next to the settings (Documents/Tapir). ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BatchPublisher.py))
- **Building Material Property Audit**: Lists the value of a custom property for every Building Material of the project, so the materials with an empty value stand out. Export the list to Excel or CSV, or give the chosen materials a value: the script shows which materials it will change and asks before changing them, then reports the materials it could not change. Based on the audit_building_material_properties.py workflow example. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BuildingMaterialPropertyAudit.py))
- **Bulk View Renamer**: Lists the views of the View Map, or of one of its folders, and renames them in one go: find and replace (optionally a regular expression), a prefix and a suffix, or a pattern with a counter. A table shows the old and the new name of every view with name clashes marked, and nothing is renamed until you confirm. The views are renamed one by one with RenameNavigatorItem, and every view that could not be renamed is reported. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/BulkViewRenamer.py))
- **Classification Overview**: Shows how many elements are classified with each item of a classification system, as a tree that follows the system's hierarchy, plus the elements that have no classification in it. Select items to highlight their elements, double-click one to select its elements in Archicad, and export the counts to Excel or CSV. Based on the get_elements_by_classification.py workflow example. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ClassificationOverview.py))
- **Complex Element Finder**: Finds the elements that make the project heavy: polylines, fills, slabs and other polygonal elements with too many points in their outline, and elements whose 3D model has too many polygons (imported objects, morphs, detailed library parts). Lists them, highlights them in red and selects them in Archicad on request. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ComplexElementFinder.py))
- **Copy Settings to Selection**: Copies the settings of one element to the selected elements of the same type, without their geometry: the eyedropper and syringe for many elements at once. The source's settings are saved as a temporary Favorite, applied to the selected elements with ApplyFavoritesToElements, and the Favorite is deleted again. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/CopySettingsToSelection.py))
- **Distribution Board Schedule**: Lists the circuits of every distribution board with their loads, totals each board and its phases, flags the circuits over a load limit and the boards whose phases are out of balance, and saves the schedule as CSV or Excel. It only reads the project. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/DistributionBoardSchedule.py))
- **Door and Window Numbering by Zone**: Gives every door and window an Element ID built from the zone it opens into, such as 1.04-D1 or 1.04-W2, numbered within each zone. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/DoorWindowNumberingByZone.py))
- **Drawing Status Report**: Lists every Drawing placed on the layouts of the Layout Book with the columns of Archicad's Drawing Manager: status, update type, stored in project, source and path. Export the list to Excel or CSV, or update the drawings whose source has changed: the script shows which drawings it will update and asks before updating them, then reports the drawings it could not update. Reading opens each layout in turn (Archicad gives a drawing's data only from its own layout) and then goes back to the window that was active. Based on the get_drawing_manager_data.py workflow example. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/DrawingStatusReport.py))
- **Electrical and Plumbing Check**: Before drawings are issued, lists the electrical and plumbing symbols that miss data: GDL symbols whose circuit, board or number parameter (chosen by the user) is empty or names a board that does not exist, Archicad 30 electrical devices that are not connected to a circuit, Archicad 30 circuits without devices, and sanitary objects that are outside every zone. Each group can be highlighted and selected in Archicad. The script only reads the model; it changes nothing but the highlight and the selection. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ElectricalPlumbingCheck.py))
- **Material Take-Off**: Totals the volume (m³) and the projected area (m²) of every building material used by the walls, columns, beams, slabs, roofs and shells, per story and optionally per element type, from the quantities Archicad calculates for each skin. The table can be copied to the clipboard or saved as Excel or CSV for a bill of quantities. It only reads the project. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/MaterialTakeOff.py))
- **Missing Library Parts**: Lists the library parts the placed Objects, Lamps, Windows and Doors use but the loaded libraries do not have (the elements Archicad shows as dots, e.g. after migrating a project), with the elements that use each one, per story. The elements can be selected in Archicad, or switched to a loaded library part with ChangeLibraryPartOfElements. Nothing is changed before the list of elements to change is confirmed; a report then shows the result of each one. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/MissingLibraryParts.py))
- **Object Counter**: Counts the placed objects, lamps, doors, windows and (from Archicad 30) electrical devices by library part, grouped by story and by the zone they stand in. The zone is found from the element's position and the zone polygons of its story. Optionally it also sums one numeric GDL parameter, for example a fixture's load or its drainage fixture units. The table can be saved as CSV or Excel. The script only reads the model; it changes nothing in it (it can select the counted elements). ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ObjectCounter.py))
- **Non-orthogonal Wall Finder**: Lists the walls that are not aligned to the allowed angle grid (every 90° or every 45°), highlights them in red and selects them in Archicad on request. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/OrthoWallFinder.py))
- **Place Symbols in Rooms**: Places a library part in the chosen zones by a rule: - along the zone's boundary at a spacing and a mounting height, keeping a distance from the corners and the doors (for example sockets), or - in a grid with a maximum spacing and a margin from the walls (for example lights). ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PlaceSymbolsInRooms.py))
- **Project Health Check**: Runs quality checks on the model and lists what it finds: elements without an Element ID, zones with the same number, unclassified elements, duplicate elements in the same place, very small elements, elements far from the project origin, elements on hidden layers, stories without elements and layers that no floor plan element uses. The findings can be highlighted and selected in Archicad, exported to Excel or CSV, and turned into Issues. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ProjectHealthCheck.py))
- **Property Highlighter**: Colors the elements in the model by the value of a chosen property, with a legend of the values and their element counts. Text values get one color each; number values can also be grouped into ranges with a color gradient. Select values in the legend to highlight only those, double-click one to select its elements in Archicad. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyHighlighter.py))
- **Property Value Exporter**: Writes the values of the chosen properties of the chosen element types into an Excel workbook or a CSV file, one row per element, without changing anything in the project. It replaces building an interactive schedule only to copy its values into Excel. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/PropertyValueExporter.py))
- **Room Finishes Schedule**: Lists the floor, wall and ceiling finish areas of every zone (or of the selected zones), one row per zone and finish, and saves the table as CSV or Excel. It reads only; nothing in the project is changed. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/RoomFinishesSchedule.py))
- **Run Lengths**: Totals the lengths of pipe, duct and wiring runs in two ways, side by side: the MEP Modeler routes and flexible segments per domain, MEP system and size, and the 2D lines, polylines and arcs drawn for them, per layer, pen or line type. In Archicad 30 each electrical circuit's estimated cable length is listed as well. The table can be copied or saved as CSV or Excel. It reads only; nothing in the project is changed. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/RunLengths.py))
- **Sheet Index Export**: Walks the Layout Book and lists one row per layout: its subset, number, name, paper size, the current revision and that revision's changes. The list can be saved as an Excel or CSV file, or copied to the clipboard to paste into a spreadsheet. It only reads the project; nothing in Archicad is changed. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/SheetIndexExport.py))
- **Solid Operation Explorer**: Lists the solid element operation links (target, operation, operator) of the elements, highlights the targets and operators, and finds the links that have no effect any more because the two elements do not touch. The chosen links can be removed. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/SolidOperationExplorer.py))
- **Story Setup**: Sets up the stories of the project from a table: paste it (name and level or height per row, from Excel or any text) or load a CSV file. The current stories are shown next to the new ones with what would be added, renamed, moved and deleted, and nothing changes until you press Apply. A table that would delete a story with elements on it is refused. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/StorySetup.py))
- **Find and Replace in Texts**: Searches the content of every Text and text Label (the selection, the current story or the whole project), with match case and whole word options. Every match is listed with its story and a preview of the changed line, with a checkbox per match; only the checked matches are replaced. The replacement is written with ChangeTextContent, so the styles of the rest of the content and the autotexts in it stay as they are. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/TextFindReplace.py))
- **Unused View Cleaner**: Finds the views of the View Map that are neither placed on a layout nor published by a Publisher Set, and moves the chosen ones into a separate folder that repeats their original folder structure. A clone folder is only moved as a whole, when none of its views is used. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/UnusedViewCleaner.py))
- **Wall Clearance**: Finds the doors, windows and objects whose space is too close to a wall and moves them just enough. One rule for every kind: - the element's space is its own floor plan outline (the convex hull of what Archicad draws for it: an object's symbol, rotated with it) plus a margin. Archicad draws doors and windows as part of their wall and gives no outline of their own, so a door's or window's space is its opening in the wall: its width (centerOffset +/- width / 2) across the wall's thickness. The swing of a door is not part of it; - the obstructions are the walls, columns and curtain walls cut on its story (their floor plan cut fill, GetDetailsOfElements floorPlanPolygons), except the wall a door or window sits in and the wall an object stands against; - the space must not come closer to an obstruction than the margin. Now in the list is the smallest gap (negative when they overlap), Needed is the margin. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/WallClearance.py))
- **Zone Area Check**: Compares the measured area of every zone with a target area read from a property you choose, within a tolerance in percent. Lists the zones that are over, under and on target, and highlights them in three colors. It changes nothing in the project apart from the highlight. Select rows to highlight only those zones, double-click one to select it in Archicad, and export the list to Excel or CSV. ([source](https://github.com/ENZYME-APD/tapir-archicad-automation/blob/main/builtin-scripts/ZoneAreaCheck.py))

# Command reference (one line each)

Parameters and results of each: https://archicad-api.com/commands.md. ## Application Commands

- **GetAddOnVersion** (since 0.1.0): Retrieves the version of the Tapir Additional JSON Commands Add-On.
- **GetCommands** (since 2.0.0): Retrieves every command of the Tapir Add-On with its command group, the Tapir version it was introduced in and its description, so a script can check that a command exists before calling it.
- **GetArchicadLocation** (since 0.1.0): Retrieves the location of the currently running Archicad executable.
- **GetArchicadReleaseInfo** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the main version, release version and build number of the running Archicad, with the caption of its window.
- **GetArchicadLicenseInfo** (since 2.0.0): Retrieves the license the running Archicad runs on: its type (Full, Education, Trial, Demo, Start or BIMcloud Team Client), the raw protection mode with its bits by name, and the highest Software Service Agreement (SSA) level of the license, so a script can warn before it uses a feature the license lacks. The SSA level is not available in Archicad 25.
- **GetPrinterInfo** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves Archicad's current print settings: the print area, grid, fixed text size and scale (the settings PrintView takes).
- **GetPrinterAndPlotterInfo** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the printer selected in Archicad, with its name and orientation, and the selected plotter, with its name and model.
- **QuitArchicad** (since 0.1.0): Performs a quit operation on the currently running Archicad instance.
- **GetPointFromUser** (since 1.5.9): Asks the designer to click a point in the current window and returns it. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; the call fails when the input is cancelled. Parameters: prompt, snapFilter, constraint.
- **ModelToScreen** (since 1.8.0): Converts model coordinates to pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window (not global desktop coordinates), using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. In a 3D window the coordinates are projected with the current camera; in other windows z is disregarded. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: coordinates.
- **ScreenToModel** (since 1.8.0): Converts pixel positions local to the current Archicad view window to 2D model coordinates of the current database, using the current window's size, drawing scale and zoom. It is a 2D mapping: it does not reconstruct a 3D point, and several model coordinates can map to the same pixel. Parameters: screenPoints.
- **GetElementFromUser** (since 1.7.3): Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled. Parameters: prompt, elementTypes, snapFilter, constraint.
- **GetCurrentTool** (since 2.0.0): Returns the tool active in the Toolbox: its element type, its variation (the subtype, e.g. Door, Skylight or a library part subtype of an add-on) and, for the tools of add-ons, its class id, in the form SetCurrentTool accepts. Nothing is returned when the active tool makes no element, e.g. the Arrow or the Marquee.
- **SetCurrentTool** (since 2.0.0): Activates a tool in the Toolbox, given as GetCurrentTool or GetToolboxItems returns it; an empty input activates the Arrow. Archicad switches the tool once it processes its events, so GetCurrentTool may still return the previous tool right after this command. Parameters: elementType, variation, classId.
- **GetToolboxItems** (since 2.0.0): Lists the tools of the Toolbox, the tools of add-ons included, in the form SetCurrentTool accepts, and the active tool. includeHidden also lists the tools without an icon, e.g. the Slab Accessory. Parameters: includeHidden.
- **GetLineFromUser** (since 1.8.0): Waits for the user to input a line in the active Archicad window and returns start and end coordinates. Parameters: startPrompt, endPrompt, showRubberLineFeedback, snapFilter, constraint.
- **GetArcFromUser** (since 2.0.0): Asks the designer to draw an arc in the current window - its center, its start point (which sets the radius) and its end point - with a rubber-band circle shown while drawing, and returns its center, radius, start and end angles, the angle it turns through, its direction and its start and end points. Archicad waits for the clicks or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled. Parameters: centerPrompt, startPrompt, endPrompt, showRubberArcFeedback, snapFilter, constraint.
- **GetPolygonFromUser** (since 1.8.0): Waits for the user to input a polygon in the active Archicad window and returns its points and arcs. Parameters: startPrompt, prompt, method, snapFilter, constraint.
- **GetMagicWandSettings** (since 2.0.0): Returns the settings of Archicad's Magic Wand Settings dialog: how curves are approximated with straight segments (a number of segments along arcs or circles, a largest deviation from the curve, or a segment length) and the trace method. Useful to know how the Magic Wand will trace a curve. Changes nothing in the project.
- **ConvertImages** (since 2.0.0): Converts base64 encoded images from one image format to another with Archicad's own image converters, for example a PNG preview image to JPEG. The formats are Bitmap, GIF, TIFF, JPEG and PNG, or the MIME type of another format Archicad can read or write. The output is aligned with the input array of images. Changes nothing in the project. Parameters: images.
- **GetCurrentWindowType** (since 1.0.7): Returns the type of the current (active) window and, when it has one, the databaseId of the database it shows, which ChangeWindow takes to bring the window back after a script switched to another one. The saved view (View Map item) the window was opened from is not returned, as Archicad does not tell which one it was.
- **GetCurrentWindowDrawingScale** (since 1.7.3): Returns the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, as its denominator: 100.0 for 1:100, 20.0 for 1:20. Unlike GetViewSettings it needs no saved view. It reads the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts always return 1.0.
- **SetCurrentWindowDrawingScale** (since 1.7.3): Changes the drawing scale of the current (active) window, the scale shown in the bottom bar, to the given denominator: 100 for 1:100. It changes the scale of the current database: the floor plan, a section, elevation, interior elevation, detail, worksheet or 3D document window, each of which has its own. Layouts are always 1:1 and are rejected. The scale must be between 1 and 30000. The change is undoable. Parameters: scale, rebuild.
- **ChangeWindow** (since 1.3.1): Changes the current (active) window to the given window. A databaseId on its own is enough; the window type is taken from the database. The databaseId of a worksheet or detail whose window was never opened opens its Project Map item instead (from Archicad 27). With windowType 'FloorPlan' and a storyIndex it also activates that story on the floor plan. windowType 'Report' on its own opens the Session Report window (from Archicad 26); its text cannot be read through the Archicad API.
- **GetContainingDatabases** (since 1.7.3): Returns the database (window type, database id and name) that contains each of the given elements, from any database, not only the current one. Pass the windowType and databaseId to ChangeWindow to open it, for example to find an element placed on a layout. Parameters: elements.
- **CloseWindows** (since 1.8.0): Closes the windows of the given databases (for example layouts, sections or details opened earlier with ChangeWindow), with one execution result per window; a window Archicad cannot close gets a failed result. Requires Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: windows.
- **RebuildCurrentDatabase** (since 1.8.0): Rebuilds the current database, the one the API works on (see ChangeWindow). Requires Archicad 27 or later.
- **DeleteGhostRecords** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the trace (ghost) record of each given parent database, which removes the trace reference shown in that database's window. A database without a trace reference gets a failed execution result. Not undoable. Parameters: databases.
- **GetUserGSID** (since 1.5.6): Get the current registered User-GSID and OrganizationsID. Requires Archicad 27 or later.
- **ShowAlert** (since 1.5.6): Display a dialog with up to three buttons. Parameters: alertType, title, message, subMessage, button1, button2, button3.
- **ShowNotificationBubble** (since 2.0.0): Shows a non-blocking notification bubble with a message in the current Archicad window, e.g. to report progress or a result without stopping the user as ShowAlert does. The bubble disappears by itself after the timeout. It is shown at a model coordinate or a pixel position of the current view, by default at the center of the current 2D view. Optionally it gets a large icon, is shown at most a given number of times, or is turned off, until the user runs 'Enable all informational messages'. Returns the bubble's settings read back from Archicad. Requires Archicad 29 or later. Parameters: message, icon, timeoutMilliseconds, coordinate, screenPoint, offset, largeIcon, redrawCountLimit, disabled.
- **GetSpecialFolders** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the filesystem paths of the special folders of the running Archicad (preferences, cache, data, temporary, application, defaults, templates, help, embedded project library, etc.). Parameters: folderTypes.
- **GetEditModeState** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether Archicad is in a hierarchical editing mode (curtain wall, stair, beam or column editing), and which element is being edited. Read only: it never enters, leaves or cancels an editing mode. Commands that modify the project can fail while such a mode is active. The overall inEditMode flag requires Archicad 29 or later; the command requires Archicad 27 or later.
- **GetArchicadVisibility** (since 1.8.0): Returns whether the Archicad application is shown or hidden. Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error.
- **SetArchicadVisibility** (since 1.8.0): Hides or shows the Archicad application, e.g. to keep it out of the way while a batch runs. A script that hides Archicad must show it again, also when the script fails (e.g. in a finally block). Supported on Windows only; on macOS it returns an error. Parameters: isVisible.
- **RunActionCenterChecks** (since 1.8.0): Runs the given checks of the Action Center (by default the hotlink check). A successful result means the check ran, not that nothing was found: Archicad does not report the outcome to the caller, it shows the Action Center tab when the check found an issue. Parameters: checks.
- **RedrawCurrentDatabase** (since 1.8.0): Redraws the current database, even when its window is in the background. Only the visible region of its window is updated.
- **GetProductVersionInfo** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the version information of the running Archicad: build number, language code, product family and version text, plus the product name, product type, main/update/hotfix versions, the available domains (Architecture, MEP) and the CEIP project identifier of the open project from Archicad 29. Requires Archicad 28 or later.
- **Get3DCutawayStatus** (since 1.7.3): Returns whether 3D Cutaway is on and whether the cutting planes are shown in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open.
- **Set3DCutawayStatus** (since 1.7.3): Turns 3D Cutaway on or off and shows or hides the cutting planes in the 3D window. In Archicad 25-27 the 3D window may need to be open. Parameters: cutawayEnabled, cuttingPlanesVisible.
- **SetDialogAutoClose** (since 1.7.3): Turns the dialog auto close on or off. While it is on, Archicad closes the dialogs it would show with their default button instead of waiting for the user, so automation is not blocked by them. To have it on already while Archicad opens a project (before any command can be sent), set the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable to true for the Archicad process before starting it. Parameters: enabled.
- **GetDialogAutoClose** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the dialog auto close is on, the same state SetDialogAutoClose writes, so a script can restore it afterwards. The state belongs to the running Archicad process: it is off when Archicad starts (unless the TAPIR_DIALOG_AUTOCLOSE environment variable is true), it stays as last set until Archicad quits, and it is shared by every add-on and script in that Archicad.

## Project Commands

- **GetProjectInfo** (since 0.1.0): Retrieves information about the currently loaded project.
- **GetProjectInfoFields** (since 0.1.2): Retrieves the names and values of all project info fields.
- **SetProjectInfoField** (since 0.1.2): Sets the value of a project info field. Parameters: projectInfoId, projectInfoValue.
- **CreateProjectInfoFields** (since 1.5.2): Creates one or more custom project info fields. From Archicad 30 the Project Info group of each field can be given; without it the field goes to the first group. Parameters: projectInfoFields.
- **DeleteProjectInfoFields** (since 1.5.4): Deletes one or more custom project info fields, by their autotext keys or, from Archicad 30, by the ids of the fields of the Project Info groups. Hardcoded fields cannot be deleted. Parameters: projectInfoIds, projectInfoFieldIds.
- **RenameProjectInfoFields** (since 2.0.0): Renames custom fields of the Project Info groups. Fixed (built-in) fields cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoFields.
- **MoveProjectInfoFields** (since 2.0.0): Moves fields of the Project Info groups to a group, before another field of it or to its end. A subfield of a calculated field moves with its parent field. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoFields.
- **GetProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the Project Info groups in their order, each with its fields: id, name, value and, when exactly one project info autotext has the name of the field, the autotext key that SetProjectInfoField takes. Available from Archicad 30.
- **CreateProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Creates Project Info groups with the given names, at the end of the group list. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **RenameProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Renames Project Info groups. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **DeleteProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Deletes Project Info groups. A group that contains fixed (built-in) fields cannot be deleted. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **MoveProjectInfoGroups** (since 1.8.0): Moves Project Info groups before another group, or to the end of the group list when no other group is given. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: projectInfoGroups.
- **GetStories** (since 1.1.5): Retrieves information about the story structure of the currently loaded project: index, floor id, name, level, height and, from Archicad 28, the IFC GlobalId of each story.
- **SetStories** (since 1.1.5): Sets the story sructure of the currently loaded project. Parameters: stories.
- **GetAutoTextKeys** (since 1.5.9): Retrieves the available autotext keys (name and embeddable key): the Project Info, layout, drawing, date and other autotexts Archicad lists, and the property based ones, optionally for a specific element. Embed a key in a Text or Label content by surrounding it with '<' and '>'. Parameters: elementId.
- **GetAutoTextName** (since 1.5.9): Retrieves the display names of one or more autotext keys (as returned inside a '<...>' embedded key), with a direct guid lookup for property-based keys instead of enumerating every property definition. Parameters: keys.
- **GetAllAutoTextKeys** (since 2.0.0): Retrieves every autotext key Archicad knows (not only the property-based ones returned by GetAutoTextKeys) with its current value, resolved without an element context.
- **InterpretAutoTexts** (since 2.0.0): Resolves one or more autotexts (e.g. '<LAYOUTID>') to their values, optionally in the context of an element, so a key can be tested before it is written into a Text or Label. Parameters: autoTexts, elementId.
- **GetNoteAutotexts** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the autotexts available in the notes of an element type (e.g. a Dimension), each with the element types it is available for. The autotexts are identified by the numeric value of their API_NoteAutotextID. For a Dimension, the optional dimensionAppearance (Linear by default) chooses the dimension type. Needs Archicad 26 or later. Parameters: noteOwnerType, dimensionAppearance.
- **GetNoteAutoTextKeywords** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the keywords of note autotexts (the autotexts of dimension, label and other element notes) by their numeric API_NoteAutotextID values. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: autoTextIds.
- **GetHotlinks** (since 0.1.0): Gets the file system locations (path) of the hotlink modules and the instance elements placed from each node. The hotlinks can have tree hierarchy in the project.
- **CreateHotlinkNodes** (since 1.5.9): Creates hotlink module nodes from source files. A node that already points at the same file is returned instead of duplicated (Archicad 26 and later; 25 cannot see an unplaced node). Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **CreateHotlinkInstances** (since 1.5.9): Places instances of hotlink module nodes at an origin, rotation and mirroring. Parameters: hotlinkInstances.
- **ChangeHotlinkInstances** (since 1.5.9): Moves, rotates or mirrors placed hotlink instances by changing their transformation. MoveElements and RotateElements do not work on hotlink instances. Parameters: hotlinkInstances.
- **UpdateHotlinks** (since 1.7.1): Re-reads the source files of hotlink module nodes and refreshes their cached content in the project, as the Hotlink Manager's Update button does. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **ChangeHotlinkNodes** (since 1.7.1): Repoints hotlink module nodes at other source files, as the Hotlink Manager's Relink button does. Follow it with UpdateHotlinks to re-read the content. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **BreakHotlinkNodes** (since 1.8.0): Breaks hotlink nodes, as the Hotlink Manager's Break Hotlink does: the elements of each node's placed instances stay in the project as ordinary elements, no longer tied to the source file. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **DeleteHotlinkNodes** (since 1.8.0): Deletes hotlink nodes together with their placed instances, as the Hotlink Manager's Delete does. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.
- **GetHotlinkOwnersOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Tells for each element whether it comes from a hotlinked module, and returns the hotlink element that contains it and the hotlink instance it belongs to. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements.
- **GetHotlinkProxyElementTable** (since 1.7.3): Maps the proxy elements of placed hotlink instances to the elements of the source file they were made from, so an element seen in a hotlinked module can be traced back to its source element. Parameters: hotlinkInstances.
- **GetHotlinkSourceStatus** (since 1.8.0): Tells for each hotlink source file whether it is available, missing, not accessible, incompatible or offline. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: hotlinks.
- **OpenProject** (since 1.0.7): Opens the given project. The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded without asking: Archicad has no query for them, so call SaveProject first when they must be kept. Parameters: projectFilePath.
- **NewProject** (since 1.7.3): Starts a new, untitled project from the template set in Archicad's New Project settings, as File > New does; with newAndReset also the working environment is reset, as New and Reset All does. The unsaved changes of the open project are discarded, as with OpenProject. Parameters: newAndReset.
- **CloseProject** (since 1.3.1): Closes the currently opened project.
- **SaveProject** (since 1.3.1): Saves the currently opened project, in place or to a given path. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file at the path. Parameters: projectPath, overwrite.
- **SaveAsModuleFile** (since 1.5.9): Saves the given elements, or the current selection, as a hotlink module (.mod) file. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file. Parameters: moduleFilePath, overwrite, elements.
- **SaveProjectAsArchive** (since 1.6.0): Saves the open project as an archive (.pla) file, with the library parts it uses inside. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file. Parameters: archiveFilePath, overwrite, includeLibraryParts, includeProperties, includeTextures, includeBackgroundPicture.
- **GetRenderingScenes** (since 1.8.0): Gets the names of the rendering scenes of the project (the Scene list of the PhotoRendering Settings palette), the most recently used first, and the name of the current scene.
- **SetCurrentRenderingScene** (since 1.8.0): Makes the given rendering scene the current one, as selecting it in the PhotoRendering Settings palette does. Parameters: sceneName.
- **PhotoRender** (since 1.8.0): Renders the 3D model with the current rendering scene, or with the given one, as Document > Creative Imaging > PhotoRender Projection does, and saves the image to a file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif). The image size, resolution and quality come from the scene; a width, height or resolution given here is used for this render only, the scene is not changed. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file. Parameters: imageFilePath, overwrite, format, sceneName, width, height, resolution.
- **SaveCurrentWindowAsImage** (since 1.7.2): Saves what the current window shows as an image file (png, jpg, bmp, tiff or gif), as File > Save as does with a picture format. Master layout windows are not supported: save a layout that uses the master layout instead. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file. Parameters: imageFilePath, overwrite, format, colorDepth, dithered, entireDrawing.
- **GetCurrentViewImage** (since 1.7.3): Returns what the 3D window, or the PhotoRendering window, shows as a base64 encoded png or jpg image with its size in pixels, without writing a file. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: source, format.
- **GetCalculationUnits** (since 1.4.0): Gets the project calculation units.
- **GetDimensionStandards** (since 1.8.0): Gets the dimension standards of the project (Options > Project Preferences > Dimensions) with their name and the unit, decimals and rounding of each dimension type, optionally only the one with the given name. Read-only. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: name.
- **GetExportTolerance** (since 1.8.0): Gets the export tolerance: the largest distance allowed between an arc and the straight segments that replace it when curves are segmented for export. Archicad only provides this value while an export is in progress, so outside an export the command returns an error saying so.
- **GetLast3DDefaultLevels** (since 1.8.0): Gets the last 3D default levels of the given element types' defaults. Parameters: elementTypes.
- **SetLast3DDefaultLevels** (since 1.8.0): Sets the last 3D default levels of the given element types' defaults. Parameters: elementTypes, levels.
- **GetProjectPreferences** (since 1.7.3): Gets pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units, the zones and the reference levels, and the Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings. Further pages may follow. Parameters: preferenceTypes.
- **SetProjectPreferences** (since 1.7.3): Changes pages of the project preferences (Options > Project Preferences): the working units, the dimensions, the calculation units, the zones and the reference levels, and the Floor Plan Cut Plane Settings. Only the given fields change, the rest of each page keeps its value. In Teamwork the PreferencesDialog lockable object set has to be reserved first (ReserveLockableObjectSet). Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: workingUnits, dimensions, calculationUnits, zones, referenceLevels, floorPlanCutPlane.
- **ConvertUnitValues** (since 1.8.0): Formats lengths, areas, volumes and angles (given in meters, square meters, cubic meters and radians) as Archicad shows them with the unit and rounding of the given Project Preference, returning the text, its extra accuracy decimals and the unit. The output is aligned with the input array of values. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: values.
- **GetRenovationStatusNames** (since 1.8.0): Gets the names the running Archicad shows for the renovation statuses Existing, New and Demolished (localized). Available from Archicad 27.
- **GetGeoLocation** (since 1.1.6): Gets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26).
- **GetSurveyPointTransformation** (since 1.7.3): Gets the 3x4 matrix that transforms points from the Project Origin coordinate system into the Survey Point coordinate system, row by row, and its inverse when it is invertible. Read only. Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetGeoLocation** (since 1.2.9): Sets the project location details: the project location, and the survey point's position, geo-referencing parameters, visibility and lock state (the lock from Archicad 26). Omitted fields stay unchanged. Parameters: projectLocation, surveyPoint.
- **SetPlaceSettings** (since 1.8.0): Changes the place settings of the project: location (longitude, latitude, altitude, north), date, time, summer time and time zone. Only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back, with the sun position Archicad calculated for them. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: placeInfo.
- **FindDimensionStandard** (since 1.8.0): Finds a dimension standard (Options > Project Preferences > Dimensions) by its name and returns its index, name and guid. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: name.
- **GetProjectNotes** (since 1.7.3): Gets the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes): client, project name, company, address, architect, draftsmen, project status, date of issue, keywords and notes.
- **SetProjectNotes** (since 1.7.3): Changes the Project Notes of the project (File > Info > Project Notes). Only the given fields are changed; texts longer than the field Archicad stores are truncated. architect and draftsmen are full names that Archicad keeps as name parts: a new name is stored in the given name with the other parts cleared, and the parts of a name that is not given or not changed are kept. Parameters: client, projectName, company, street, city, country, postalCode, architect, draftsmen, projectStatus, dateOfIssue, keywords, notes.
- **GetSunSettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the project's date and time (Options > Project Preferences > Location Settings), the sun position Archicad calculates for them at the project location, and the sun and ambient light settings.
- **CalculateSunPosition** (since 1.8.0): Calculates the sun position (azimuth and altitude in degrees) for a date and time, at the project location unless another one is given, without changing the project. Parameters: dateTime, location.
- **GetCoordinateOrigins** (since 2.0.0): Gets the offset of the virtual coordinate system origin from the world origin, and the user origin of the current database. Use it to tell which origin the coordinates of different sources (elements, views, survey point) are relative to.
- **PrintView** (since 1.3.1): Prints from the current view. Parameters: grid, fixText, scale, printArea.
- **RebuildView** (since 1.5.0): Rebuilds the current view. Parameters: regenerate.
- **GetAutoIntersect** (since 1.8.0): Gets whether Auto-Intersection (Options > Auto-Intersection) is on. It changes what the wall and beam creation commands produce: with it on, the new elements are joined at their intersections.
- **SetAutoIntersect** (since 1.8.0): Turns Auto-Intersection on or off. It is a setting of the running Archicad, not of the project; remember to restore the previous state afterwards. Parameters: isOn.
- **ResolveNames** (since 2.0.0): Looks up words or phrases (for example from a user's question) among the names of the open project before they are passed to other commands: stories, layers, layer combinations, building materials, composites, profiles, surfaces, fills, lines, zone categories, element types (by API name and, from Archicad 27, by the name the Archicad interface shows), properties (by name, and by group and name together) and classifications (systems by name and version, items of every system by name and ID). For each name it returns 'found' with the items named exactly so, 'closeMatches' with the nearest names, best first (ranked by differences in case, accents, spacing and separators, shared words, one name containing the other and a few differing characters), or 'notFound' when nothing in the project is close, meaning the project has no such item and it must not be guessed. Each match carries what the other commands take: the story index, the attribute id and index, the elementType, the propertyId (with the property's group, value type and the classification items a custom property is available for), or the classificationSystemId and classificationItemId. Matching is lexical and deterministic. Read only. Parameters: names, maxCloseMatches.

## Custom Data Commands

- **SetElementUserData** (since 1.8.0): Stores string values under keys on elements, for scripts to keep their own state per element (external database ids, sync timestamps, markers). The data is saved with the project as the user data of the Tapir add-on on the element and appears nowhere in the Archicad UI. The given keys are merged into what the element already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. One undo step per call; in a Teamwork project the element has to be reserved. Parameters: elementUserData.
- **GetElementUserData** (since 1.8.0): Reads the values stored on elements by SetElementUserData: every key of each element, or only the given keys. Parameters: elements, keys.

## Element Commands

- **GetSelectedElements** (since 0.1.0): Gets the list of the currently selected elements.
- **GetElementsByType** (since 1.0.7): Returns the identifier of every element of the given type on the plan. It works for any type. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Parameters: elementType, filters, databases.
- **GetAllElements** (since 1.0.7): Returns the identifier of all elements on the plan. Use the optional filter parameter for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Parameters: filters, databases.
- **CaptureElementState** (since 1.8.0): Captures the current state of the elements of the project and returns a stateId for it, so that GetElementChangesSince can later list what was created, modified and deleted since. The optional type selects how changes are detected (modification stamps by default, or the 3D model). The state is kept in a file in the temporary folder for the Archicad session only: it is lost when the project is closed or Archicad restarts, and ReleaseElementState frees it earlier. Parameters: type.
- **GetElementChangesSince** (since 1.8.0): Returns the new, modified and deleted elements between a state captured by CaptureElementState and either another captured state (toStateId) or the current state of the project. Scripts that keep an external copy of the model use it to sync only what changed instead of re-reading every element. The changes come from Archicad's element difference generator, which tracks the model elements: 2D elements such as texts, labels and hatches can be missing from the lists, so read those directly. Fails for a stateId that is unknown - never captured, released, or lost because the project was closed or Archicad restarted. Parameters: stateId, toStateId.
- **ReleaseElementState** (since 1.8.0): Frees a state captured by CaptureElementState. Every state is freed anyway when the project is closed or Archicad quits. Parameters: stateId.
- **GetElementTypeNames** (since 1.7.3): Gets the localized names of the given element types, as the running Archicad shows them (for example 'Wand' for Wall in German Archicad). The output is aligned with the input array of element types. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elementTypes.
- **GetElementsInCreationOrder** (since 1.8.0): Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in the order the elements were created. Parameters: databases.
- **ChangeSelectionOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Adds/removes a number of elements to/from the current selection. Parameters: addElementsToSelection, removeElementsFromSelection.
- **DeselectAll** (since 2.0.0): Clears the selection in the current window.
- **GetMarquee** (since 2.0.0): Gets the marquee of the current window: its shape (rectangle, rotated rectangle or polygon), whether it is multi-story, and its outline as a polygon. Returns the type 'none' when there is no marquee.
- **SetMarquee** (since 2.0.0): Draws a marquee in the current window from a polygon or a box (optionally rotated), single- or multi-story. Called without polygon and box it removes the marquee. Parameters: polygon, box, rotationAngle, multiStory.
- **FilterElements** (since 1.0.7): Keeps the elements that match all the given criteria: Archicad's flag filters (filters), layer (layerIndices), home story (floorIndices), element type (elementTypes) and hotlink (fromHotlink, hotlinkIds). Within one criterion any of the listed values matches; an omitted criterion does not filter. Parameters: elements, filters, layerIndices, floorIndices, elementTypes, fromHotlink, hotlinkIds.
- **GetElementsByCriteria** (since 2.0.0): Returns the elements, or with countOnly only their number, that match all the given criteria: element types, home stories, layers, Archicad's element filter flags and property criteria (a value compared in internal units, or a value status such as hasValue, isUserUndefined, isNotAvailable, isDefault or hasCustomValue). An unknown type, property or operator is an error, not ignored. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Parameters: types, floorIndices, layerIndices, filters, propertyCriteria, countOnly, limit.
- **GetDetailsOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Gets the details of elements (geometry parameters etc). When elements is omitted, all elements matching the optional server-side filter (types, floorIndices, layerIndices) are queried; an empty elements list returns no details. Use the optional fields parameter to return only the fields you need (e.g. elementId, type, id, floorIndex) and skip the computation of the others (for example floorPlanPolygons). Use the optional additionalFields parameter to also get the info string, the compound info string, the library part unique ID and the creator tool unique ID. An element of another database (a layout, a section, a worksheet ...) returns only its header fields (type, floor index, layer, draw index) with fromOtherDatabase set to true. Parameters: elements, fields, filter, additionalFields.
- **SetDetailsOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Sets the details of the given elements. Every element type: Element ID (id), story (floorIndex), layer (layerIndex) and display order (drawIndex). In typeSpecificDetails: Wall - start and end point, height, base offset, and the start and end thickness of a trapezoid wall; Zone - the ZoneSettings fields (the same as ModifyZones); Line - start and end point, pen, line type, room separator; Arc and Circle - origin, radius, angle, ratio, start and end angle (arcs only), reflected, pen, line type, room separator; Polyline - points and arcs, pen, line type, room separator; Spline - pen, line type, room separator; Hatch - outline, holes, contour pen, fill pen and background pen or colors, fill or building material, area display, room special and fill orientation; Hotspot - position, height, pen; Text - text, position, angle, height, justification; Label - the text of a text label; Drawing - position, angle, ratio, model offset, clip polygon (isCutWithFrame), name, ID and numbering, scale in Autotext, border, title library part, pen table (penTableUsageMode, penTableIndex), colorMode, isTransparentBackground, rasterizeDPI and the anchor (anchorPoint, useOwnOriginAsAnchor). Not written, because the Archicad API does not take them: the geometry of a Spline, the source of a Drawing (use ChangeDrawingLink), the Drawing Manager's update type and stored in project, and often a placed Drawing's drawingScale, which comes from its source view (the element's result then names the kept value). Other wall, slab, column, beam, stair and object settings are written by their Modify commands. An element Archicad does not let you edit (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not reserved by you in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason; a Drawing setting Archicad kept unchanged is named in a failed execution result too. Parameters: elementsWithDetails.
- **SetElementInfoStrings** (since 1.8.0): Sets the info string of the given elements: the Element ID shown in the Info Box, which GetDetailsOfElements returns as id. Returns one execution result per element. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElementCategories** (since 1.7.3): Lists the element categories of the project (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status, Renovation Filter and, in the German version, BRI) with their possible values. The names of the categories and values are localized: identify a category by its type and a value by its categoryValueId, never by name.
- **GetCategoryValuesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, optionally only for the given category types. An element that has none of the requested categories (an annotation, for example) gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. Parameters: elements, categories.
- **GetCategoryValuesOfDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Gets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the tool defaults of the given element types, the values new elements of the type get, optionally only for the given category types. A category the default has no value in is listed without categoryValueId; an element type without any of the requested categories gets an error item. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. Parameters: elementTypes, categories.
- **SetCategoryValuesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Sets the category values (Structural Function, Position, Renovation Status ...) of the given elements, one element and one category per item, in a single undoable step. The value must belong to the given category, as GetElementCategories lists them; an element without that category gets a failed execution result. The names are localized: use the type and the categoryValueId in scripts. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's value in the category now (oldValue) and the value a real run would set (newValue). Parameters: elementCategoryValues, dryRun.
- **Get3DBoundingBoxes** (since 1.1.2): Get the 3D bounding box of elements. The bounding box is calculated from the global origin in the 3D view. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements. An element without 3D geometry of its own gets an error item instead of a bounding box. Walls, Slabs, Roofs, Zones and Stairs are measured on their 3D model, so the box of a Wall includes its connections to other walls. The current window does not need to show the element: it works with a layout or a section open as well. Parameters: elements.
- **Get2DBoundingBoxes** (since 2.0.0): Get the 2D bounding box of elements as Archicad draws them, in the coordinates of the database the element is in: the floor plan, a section, a worksheet, a layout or a master layout. Works for 2D elements (Line, PolyLine, Arc, Hatch, Text, Label, Dimension, Drawing ...) as well as for model elements; a Text's box covers its drawn lines, a Drawing's box its frame with the title. The current window does not need to show the element. The output is the array of the bounding boxes respective to the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetLibPartTransformations** (since 1.8.0): Gets the placement transformation of library part instances (Window, Door, Object, Lamp, Zone) as Archicad computes it: the location, the rotation angle and the x/y scaling. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetSnapPointsOfElements** (since 2.0.0): Gets the snap points (hotspots) of the given elements, of any element type: the points of an element that the cursor snaps to and dimensions attach to (for example the endpoints of a Wall's reference line or the vertices of a Slab), in world coordinates, each with the neig kind and subindex identifying which point of the element it is. For the 2D hotspots of library part instances see GetHotspotsOfElements. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **ConvertRevealOffsets** (since 1.7.3): Converts the reveal depth offset of windows and doors placed in walls between the two references Archicad uses: measured from the core skin of a composite wall, or from the wall side. Give exactly one of coreOffset or sideOffset per opening; both values are returned. For walls with a basic structure the two values are equal. The output is aligned with the input array of openings. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: openings.
- **Get3DGeometryOfElements** (since 1.7.2): Gets the 3D geometry of elements as the solid bodies of their 3D model: a vertex list in world coordinates and the planar faces (with their holes) referencing it, each face with its surface attribute when that is a project attribute. The bodies of the subelements of a Stair, Railing or Curtain Wall, and of the segments of a Column or Beam, are included. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. The 3D model of the elements is generated as needed, so many elements can take a while. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElementConnections** (since 1.8.0): Gets the connections among the given elements: each pair of touching elements once, with the polygons of the surface where they touch, in world coordinates. The 3D model of the elements is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. Also returns, aligned with the input array of elements, whether each element was found. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetBodyMaterialsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the building material of each body of the 3D model of the given elements. The 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetCutPolygonsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Cuts each body of the 3D model of the given elements with a plane and returns, for each body, its building material, the area of the cut surface and its polygons (outline and holes) in 2D coordinates of the plane. From Archicad 28 the 3D model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so a composite structure has one body per skin and the 3D window is not changed. Before Archicad 28 the bodies are those of the element's 3D model (a composite structure is one body) and their building materials are left out. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements, cutPlane.
- **GetElementAtCoordinate** (since 1.7.3): Finds the element of the given polygonal type (for example Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone or Hatch) at a coordinate of the floor plan of the current database, the way a click there would. Use the optional filters parameter (the values of FilterElements) to consider only, for example, the elements visible by layer, and the optional z parameter to give the elevation of the point. Returns found: false when there is no such element. Useful together with GetPointFromUser. Parameters: elementType, coordinate, z, filters.
- **GetSkylightHolePolygons** (since 1.8.0): Gets the polygon of the hole each given Skylight cuts into its host Roof or Shell: the outline and any holes of it as 2D coordinates. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element that is not a Skylight gets an error item. Parameters: elements.
- **GetVisibleSkinStatus** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether elements have a visible skin in a given Partial Structure Display mode (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly), e.g. a finish-only slab has none in CoreOnly. The current window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements, structureDisplay.
- **GetRoofPlanes** (since 2.0.0): Gets the single planes of roofs, without changing the roofs. A multi-plane roof is decomposed by Archicad into its planes, each returned with its part identifier and its details as a single-plane roof (slope, pivot line, level, outline with arcs and holes); a single-plane roof is returned as its only plane. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetCurtainWallAbsoluteBottoms** (since 1.8.0): Gets the absolute bottom level of curtain walls or their subelements (segments, frames, panels, junctions, accessories). The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetQuantitiesOfElements** (since 1.7.2): Gets the quantities of the given elements calculated by Archicad (volumes, surfaces, lengths etc.), together with the volume and projected area per building material (one item per skin of composite and complex profile elements, one item for basic elements). Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Zone, ColumnSegment, BeamSegment. Use the optional minOpeningSize parameter to control the conditional values, and calculateInOneCall to calculate all the elements in one Archicad call. Parameters: elements, minOpeningSize, calculateInOneCall.
- **TriangulatePolygonsOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Triangulates the plan polygon of the given elements, holes excluded, as Archicad does it: the outline of a Slab, Zone, Hatch or Mesh and the polygon of a Roof. Each triangle is given by the 2D coordinates of its three vertices. With convex: true, the faces of the 3D model of the elements (of any type) are decomposed into convex polygons instead, given by the 3D coordinates of their vertices. The output is aligned with the input array of elements; an element of another type gets an error item. Parameters: elements, convex.
- **GetTextureCoordinates** (since 1.8.0): Gets the texture coordinates (u, v) of the faces of the 3D model of the given elements: per solid body, per face, at the first vertex of the face. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetSurfaceTypesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the surface type of every polygon of the 3D model of the given elements, as ACAPI_Polygon_PolygonId2SurfaceType returns it: for each element its polygons with their body index, polygon index, polygon id and the numeric API_SurfaceTypeID value. The model is generated with separate components in a temporary sight, so the 3D window is not changed. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **Get3DModelCounts** (since 1.8.0): Gets the number of components of each type (bodies, polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices, normal vectors, materials and lights) in the 3D model Archicad currently holds. Bodies, materials and lights are counted with ACAPI_ModelAccess_GetNum; the polygons, polygon edges, edges, vertices and normal vectors, which that function refuses to count, are summed over the bodies. A type that cannot be counted gets an error item. Available from Archicad 27.
- **DeleteUserDataOfElements** (since 2.0.0): Deletes the user data this add-on stored on the given elements. Archicad keeps the user data of an element per add-on, so the data of other add-ons is left as it is. All deletions are one undo step. The output has one execution result per element, aligned with the input array of elements. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that exists gets wouldDelete. Parameters: elements, dryRun.
- **GetSurfaceQuantitiesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the exposed surface areas of the given elements calculated by Archicad: for each element one item per surface attribute and building material pair with the area that is not covered by the covering elements (for example the wall area behind a slab is taken off the wall's surface). The covering elements are the optional coverElements; by default every construction element of the project. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements, coverElements.
- **GetSubelementsOfHierarchicalElements** (since 1.0.6): Gets the subelements of the given hierarchical elements. From Archicad 28 the subelements of external hierarchical elements (for example MEP elements or elements of other add-ons) are returned as externalSubelements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetHierarchicalElementOwners** (since 1.7.3): Gets the owner of each given element in its hierarchical element: the root (e.g. the Curtain Wall, Stair or Railing of a frame, tread or post) or the immediate parent. Also returns whether the given element is a main element, a subelement or not part of a hierarchical element. Parameters: elements, ownerMode.
- **EditHierarchicalElement** (since 1.8.0): Opens the given hierarchical element (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column) in its hierarchical 3D editing mode, as the Edit button of the element does. Fails when Archicad is already in an editing mode. Limitation: while the editing mode is open, Archicad refuses every JSON command, this add-on's included, with error 4001 (ongoing user input), FinishHierarchicalEditing included, so the mode can only be left in Archicad, with the button of its edit mode palette (reported for Archicad 29). Requires Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: elementId.
- **FinishHierarchicalEditing** (since 1.8.0): Finishes the current hierarchical editing mode (Curtain Wall, Stair, Railing, Beam or Column): accept true keeps the changes (OK), accept false discards them (Cancel). The accept parameter is required, so changes are never discarded silently. Fails when Archicad is not in such an editing mode. Limitation: while an editing mode is open, Archicad refuses JSON commands with error 4001 (ongoing user input) before they run, so this command cannot leave a mode opened by EditHierarchicalElement or in Archicad (reported for Archicad 29); leave it in Archicad instead. Requires Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: accept.
- **GetConnectedElements** (since 1.1.4): Gets the elements hosted by (connected to) the given owner elements, filtered to the given element type: for example the Windows or Doors of a Wall, the frames, panels, junctions and accessories of a Curtain Wall, the risers, treads and structures of a Stair, or the posts, rails and panels of a Railing. Parameters: elements, connectedElementType.
- **GetElementsInDrawOrder** (since 1.7.3): Returns the identifier of every element of the current database, or of the given databases, in Archicad's drawing order (the order set by Bring to Front and Send to Back), as ACAPI_DrawOrder_DrawOrderGetNext walks it. Use the optional elementType and filters parameters for filtering. Objects that belong to another element (zone stamps, the parts of stairs and railings) are left out unless the IncludeSubElemObjects filter is given. Parameters: elementType, filters, databases.
- **GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Returns the 2D drawing primitives (points, lines, arcs, texts, polylines, triangles, polygons, pictures) Archicad draws each given floor plan element from, in drawing order, as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrimsExt decomposes it on every story and unclipped. Control items (type Ctrl_*) mark the beginning and the end of sub-parts such as hatches and texts. Texts are returned without their content and polylines without their vertices. A Ctrl_ElementRef item names the element it refers to: the drawing of a Wall ends with one for each Window and Door in it, while Windows and Doors give no primitives of their own. The floor plan must be the current database. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetStoryControlPrimitives** (since 1.8.0): Returns the 2D drawing primitives of the story levels (story lines and their markers) drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation database, as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_DrawStoryControl draws them, in the same format as GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements. The databaseId can be obtained with GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId. Parameters: databaseId.
- **GetShapePrimitivesOfElements** (since 2.0.0): Returns the 2D drawing primitives of each given floor plan element in the same format as GetDrawingPrimitivesOfElements, but drawn as ACAPI_DrawingPrimitive_ShapePrims draws it by default (on the current story, clipped as Archicad clips it) instead of on every story and unclipped. With includeMarkers the objects attached to the elements (window and door markers, drawing titles, ...) are drawn with them or left out; Archicad's setting is changed back afterwards. An element on another story gets an error item. The floor plan must be the current database. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements, includeMarkers.
- **GetSectionElements** (since 1.5.8): Gets the elements drawn in the given section, elevation or interior elevation databases, each with the owner element it was generated from. This is the only command that returns raw section element identifiers - every other listing command converts them to their owner - so it is the way to obtain the sectionElementId that CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection requires. Parameters: databases.
- **GetRelationsOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Gets the type-specific relations of the given elements: endpoint and reference line connections of walls, beams and beam segments, boundary elements and boundary sections of zones, the zones on the two sides of windows, doors, skylights and curtain wall panels, and the zones connected to roofs and shells. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: elements, otherElementType.
- **LinkElements** (since 1.7.3): Creates persistent links between pairs of elements, each from one element to another, with an optional integer flags value per link. Scripts can record their own relations between elements this way (for example which label documents which column) instead of storing GUIDs in properties. The links are stored in the project and have no effect on geometry; they are independent from groups, hotlinks and solid element operations. A link is directional: it is returned by GetLinksOfElements for the element it starts from only, and removed by UnlinkElements. Undoable. Parameters: links.
- **UnlinkElements** (since 1.7.3): Removes the links created by LinkElements between the given pairs of elements. The direction matters: the link starting from fromElementId and pointing to toElementId is removed. Undoable. Parameters: links.
- **GetLinksOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the links created by LinkElements that start from the given elements: the linked element and the flags of each link. Links pointing to an element are not returned; query the elements they start from. Returns an error item for an element that does not exist. Parameters: elements.
- **GetZoneBoundaries** (since 1.2.3): Gets the boundaries of the given Zones (connected elements, neighbour zones, etc.). Accepts either a single zoneElementId or a list of zones. Prefer the list: the expensive boundary recalculation runs once per call, so querying many Zones in one call is much faster than calling the command once per Zone. Parameters: zoneElementId, zones.
- **GetZoneReductions** (since 1.7.3): Gets the area reductions of the given Zones, as the Zone Stamp's area calculation uses them: the polygons of the Zone covered by Walls, Columns, reducing Fills, sloping Roofs and low ceilings, each with its type, the percentage it is reduced by, its area and its outline with holes. Area calculations by local standards need these parts, which GetQuantitiesOfElements only gives as totals. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetPropertyObjectsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the property objects of the given elements: the library parts of the old listing system (used by projects migrated from older Archicad versions) linked to each element by criteria or individually, with the library part's index (the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts), name and guid. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetDescriptorsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the descriptors of the given elements: the listing descriptors in the property objects of each element, with the library part that declares them (index, name and guid), their listing database set and index, and their status (Normal, Deleted or Local). The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets how property objects (the library parts of the old listing system) are linked to the given elements, or to the element defaults of the given element types: whether the property objects matching their criteria are linked, which of them match, and which one is assigned individually, each with the library part's index (the same as the index returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts), name and guid. The output is aligned with the input array of elements. Parameters: elements.
- **SetLinkedPropertyObjectsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Sets how property objects (the library parts of the old listing system) are linked to the given elements, or to the element defaults of the given element types: whether the property objects matching their criteria are linked, and which one is assigned individually (0 removes the individual assignment). A link that is not given stays unchanged. All changes are made in one undoable step. Parameters: elementsWithLinkedPropertyObjects.
- **UpdateZones** (since 1.5.4): Updates Zones (recalculates their geometry, updates their Zone Stamps and the connected elements): the selected Zones, every Zone when nothing is selected, or the Zones given in zones. Archicad runs the update right after the command has returned, on the Zones selected at that moment, so the new geometry can only be read with a later command. Parameters: keepStampPosition, undoTopTrim, undoBottomTrim, zones.
- **SetZoneLabelingSettings** (since 1.7.3): Turns the automatic labeling of Zones on or off and selects the Label Favorite it places. Only the given settings are changed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: automaticLabeling, favoriteName.
- **GetZoneLabelingSettings** (since 1.8.0): Returns whether the automatic labeling of Zones is on and the name of the Label Favorite it places. Available from Archicad 28.
- **GetCollisions** (since 1.2.2): Detect collisions between the given two groups of elements. Parameters: elementsGroup1, elementsGroup2, settings.
- **HighlightElements** (since 1.0.3): Highlights the elements given in the elements array. In case of empty elements array removes all previously set highlights. On Archicad 25 nonHighlightedColor is ignored. Parameters: elements, highlightedColors, wireframe3D, nonHighlightedColor.
- **MoveElements** (since 1.0.2): Moves elements with a given vector. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently. Parameters: elementsWithMoveVectors.
- **AlignElements** (since 2.0.0): Aligns elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view to one edge of their plan bounding boxes (left, right, top or bottom) or to their middle (centerX, centerY), either of the whole set or of a reference element, by moving them in one undo step. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still aligned. Parameters: elements, alignTo, reference.
- **DistributeElements** (since 2.0.0): Distributes 3 or more elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view evenly along X (horizontal) or Y (vertical), with equal distances between the middles of their plan bounding boxes (centers) or equal space between the boxes (gaps), by moving them in one undo step. The elements are taken in the order of their middles along the direction, and the two outermost stay where they are. The bounding boxes are those Get2DBoundingBoxes returns. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Shell, Morph, Mesh, Zone, Object, Lamp, Stair, Railing, CurtainWall, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch, Text and Hotspot. An element of another type (doors, windows and openings, which only slide along their host, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still distributed. Parameters: elements, direction, mode.
- **SplitElements** (since 2.0.0): Splits each given element along a line (the infinite line through its begin and end point, like Archicad's Split command). The original element keeps one part, copies of it (Drag a Copy, so they keep the layer, classifications, properties and every other setting) get the others; all are returned, the original first. Supports straight walls without doors, windows or openings, straight unslanted single segment beams without holes or openings, and lines (their arrows stay at the original ends), which are split in two, the original keeping the part from its begin point; and slabs, meshes without level lines or points, fills and single contour polylines, whose polygon (holes and arcs included) or points are cut along the line into one part per piece, the original keeping the largest piece (a polyline: the piece with its begin point). Slab edges keep their trim and side surface, the edges along the line are vertical; the corners a mesh gets on the line take their height from the edge they lie on. An element the line does not cross is reported as notCut, an unsupported one as an error naming its type. One undo step. Parameters: elements, line.
- **CopyElementsToDatabase** (since 2.0.0): Copies 2D elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, hotspots, texts, hatches, independent labels) from one database into another, e.g. from a worksheet into another worksheet, a detail or a layout, optionally moved by an offset. Returns the new elements in the order of the given ones. Parameters: elements, sourceDatabaseId, targetDatabaseId, offset.
- **ElevateElements** (since 2.0.0): Moves elements vertically by a given offset in meters, like Edit > Move > Elevate. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently. Parameters: elementsWithElevations.
- **RotateElements** (since 1.5.3): Rotates elements around a reference point. An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently. Parameters: elementsWithRotations.
- **MirrorElements** (since 1.7.3): Mirrors elements across an axis given by two points on the floor plan, optionally as a copy.
