An element that cannot be edited (its layer is hidden or locked, it is locked, or it is not available in teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming the reason instead of being skipped silently. Parameters: elementsWithMirrorAxes.
- **CopyElements** (since 2.0.0): Copies elements by an offset, like dragging a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is moved by n times the offset, which makes a linear array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy (a part of a curtain wall, stair or railing, a locked element or one on a hidden or locked layer, ...) gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step. Parameters: elements, offset, count.
- **RotateCopyElements** (since 2.0.0): Copies elements rotated around a center on the floor plan by an angle in radians, like rotating a copy in Archicad, keeping all their settings. With count, copy n is rotated by n times the angle, which makes a circular array. Returns the new elements of each given element, in the order of the given ones; an element Archicad cannot copy gets an error naming the reason, and the other elements are still copied. All copies are one undo step. Parameters: elements, center, angle, count.
- **ScaleElements** (since 2.0.0): Scales elements on the floor plan or in the current 2D view by a factor around a center point with Archicad's Resize edit, in one undo step. Resize scales X and Y by the same ratio, so factorY, if given, must equal factor. Supported types: Wall, Column, Beam, Slab, Roof, Mesh, Zone, Line, PolyLine, Arc, Circle, Spline, Hatch and Hotspot. An element of another type (library parts such as objects, lamps, doors and windows, stairs, railings, curtain walls, shells, morphs, texts, subelements, dimensions, labels, ...) or one that cannot be edited gets a failed execution result naming the reason, and the other elements are still scaled. Parameters: elements, center, factor, factorY.
- **DeleteElements** (since 1.2.1): Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) or a guid that is not in the project gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently, and does not stop the other elements from being deleted. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before deleting gets wouldDelete, so a script can preview a deletion before making it. Parameters: elements, dryRun.
- **DeleteSelectedElements** (since 1.7.3): Deletes the currently selected elements in one undo step, the same as pressing the Delete key. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true and lists the selected elements, with wouldDelete when there is at least one, or fails when one of them cannot be edited (Archicad then deletes none of them). Parameters: dryRun.
- **LockElements** (since 1.5.2): Locks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork! Parameters: elements.
- **UnlockElements** (since 1.5.2): Unlocks the given elements. Manual lock, not teamwork! Parameters: elements.
- **RefreshElements** (since 1.8.0): Refreshes (rebuilds) the given elements, for example placed Objects, Windows and Doors that still show the old geometry after their library part's script or embedded file changed. Set force to true to run the parameter script of GDL-based elements too. The elements are looked up in the current database (floor plan, section or detail window). Returns an execution result for each input element. The refresh cannot be undone. Parameters: elements, force.
- **GetGDLParametersOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Gets all the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **SetGDLParametersOfElements** (since 1.5.7): Sets the given GDL parameters of the given elements. An element Archicad does not let the user edit (its layer locked, the element locked, or not reserved by the user in Teamwork) gets a failed execution result naming that reason, whatever the parameter. On a Curtain Wall Frame, A, B, ac_frameWidth and ac_frameDepth mirror the frame's contour, which Archicad derives from the frame's settings, so they are rejected instead of reporting a change that does not take effect; a frame without a library part (an invisible Boundary frame, for example) has no GDL parameters. The parameters are read back after the change, and a written parameter Archicad did not keep (e.g. one it sets from the element's own settings, like AC_TextSize_1 of a label) gives a failed execution result naming it. With dryRun true no element is changed and no undo step is created: the parameters are written to the element's parameter list and its Parameter Script runs as in a real run, the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that passes the checks made before changing it gets wouldChange, listing the parameters a real run would change (the given ones and the ones the Parameter Script changes with them) with their old and new values. Parameters: elementsWithGDLParameters, dryRun.
- **GetMarkerParametersOfElements** (since 1.7.1): Gets the marker library part and the marker's GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Window and Door elements. The marker is the stamp drawn next to the opening on the floor plan; its parameters are separate from the opening's own GDL parameters, which GetGDLParametersOfElements returns. Parameters: elements.
- **SetMarkerParametersOfElements** (since 1.7.1): Sets the given GDL parameters of the marker of the given Window and Door elements. The opening's own settings and the other marker parameters are left as they are. Parameters: elementsWithMarkerParameters.
- **GetURLReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. An element without a link gets the error APIERR_NOUSERDATA. Parameters: elements.
- **SetURLReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Sets the web link (URL reference) of the given elements: a URL with a description, shown in Archicad in the element's settings under Element Information > Link. Fails with APIERR_MOREUSER for an element that already holds a link. Parameters: elementsWithURLReferences.
- **ChangeLibraryPartOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Changes the library part of the given Object, Lamp, Window, Door, Skylight, Zone and symbol Label elements to another library part of the same type, given by name, index or guid, e.g. to replace missing library parts with ones from the loaded libraries. The elements themselves (guid, properties, classifications) are kept. Components of stairs and railings are not supported, even when they are reported as Objects. Optionally keeps the values of the GDL parameters with the same name and type, and the size (A and B). Parameters: elementsWithLibraryPart.
- **GetCalculatedParametersOfCurtainWallSubElements** (since 2.0.0): Gets the GDL parameters (name, type, value) of the given Curtain Wall Frame, Panel, Junction and Accessory elements as Archicad calculated them for their place in the curtain wall. GetGDLParametersOfElements returns the parameters the sub-element was set up with instead. Parameters: elements.
- **GetHotspotsOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Gets the 2D hotspots of the given library part instances (Objects, Lamps, Windows, Doors, Skylights, Zones, Curtain Wall parts, etc.), e.g. to dimension to them. Parameters: elements.
- **SetMarkerLibraryPartOfElements** (since 2.0.0): Changes which library part the marker of the given Window and Door elements uses, given by its name (find the available ones with GetAvailableLibraryParts); only a marker library part for the opening's type is accepted. The marker gets the new library part's default parameters, which SetMarkerParametersOfElements can change afterwards; the opening's own settings are left as they are. Parameters: elementsWithMarkerLibraryPart.
- **RunParameterScriptOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Runs the parameter script of the library part of the given elements (objects, lamps, windows, doors, etc.), so that parameter values that depend on other parameters are updated, e.g. after SetGDLParametersOfElements. Parameters: elements.
- **CreateColumns** (since 1.0.3): Creates Column elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill as ModifyColumns, besides the position, size, slant, cross section and veneer; settings not given come from the Column tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surfaces of the column segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27. Parameters: columnsData.
- **CreateWalls** (since 1.4.0): Creates Wall elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same wall settings as ModifyWalls, applied by the same code, except geometryType and profileType, which the new wall takes from the favorite or the Wall tool defaults (its plan outline is always Straight), and bottomOffset, which comes from zCoordinate. Neither command can write a Polygonal outline (it needs an outline polygon, which these commands do not take), connectionPriority or junctionSequence (Archicad ignores writes to them; GetDetailsOfElements reads them), and on Archicad 29 any story visibility other than 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories'. Parameters: wallsData.
- **CreateBeams** (since 1.4.0): Creates Beam elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill as ModifyBeams, besides the position, shape, slant and cross section; settings not given come from the Beam tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surfaces of the beam segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27. Parameters: beamsData.
- **CreateStairs** (since 1.5.0): Creates Stair elements based on the given baseline and parameters, optionally with the segment type of each baseline edge and the turn at each baseline point (landings and winders). Accepts the same settings as ModifyStairs: the step values with their locks, the finish and structure visibility, the extra treads, the walking line, the numbering, the walking direction, and the tread, riser and structure settings of the flights and the landings; settings not given come from the Stair tool defaults or the favorite. Parameters: stairsData.
- **SolveStairBaseline** (since 1.7.3): Runs the Archicad stair solver on the given Stair baselines and parameters without creating any element. Returns for each one whether the baseline was already correct, could be solved or could not be solved, with the baseline and the main stair settings after solving. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: stairsData.
- **CreateSlabs** (since 1.0.3): Creates Slab elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same surfaces (top, side, bottom), cut fill pens and floor fill as ModifySlabs, besides the outline, holes, level and structure; settings not given come from the Slab tool defaults or the favorite. Not written by either command: the surface of a single edge, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27; of the floor fill orientation Archicad applies only the type through the API. Parameters: slabsData.
- **CreateWindows** (since 1.4.0): Creates Window elements in host walls based on the given parameters. Parameters: windowsData.
- **CreateDoors** (since 1.4.0): Creates Door elements in host walls based on the given parameters. Parameters: doorsData.
- **CreateOpenings** (since 1.4.0): Creates Opening elements in the given host elements. Parameters: openingsData.
- **GetOpeningDefault** (since 1.7.3): Returns the settings of the Opening tool defaults: the extrusion parameters (as GetOpeningDetails returns them) and the floor plan parameters (as GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters returns them). Available from Archicad 29.
- **SetOpeningDefault** (since 1.8.0): Changes the settings of the Opening tool defaults, with the names GetOpeningDefault returns. Only the given settings change. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: extrusionParameters, floorPlanParameters.
- **PlaceOpenings** (since 1.8.0): Places openings with the Opening tool settings at points of their parent elements. A point off the parent element's surface is moved to the closest point of the surface. Each opening can be given its own extrusion and floor plan settings, which change only that opening and not the tool's settings. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: openingsData.
- **GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters** (since 1.7.3): Returns the floor plan parameters of Opening elements: the floor plan display mode, the divided opening mode, the open edge style, the reference axis, the cut surface and outline lines, the cover fills and the cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **SetOpeningFloorPlanParameters** (since 1.7.3): Changes the floor plan parameters of Opening elements returned by GetOpeningFloorPlanParameters, and sets or removes their cut and uncut symbols. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: openingsWithFloorPlanParameters.
- **GetOpeningSymbolParameters** (since 1.8.0): Returns the GDL parameters of the cut and uncut floor plan symbols of Opening elements, in the format of GetGDLParametersOfElements. A symbol the opening does not have is left out. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **SetOpeningSymbolParameters** (since 1.8.0): Changes the GDL parameters of the cut and uncut floor plan symbols of Opening elements, in the format of SetGDLParametersOfElements. Only the given parameters are changed. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **GetOpeningDetails** (since 1.7.3): Returns the details of Opening elements: whether they exist, the parent element, the cut and connected elements, the geometry (anchor point, extrusion direction, axes, polygon) and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides). Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **SetOpeningDetails** (since 1.7.3): Changes the details of Opening elements: the parent element, the cut elements, the polygon, a transformation of the geometry and the extrusion parameters (constraint, limit type, linked status, shape type, size, anchor, offsets, surface overrides) returned by GetOpeningDetails. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: openingsWithDetails.
- **CreateMorphs** (since 1.4.0): Creates Morph elements from simple box definitions or arbitrary bodies. Each item may name a favorite (favoriteName) to start from, a layer (layerIndex) and an Element ID (id); the given geometry and floor are kept. Parameters: morphsData.
- **CreateRoofs** (since 1.4.0): Creates Roof elements based on footprint, level and roof profile data. Creates a multi-plane roof by default; pass 'pivotLine' (and optionally 'angle') to create a single-plane roof instead. Parameters: roofsData.
- **CreateShells** (since 2.0.0): Creates extruded, revolved and ruled Shell elements from profile polylines, with thickness, structure, an optional clipping contour and holes. Parameters: shellsData.
- **CreateSkylights** (since 2.0.0): Creates Skylight elements with a roof or shell owner and a floor plan anchor position. It takes the same settings as ModifySkylights (anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display, pens, line types, section fill, surface and the library part flags) and optionally a library part; the settings not given come from the Skylight tool defaults or a favorite. Surface placement is handled by Archicad and has not yet been verified for this command. Parameters: skylightsData.
- **ModifySkylights** (since 2.0.0): Modifies Skylight elements: anchor position and anchor point, fix mode, width, height, azimuth and elevation angles, mirroring, floor plan display option, pens, line types, section fill and pens, surface and the use-the-library-part's-settings flags - the same settings CreateSkylights takes and GetDetailsOfElements returns. Only the given settings change. Not written by this command: the owner roof or shell, the anchor level and the vertical link (Archicad places the skylight on its owner), the plane of a multi-plane roof it sits on, the dimension marker (a separate element) and the library part's own parameters (use SetGDLParametersOfElements). Archicad may set the elevation angle again from the owner. Parameters: skylightsWithDetails.
- **CreateRailings** (since 1.8.0): Creates Railing elements along a reference polyline. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite, from an existing railing (templateElementId) or from the Railing tool defaults; Archicad generates one node per vertex and one segment per pair of consecutive vertices. Parameters: railingsData.
- **CreateRailingsFromPolyline** (since 2.0.0): Creates Railing elements along a 3D reference polyline: each node has its own elevation and segments can be arcs. Posts, rails, handrails, toprails, panels and balusters come from the favorite or from the Railing tool defaults. Parameters: railingsData.
- **CreateCurtainWalls** (since 1.7.2): Creates Curtain Wall elements along a reference polyline with a column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern. The frame and panel classes come from the favorite or from the Curtain Wall tool defaults; the pattern cells can assign them to the grid. Parameters: curtainWallsData.
- **CreateAssociativeDimensions** (since 1.4.0): Creates associative dimensions from explicit witness point references: linear by default, or cumulative, baseline or elevation dimensions (appearance). A witness point can also be static, given by its coordinate instead of an element. Parameters: dimensionsData.
- **CreateAssociativeDimensionsOnSection** (since 1.4.0): Creates associative dimensions on section elements using common wall, slab, beam, column, door and window presets: linear by default, or cumulative, baseline or elevation dimensions (appearance), e.g. level marks. The preset points of multiple section elements can be merged into one continuous dimension chain via sectionElementIds. For Opening tool elements, which Archicad does not associate with dimensions, the OpeningEdges preset places fixed points at their edges instead. Parameters: dimensionsData.
- **CreateWallThicknessDimensions** (since 1.4.0): Creates associative wall thickness dimensions for the given walls. Parameters: dimensionsData.
- **ModifyAssociativeDimensions** (since 2.0.0): Changes the settings of existing linear dimensions (the Dimension tool's elements, also in sections): the dimension type, the elevation origin, the line pen, the marker type and pen, the text height, pen and frame and the witness line form and value, with the same keys as the dimension creation commands. The text and witness line settings are applied to every witness point. Not written: the witness points, the dimension line position and direction (use MoveElements), the marker size, the text content and position, the witness extension line, the layout and the hole and composite wall dimensioning settings. Parameters: dimensionsWithDetails.
- **GetDimensionData** (since 1.5.0): Gets the data of existing dimension chains: the line pen, the marker type and pen and the default witness line, and per witness point the coordinates, measured value, witness line and the text height, pen and frame. Parameters: elements.
- **GetOpeningTransformations** (since 1.7.3): Gets the placement of Opening elements, Windows, Doors and Skylights without changing them: a global-to-local transformation matrix, its inverse, and the origin and axes in world coordinates derived from the inverse. For Windows, Doors and Skylights the local-to-global matrix is the one Archicad returns, and mirrored ones give a left-handed matrix (isMirrored). For Opening elements it is built from the opening geometry (Archicad 29 and later): origin at the anchor point, the X and Y axes of the opening and Z = X × Y, which points against the extrusion direction. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: elements.
- **CreateZones** (since 1.1.8): Creates Zone elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same zone settings as ModifyZones (name, number, category, zone stamp, levels, contour line and cover fill), applied by the same helpers; the polygon or reference point is only set here. An item whose area would overlap an existing Zone on the same story fails with an error naming that Zone instead of opening Archicad's modal overlap warning, unless its allowOverlap is true. Parameters: zonesData.
- **CreatePolylines** (since 1.1.5): Creates Polyline elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: polylinesData, databaseId.
- **CreateLineElements** (since 1.5.6): Creates Line elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: linesData, databaseId.
- **CreateArcs** (since 1.5.6): Creates Arc elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: arcsData, databaseId.
- **CreateCircles** (since 1.5.6): Creates Circle elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: circlesData, databaseId.
- **CreateHotspots** (since 1.5.6): Creates Hotspot elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: hotspotsData, databaseId.
- **CreateHatches** (since 1.5.6): Creates Hatch elements based on the given parameters. A hatch can have holes, in the same format SetDetailsOfElements accepts for hatches. Parameters: hatchesData, databaseId.
- **CreateSplines** (since 1.5.6): Creates Spline elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: splinesData, databaseId.
- **CreateObjects** (since 1.5.7): Creates Object elements based on the given parameters. A library part named in libraryPartName starts from its own default size and GDL parameters, not from those of the part the Object tool holds; the dimensions and the GDL parameters given (by name, in parameters) override them. layerIndex places the element on a layer. With databaseId the objects are placed in that database, e.g. a worksheet, instead of the current one. Parameters: objectsData, databaseId.
- **CreateLamps** (since 1.5.7): Creates Lamp elements based on the given parameters. A library part named in libraryPartName starts from its own default size and GDL parameters, not from those of the part the Lamp tool holds; the dimensions and the GDL parameters given (by name, in parameters) override them. layerIndex places the element on a layer. With databaseId the lamps are placed in that database, e.g. a worksheet, instead of the current one. Parameters: lampsData, databaseId.
- **GetGridElementDefaults** (since 1.7.2): Returns the Grid Tool defaults: library part, size and GDL parameters of a new grid element. Needs Archicad 26 or later.
- **GetGridElements** (since 1.7.2): Lists the grid elements (placed with the Grid Tool or created by CreateGridElements) with their position, angle, size, library part and optionally GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later. Parameters: includeParameters.
- **CreateGridElements** (since 1.7.2): Creates grid elements, the elements the Grid Tool places, from begin and end coordinates, with optional story, layer and GDL parameters. Needs Archicad 26 or later. Parameters: gridElements.
- **CreateMeshes** (since 1.1.9): Creates Mesh elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: meshesData.
- **CreateLabels** (since 1.2.5): Creates Label elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: labelsData, databaseId.
- **CreateTexts** (since 1.5.0): Creates standalone Text elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: textsData, databaseId.
- **CreateLevelDimensions** (since 1.7.2): Creates Level Dimension elements (the Level Dimension tool) based on the given parameters. With a parentElementId the dimension is associative: it shows the height of the parent element (Mesh, Slab, Roof ...) at its position and follows the element when it changes. Parameters: levelDimensionsData.
- **ModifyLevelDimensions** (since 2.0.0): Changes existing Level Dimension elements: the position of the marker and the settings CreateLevelDimensions takes (pen, text height and pen, marker type and size, plus sign, angle, origin), with the same keys. Not written: the parent element and the static level (delete and recreate the dimension to change them), the text content and the hide-with-base-element setting. Parameters: levelDimensionsWithDetails.
- **ModifyWalls** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Wall elements based on the given parameters. Takes the same wall settings as CreateWalls, applied by the same code, plus geometryType (Straight or Trapezoid), profileType and bottomOffset. Neither command can write a Polygonal outline (it needs an outline polygon, which these commands do not take), connectionPriority or junctionSequence (Archicad ignores writes to them; GetDetailsOfElements reads them), and on Archicad 29 any story visibility other than 'Home story only' and 'All relevant stories'. Parameters: wallsWithDetails.
- **ModifyBeams** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Beam elements based on the given parameters. CreateBeams takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill, and the same absolute zCoordinate of the reference line (with an optional floorIndex). Not written: the surfaces of the beam segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27. Parameters: beamsWithDetails.
- **ModifySlabs** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Slab elements based on the given parameters. CreateSlabs takes the same surfaces, cut fill pens and floor fill. Not written: the surface of a single edge, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27. Of the cover fill orientation, Archicad applies only the type to a Slab through the API; a given origin or distortion matrix that did not stick gets a failed execution result, while the other details are applied. Parameters: slabsWithDetails.
- **ModifyColumns** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Column elements based on the given parameters. CreateColumns takes the same cut fill pens and cover fill. Not written: the surfaces of the column segments, and the cut fill pens before Archicad 27. Parameters: columnsWithDetails.
- **ModifyWindows** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Window elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: windowsWithDetails.
- **ModifyDoors** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Door elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: doorsWithDetails.
- **ModifyOpenings** (since 2.0.0): Modifies Opening elements: the width, the height and the base point CreateOpenings takes. Needs Archicad 28 or earlier; in Archicad 29 and later every item fails with a message pointing to SetOpeningDetails, which changes the size and the position of an opening there. Parameters: openingsWithDetails.
- **ModifyMorphs** (since 1.4.0): Modifies Morph elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: morphsWithDetails.
- **ModifyRoofs** (since 1.4.0): Modifies single-plane and multi-plane Roof elements based on the given parameters. The plan outline, level, thickness and structure apply to both; angle, pivotLine and edgeTrims (the cut of each polygon edge) only to single-plane roofs; levels, eavesOverhang and pivotEdges only to multi-plane roofs. Parameters: roofsWithDetails.
- **ModifyShells** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the structure (Basic or Composite, building material or composite) of Shell elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: shellsWithDetails.
- **ModifyMeshes** (since 1.5.4): Modifies the attributes of Mesh elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: meshesData.
- **ModifyRailings** (since 2.0.0): Modifies Railing elements in place: the height of their segments, the bottom offset and the home story. The reference line, the nodes and segments, and the posts, rails and panels stay as they are. Each railing is read back after the change, and a value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result. Parameters: railingsWithDetails.
- **ModifyObjects** (since 1.5.7): Modifies Object elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: objectsWithDetails.
- **ModifyLamps** (since 1.5.7): Modifies Lamp elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: lampsWithDetails.
- **ModifyTexts** (since 1.5.9): Modifies standalone Text elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: textsWithDetails.
- **ModifyLabels** (since 1.5.9): Modifies Label elements based on the given parameters. Parameters: labelsWithDetails.
- **ModifyCurtainWalls** (since 1.8.0): Modifies Curtain Wall elements in place, keeping their GUID, properties and classifications: the height, the bottom elevation and story, the reference line (with the same number of segments), and the column (primary) and row (secondary) pattern with its cell assignments, in the fields of CreateCurtainWalls. Parameters: curtainWallsWithDetails.
- **ModifyCurtainWallFrames** (since 2.0.0): EXPERIMENTAL. Modifies single Curtain Wall Frames by their GUID: the frame contour (a1, a2, b1, b2), the frame class and the frame type. ACAPI_Element_Change does not take a frame on its own, so the change is written through the memo of the owner curtain wall, and read back to check that Archicad applied it. Parameters: framesWithDetails.
- **ModifyStairs** (since 2.0.0): Modifies Stair elements in place, keeping their baseline and position: the flight width, total height, number of steps, riser height and going with their locks, the finish and structure visibility, the extra top and bottom treads, the walking line position and offset, the step numbering, the walking direction, the uniform finish, monolith and draining settings, and for the flights and the landings the tread and riser settings (presence, thickness, offset, nosing, riser cross section and position) and the structure of each side (presence, type, underside shape and thickness). CreateStairs accepts the same settings. Only the given settings are changed. Archicad solves the stair again within its baseline, so it may adjust the step values; read them back with GetDetailsOfElements. Not written by this command: the baseline with its landings and winders, the top link, the floor plan display (symbol and marker layout), the headroom and the stair rules; the subelements (treads, risers, structures) take the per-part settings above and cannot be written one by one through the API. Parameters: stairsWithDetails.
- **ChangeTextContent** (since 1.8.0): Replaces a range of the content of Text elements and text Labels, keeping the styles of the runs and the autotexts in the rest of the content. Parameters: contentChanges.
- **ModifyZones** (since 1.8.0): Modifies Zone elements: name, number, category, zone stamp, height, base offset, top link, floor thickness, contour line and cover fill - the same settings as CreateZones, applied by the same helpers. Only the given fields are changed. The polygon of a manual zone cannot be changed here (the change takes no polygon memo), nor the reference point of an automatic one (SetDetailsOfElements moves it). Parameters: zonesWithDetails.
- **MeasureTexts** (since 1.7.3): Measures texts before placing them: the length of every line for a given font, style and height, on paper in millimetres or in the model at the current drawing scale, and the font's capital size factor. Creates nothing. Parameters: texts.
- **GetElementPreviewImage** (since 1.2.7): Returns the preview image of the given element. Parameters: elementId, imageType, format, width, height.
- **GetRoomImage** (since 1.2.7): Returns the room image of the given zone. Parameters: zoneId, format, width, height, offset, scale, backgroundColor.
- **GetModelExtent** (since 2.0.0): Returns the 3D extent (xMin, yMin, zMin, xMax, yMax, zMax) of the current database, the region Archicad's Fit in Window would show.
- **SetElementNotificationClient** (since 1.2.8): Sets up a new notification client to receive element events. Parameters: host, port, notifyOnNewElement, notifyOnModificationOfAnElement, elementTypesToObserve, notifyOnReservationChanges, notifyOnSelectionChange, notifyOnWindowChange, notifyOnProjectEvents, notifyOnAttributeReplacement, notifyOnToolChange, notifyOnViewEvents, notifyOnLockableReservationChanges, notifyOnToolDefaultChanges, notifyOnAttributeChanges, notifyOnClassificationChanges, notifyOnPropertyDefinitionChanges, notifyOnMarqueeChange, notifyOn3DSettingsChanges.
- **RemoveElementNotificationClient** (since 1.2.8): Removes an element notification client. Parameters: host, port.
- **RegularizePolygons** (since 1.7.3): Regularizes polygons with Archicad's own polygon regularization, before they are used to create slabs, zones or fills: removes duplicate points, fixes the orientation, resolves self-intersections and touching holes. Each input polygon gives 0, 1 or more valid polygons in the format of CreateSlabs, optionally with the input vertex and edge each result vertex and edge came from. Changes nothing in the project. Parameters: polygons, withAncestry.
- **RegularizePolylines** (since 1.7.3): Regularizes polylines with Archicad's own polyline regularization: removes repeated consecutive points. The result is in the format of CreatePolylines and may be empty, optionally with the input point and segment each result point and segment came from. Changes nothing in the project. Parameters: polylines, withAncestry.
- **GetSplineMaxDistances** (since 2.0.0): Measures how far the given 2D coordinates are from a segment of a Spline element, between two of its fit points, with its own Bezier handles: returns the largest distance, for example to check how well a polyline follows the spline. The output is aligned with the input array. Changes nothing in the project. Parameters: splines.

## Element grouping Commands

- **CreateGroups** (since 1.4.0): Creates groups of the passed elements Parameters: elementGroups.
- **UngroupElements** (since 1.7.3): Ungroups the given groups one level, like Edit > Grouping > Ungroup: each group is dissolved, the elements and subgroups it directly contains stay. A group nested in another group is reported as failed; ungroup the containing group first. Returns an execution result per group. Parameters: groups.
- **GetGroupsOfElements** (since 1.5.6): Gets the identifier of the group that directly contains each given element. Returns an error for elements that are not part of any group. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElementsOfGroups** (since 1.5.6): Gets the elements directly contained by each given group. Parameters: groups.
- **GetMainGroups** (since 1.8.0): Gets the top level group of each given group. A group that is not nested in another group is its own top level group. Parameters: groups.
- **GetAllElementsOfGroups** (since 1.8.0): Gets all the elements of each given group, including the elements of its nested groups. Parameters: groups.
- **GetAutoGroupMode** (since 1.8.0): Gets the current state of the Auto Group mode.
- **GetElementSetData** (since 1.8.0): Gets the elements and the custom data of each given element set. Element sets are created by add-ons to link elements together; the custom data is returned as Base64 encoded bytes. Parameters: elementSets.
- **GetUserDataOfGroups** (since 1.7.3): Gets the user data an add-on attached to each given group: its version, platform sign, flags and bytes (base64 encoded), and, when its version is 1 (the layout SetUserDataOfGroups writes), its key-value pairs. Returns an error for groups that have no user data. Parameters: groups.
- **SetUserDataOfGroups** (since 1.8.0): Stores string values under keys in the user data of groups, for scripts to keep their own state on a group. The given pairs are merged into what each group already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. One undo step per call. Parameters: groups, pairs, keysToDelete.
- **GetSuspendGroupsMode** (since 1.5.6): Gets the current state of the Suspend Groups mode.
- **SetSuspendGroupsMode** (since 1.5.6): Turns the Suspend Groups mode on or off. Suspend groups to perform operations on elements that are part of a group; remember to restore the previous state afterwards. Parameters: suspendGroups.
- **CreateElementSets** (since 1.8.0): Creates element sets of the given elements. An element set is a hidden, persistent collection of elements (it is not a group and has no effect on selection or editing). Parameters: elementSets.
- **DeleteElementSets** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the given element sets. The elements of a set are not deleted. Only element sets created by the Tapir Add-On can be deleted; sets created by other add-ons are reported as failed. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element set that a real run would delete gets wouldDelete. Parameters: elementSets, dryRun.
- **GetElementSetsOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Gets the element sets that contain each given element. Only element sets created by the Tapir Add-On are examined; sets created by other add-ons are not found. Parameters: elements.

## Favorites Commands

- **GetFavoritesByType** (since 1.2.2): Returns a list of the names of all favorites with the given element type Parameters: elementType.
- **GetAllFavorites** (since 1.7.3): Returns every Favorite of the project, or only those of the given element type, with its name and element type. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elementType.
- **GetFavoritePreviewImage** (since 1.2.7): Returns the preview image of the given favorite. Parameters: favorite, imageType, format, width, height.
- **GetFavoriteDetails** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classifications, property values and element category values stored in the given favorites, so they can be audited before elements are placed. Each property value comes with its evaluation status and default-value flag; the value itself is only returned when it has been evaluated. Parameters: favorites.
- **ApplyFavoritesToElementDefaults** (since 1.1.2): Apply the given favorites to element defaults. Parameters: favorites.
- **CreateFavoritesFromElements** (since 1.1.2): Create favorites from the given elements. Parameters: favoritesFromElements.
- **ImportFavorites** (since 1.5.0): Import Favorites from a .prefs file or folder into the current project. From Archicad 29 they can also be imported from a folder of Favorite files (xml format, all of them or the given fileNames) or from a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format), with the conflict policies Error, Skip, OverwriteExisting and RenameNew. In a Teamwork project the Favorites lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet). Parameters: path, format, fileNames, targetFolder, importFolders, conflictPolicy.
- **ExportFavorites** (since 1.5.0): Export the project's Favorites to a .prefs file or folder. From Archicad 29 they can also be exported to a folder of Favorite files (xml format) or to a legacy .prf file (legacyPRF format). With overwrite false an export to a single file refuses to replace an existing file. Parameters: path, names, format, overwrite.
- **ApplyFavoritesToElements** (since 1.5.4): Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves the target element. A Window or Door keeps its wall, marker and placement, and takes the Favorite's library part and parameters, size included. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes. With favorite instead of favoritesToApply, one Favorite is read once and applied to the given elements, or to every element of its type that matches the filter. Parameters: favoritesToApply, favorite, elements, filter, applySettings, applyClassifications, applyCategories, applyProperties, keepFields.
- **UpdateFavoritesFromElements** (since 1.5.4): Update existing favorites from the given elements. Parameters: favoritesFromElements.
- **RenameFavorites** (since 1.5.4): Rename existing favorites. Parameters: renames.
- **DeleteFavorites** (since 1.5.4): Delete existing favorites. Parameters: favorites.
- **GetFavoriteFolders** (since 1.8.0): Returns the folder tree of the Favorites palette from its root folder: the name and path of every folder and the names of the Favorites in it. Available from Archicad 29.
- **ReadFavoritesFile** (since 2.0.0): Read the Favorites of a .prefs file or folder without importing them, returning the name, element type and folder of each. Nothing in the project changes, so the result can be compared with the project's Favorites before ImportFavorites. Parameters: path.
- **CreateFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Creates a folder in the Favorites palette, in the parent folder given by its path. Returns the new folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: parentPath, name.
- **RenameFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Renames a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. The root folder cannot be renamed. Returns the renamed folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: path, newName.
- **DeleteFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Deletes a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. Archicad deletes the folder's Favorites and subfolders with it, so a folder that is not empty is deleted only if recursive is true. The root folder cannot be deleted. Returns the deleted folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: path, recursive.
- **GetFavoriteSettings** (since 1.7.3): Reads the stored settings of the given favorites without applying them or placing an element: the element type, the folder, the library part and GDL parameters, the marker (library part and parameters) of Window and Door favorites, and the sub-elements. A favorite without a marker has no marker field, which is not an error. The other settings of the element (pens, layer, structure, etc.) are not returned. Parameters: favorites.
- **CreateFavorite** (since 1.8.0): Creates a Favorite in the given folder from the settings of another Favorite or of the current Opening tool default. conflictPolicy says what happens when the name is taken: fail, skip, overwrite the existing Favorite's settings or create the new one under a free name. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: name, folder, source, conflictPolicy.
- **ChangeFavorite** (since 1.8.0): Gives an existing Favorite the settings of another Favorite or of the current Opening tool default. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favoriteName, source.
- **ApplyFavoriteToToolDefault** (since 1.8.0): Makes the settings of the given Favorite the settings of its tool, and returns the element type of that tool. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favoriteName.
- **MoveFavoriteFolder** (since 1.8.0): Moves a folder of the Favorites palette, with its Favorites and subfolders, into another folder. Folders are given as their path of folder names from the root. Returns the new path of the folder. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: folder, targetFolder.
- **GetFavoriteContents** (since 2.0.0): Returns the Favorites of a folder of the Favorites palette and of its subfolders (every Favorite when no folder is given), each with its folder path, classifications, element category values and property values, read through the Favorite manager. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: folderPath.
- **DeleteFavoritesWithManager** (since 2.0.0): Deletes the given Favorites through the Favorite manager, each found by name, optionally only in the given folder. One execution result for each. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favorites.
- **MoveFavorites** (since 1.8.0): Moves Favorites given by their names into a folder of the Favorites palette given by its path. Returns an execution result for each Favorite. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favorites, targetPath.
- **GetFavoriteDefaults** (since 2.0.0): Reads the element default stored in each given Favorite through the Favorite manager, without applying it or placing an element: the element type, the layer, the element ID, the folder, the library part and GDL parameters, the marker of every element type that has one, and the sub-elements with each of their kinds (Curtain Wall frames and panels, Stair treads and risers, Railing posts and rails, markers ...). Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: favorites.
- **SearchFavorites** (since 2.0.0): Searches project favorites by keyword (matching favorite name or folder) and/or element type. Parameters: query, elementType, limit.

## Property Commands

- **GetAllProperties** (since 1.1.3): Returns all user defined and built-in properties. Optionally only the given properties or property types, and without the availability lists. Parameters: properties, propertyTypes, includeAvailability.
- **SearchProperties** (since 2.0.0): Searches properties by name or group substring with optional filtering by property type, value type, and collection type. Parameters: query, propertyGroup, propertyType, valueType, collectionType, includeEnumValues, includeAvailability, limit.
- **GetPropertyValuesOfElements** (since 1.0.6): Returns the property values of the elements for the given property. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With includeAvailability it also tells whether each property is available for the element. Parameters: elements, properties, includeAvailability, useSIUnits.
- **SetPropertyValuesOfElements** (since 1.0.6): Sets the property values of elements. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With valueStatus an element's value can also be reset to the default value of the property (Default) or made undefined (UserUndefined, from 1.8.1). With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's value now (oldValue) and the value a real run would write (newValue), both as GetPropertyValuesOfElements gives them. Parameters: elementPropertyValues, dryRun.
- **GetComponentsOfElements** (since 2.0.0): Returns the components of the elements: the building material skins of composite walls, slabs, roofs and shells, and the parts of complex profile walls, beams and columns. The components have their own property values (building material, thickness, area, volume and the properties of the building material); read them with GetPropertyValuesOfElementComponents. Parameters: elements.
- **GetPropertyDefinitionsOfElementComponents** (since 2.0.0): Returns the property definitions available on the given element components, optionally filtered to user defined or built-in ones. Parameters: elementComponents, filter.
- **GetPropertyValuesOfElementComponents** (since 2.0.0): Returns the property values of the given element components for the given properties, in the shape of GetPropertyValuesOfElements. Use GetComponentsOfElements to list the components of an element. Parameters: elementComponents, properties.
- **SetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults** (since 2.0.0): Sets the property values of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of element types, so every element placed afterwards gets them, without saving and applying a favorite. Parameters: elementDefaultPropertyValues.
- **GetPropertyValuesOfAttributes** (since 1.1.8): Returns the property values of the attributes for the given property. With includeStatus it also returns whether each property is available, editable and visible for the attribute (from 1.7.3). Parameters: attributeIds, properties, includeStatus.
- **SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes** (since 1.1.8): Sets the property values of attributes. Parameters: attributePropertyValues.
- **SetBuiltInPropertyValuesOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Sets built-in property values of attributes, writing the values of each attribute together. Custom properties are refused; set them with SetPropertyValuesOfAttributes. Returns one execution result per value. Parameters: attributes.
- **SetPropertyValueOfAttributes** (since 2.0.0): Sets one property value on several attributes (for example Building Materials) in one undo step. If the property is not available for any of the given attributes, no attribute is changed. Parameters: propertyId, propertyValue, attributeIds.
- **GetPropertyDefinitionsOfAttributes** (since 1.7.3): Returns the property definitions of the given attributes (for example Building Materials): the user defined, the fundamental built-in, or all of them. Parameters: attributeIds, filter.
- **GetPropertiesOfToolDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Returns the property definitions of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types, filtered by kind (all by default), and optionally the value of each property in the tool default. Parameters: elementTypes, filter, includeValues.
- **AddPropertyToAttributes** (since 1.7.3): Makes an existing custom property available for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only. Parameters: propertyId, attributeIds.
- **RemovePropertyFromAttributes** (since 1.7.3): Makes a custom property unavailable for the given attributes (for example Building Materials), in one undo step. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 only. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and wouldDelete when the property and every attribute exist. Parameters: propertyId, attributeIds, dryRun.
- **CreatePropertyGroups** (since 1.0.7): Creates Property Groups based on the given parameters. Parameters: propertyGroups.
- **DeletePropertyGroups** (since 1.0.9): Deletes the given Custom Property Groups. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each property group that exists gets wouldDelete. Parameters: propertyGroupIds, dryRun.
- **CreatePropertyDefinitions** (since 1.0.9): Creates Custom Property Definitions based on the given parameters. Parameters: propertyDefinitions.
- **DeletePropertyDefinitions** (since 1.0.9): Deletes the given Custom Property Definitions. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each property that exists gets wouldDelete. Parameters: propertyIds, dryRun.
- **UpdatePropertyDefinitions** (since 1.5.4): Updates existing Custom Property Definitions in place, keeping their guid: name, description, group, default value or expressions, availability, and enum options (add, rename, remove, reorder). Parameters: propertyDefinitions.
- **UpdatePropertyGroups** (since 1.6.0): Updates the name and/or description of existing Custom Property Groups, keeping their guid. Parameters: propertyGroups.
- **ImportPropertiesXml** (since 1.6.0): Imports a Property Manager XML export, with the given policy for names that already exist. Returns the property definitions it created and removed. Parameters: xml, conflictPolicy.
- **GetPropertyValuesOfElementDefaults** (since 2.0.0): Returns the values of the given properties in the current tool default of an element type, which new elements of that type get. It reads the native tool default of the generic variation of the type, not a Favorite that is not applied. A property that is not available for the tool default is reported as an error. Parameters: elementType, properties.
- **ModifyPropertyValueOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Sets one property value on all the given elements in a single step. If the property is not available for any of the elements, none of them is changed. Parameters: elements, propertyId, propertyValue.
- **GetPropertyExpressionReferences** (since 2.0.0): Returns the strings that refer to the given properties in property expressions. Parameters: propertyIds.
- **CheckPropertyValues** (since 2.0.0): Checks whether the given values are acceptable for the given property definitions, without changing anything. Parameters: propertyValues.
- **GetPropertyEditability** (since 2.0.0): Tells whether the values of the given properties can be modified, and whether the properties are visible, for the given elements. Also tells whether they can be modified in the tool defaults of element types (from Archicad 26) and in the default values of the property definitions themselves. Unknown elements, element types and properties are reported as errors, not as locked properties. Parameters: properties, elements, elementTypes, propertyDefinitionDefaults.
- **GetPropertyAvailabilityOfDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the given properties are available and whether they are visible in the current tool default of an element type, before creating new elements. It checks the native tool default only, not a Favorite that is not applied. Unknown properties are reported as errors, not as unavailable. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: elementType, properties.
- **MakePropertyAvailableForElements** (since 1.7.3): Makes a property definition available for all the given elements. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27. Parameters: elements, propertyId.
- **MakePropertyUnavailableForElements** (since 1.7.3): Makes a property definition unavailable for all the given elements. Available in Archicad 25, 26 and 27. Parameters: elements, propertyId.

## Classification Commands

- **GetClassificationsOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Returns the classification of the given elements in the given classification systems. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. Parameters: elements, classificationSystemIds.
- **GetElementsByClassification** (since 1.8.0): Returns the elements classified with the given classification items, one list per item, so elements can be filtered by classification in a single call. Parameters: classificationItemIds.
- **SetClassificationsOfElements** (since 1.0.7): Sets the classifications of elements. In order to set the classification of an element to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. It works for subelements of hierarchal elements also. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each item that passes the checks made before writing gets wouldChange, with the element's classification in the system now (oldValue) and the one a real run would set (newValue). Parameters: elementClassifications, dryRun.
- **GetClassificationsOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classifications of the given attributes (building materials, composites, surfaces, etc.) in every classification system they are classified in. Parameters: attributeIds.
- **SetClassificationsOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Sets the classifications of attributes (building materials, composites, surfaces, etc.). The given item replaces the attribute's current item in the same classification system. In order to set the classification of an attribute to unclassified in a system, omit the classificationItemId field. Parameters: attributeClassifications.
- **GetClassificationOfAttributesInSystem** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classification of the given attributes (for example Building Materials) in the given classification system. classificationItemId is omitted for an unclassified attribute. Parameters: attributeIds, classificationSystemId.
- **GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults** (since 1.7.3): Returns the classification of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types in the given classification systems. Parameters: elementTypes, classificationSystemIds.
- **SetClassificationsOfElementDefaults** (since 1.7.3): Sets the classifications of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types. In order to set a default to unclassified, omit the classificationItemId field. Parameters: elementDefaultClassifications.
- **GetClassificationsOfToolDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Returns every classification of the tool defaults (the settings new elements get) of the given element types, in all classification systems at once. Unlike GetClassificationsOfElementDefaults it needs no list of classification systems; systems in which a default is unclassified are left out. Parameters: elementTypes.
- **GetAllClassificationSystems** (since 1.8.0): Returns the classification systems of the project with their guid, name, description, source, version and date. Same output as the official GetAllClassificationSystems command, so scripts can rely on Tapir commands only.
- **CreateClassificationSystems** (since 1.5.0): Creates Classification Systems including Classification Items based on the given parameters. Parameters: classificationSystemsWithItems.
- **CreateClassificationItems** (since 1.5.0): Creates Classification Items in the given Classification Systems based on the given parameters. Parameters: newClassificationItems.
- **DeleteClassificationSystems** (since 1.5.2): Deletes the given Classification Systems. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each classification system that exists gets wouldDelete. Parameters: classificationSystemIds, dryRun.
- **DeleteClassificationItems** (since 1.5.2): Deletes the given Classification Items. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each classification item that exists gets wouldDelete. Parameters: classificationItemIds, dryRun.
- **UpdateClassificationSystems** (since 1.6.0): Updates the name, description, source, version and/or date of existing Classification Systems, keeping their guid. Parameters: classificationSystems.
- **UpdateClassificationItems** (since 1.6.0): Updates the id (code), name and/or description of existing Classification Items, keeping their guid and so the elements classified with them. Items cannot be moved to another parent. Parameters: classificationItems.
- **GetClassificationItemParents** (since 1.8.0): Returns the parent item and the classification system of the given Classification Items; a top level item has no parent. The output is aligned with the input array of items. Parameters: classificationItemIds.
- **ImportClassificationsXml** (since 1.6.0): Imports a Classification Manager XML export, with the given policies for systems and items that already exist. Returns the systems and items it created and removed. Parameters: xml, systemConflictPolicy, itemConflictPolicy.
- **GetClassificationItemVisibility** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the given classification items are visible (offered) for the given elements, element tool defaults and attributes, such as building materials. Non-existing targets and classification items are reported as errors. Visibility does not tell whether the target is classified with the item, and an item can be visible even if its parent item is not. Parameters: targets, classificationItemIds.

## Attribute Commands

- **GetAttributesByType** (since 1.1.3): Returns the details of every attribute of the given type, including the path of the attribute folder holding it (Archicad 26 and newer). From Archicad 30 an attribute that Archicad keeps a creation record of also carries creationInfo: how (method), from where (source), by whom and when it was created. Parameters: attributeType.
- **GetAttributeIndexes** (since 2.0.0): Reports for each given attribute type how many attributes there are, the first valid and the highest index in use, and the free indexes between them (for example those of deleted attributes). Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: attributeTypes.
- **GetAttributesFromProject** (since 1.7.3): Reads the attributes of the given types from another project or template file without opening it, for example to compare them with the attributes of the open project. Nothing is imported into the open project. The names are the legacy 8-bit names, so non-ASCII characters may not come through. Archicad does not read Layer, Surface, BuildingMaterial and MEPSystem attributes from a file that is not open: these types get an error item instead of an empty list. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: projectFilePath, attributeTypes.
- **DeleteAttributes** (since 1.5.4): Deletes the given attributes. Returns an execution result for each input item. With dryRun true nothing is deleted: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks made before deleting (valid attribute type, attribute exists) gets wouldDelete. Parameters: attributesToDelete, dryRun.
- **ImportAttributesFromProject** (since 2.0.0): Imports Line, Fill, ZoneCategory, PenTable, OperationProfile, Composite, Profile and LayerCombination attributes from another project or template file into the open project, with their complete definition (symbol and percent fills included), like Append or Overwrite by name in Archicad's Attribute Manager. The lines and fills a composite or profile uses are matched by name; its building materials and surfaces, and the layers of a layer combination, keep their index only with referencesByIndex, since Archicad does not read these types from a closed file. An attribute with a reference that cannot be mapped is not imported. A new attribute gets a new guid: Archicad does not hand out the guids stored in the source file. An attribute whose name already exists is skipped, or overwritten in place with overwriteExisting. dryRun reports what would happen without changing anything. The names are the legacy 8-bit names of the source file. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: projectFilePath, attributeTypes, attributeNames, overwriteExisting, dryRun, referencesByIndex.
- **GetUsedAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Gets how many attributes of each type are in use (layers, lines, fills, composites, surfaces, ...), as Archicad reports them for the usedAttributes JSON query: the counts in usedAttributes, the report as text in raw. Available from Archicad 27.
- **ConsolidateLines** (since 1.8.0): Runs the Line Consolidation menu command of Archicad on the current window, as the menu does, and reports whether it ran together with what Archicad answered. Available from Archicad 27.
- **ConsolidateFills** (since 1.8.0): Runs the Fill Consolidation menu command of Archicad on the current window, as the menu does, and reports whether it ran together with what Archicad answered. Available from Archicad 27.
- **CreateAttributeFolders** (since 1.7.3): Creates attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path (the folder names from the root folder down). Missing parent folders are created too; a folder that already exists is kept and reported as success. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeFolders.
- **DeleteAttributeFolders** (since 1.7.3): Deletes attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, together with all the subfolders and deletable attributes they contain (a folder holding an attribute that cannot be deleted is kept). The root folder cannot be deleted. With dryRun true nothing is deleted: the response has dryRun set to true, and each folder that exists and is not the root folder gets wouldDelete. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeFolders, dryRun.
- **RenameAttributeFolders** (since 1.7.3): Renames attribute folders, each given by attribute type and path, to the given new names. The root folder cannot be renamed. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeFolders.
- **MoveAttributesAndFolders** (since 1.7.3): Moves attributes and attribute folders (with their contents) into the target folder, which must be of the same attribute type; an empty target path is the root folder. Returns one execution result per attribute and per folder; an attribute or folder that is already directly in the target folder counts as moved. Available from Archicad 26. Parameters: attributeIds, attributeFolders, targetFolder.
- **ReindexLayers** (since 2.0.0): Moves layers to new indices. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so each layer is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary layers, which are deleted again), gets the old layer's state in every layer combination, and then every element of the old layer is moved to it, in the floor plan and in every view and layout database, with the tool defaults on that layer. Only when the old layer is empty everywhere is it deleted, and the new layer gets its name, flags and folder. If an element cannot be moved (it is locked, not reserved in Teamwork, or comes from a hotlinked module), that layer is left as it was. The new layer has a new attribute id; Favorites that use the layer are not updated. Archicad keeps the shown, locked and wireframe state of a layer per open window: the new layer gets the old one's state in the current window and in every layer combination, and starts shown and unlocked in the other open windows. The model elements that sections, elevations, interior elevations and 3D documents show of the layer come back on the new layer when those views are rebuilt (listed as viewsToRebuild). dryRun lists the elements and tool defaults on each layer without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: layers, dryRun, maxPlaceholders.
- **ReindexAttributes** (since 2.0.0): Moves fills, line types, surfaces, building materials and zone categories to new indices, the way ReindexLayers moves layers. Archicad cannot renumber an attribute, so the attribute is recreated at its new index (free indices below it are filled with temporary attributes, which are deleted again) and every reference to the old index is rewritten to the new one: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, the memo data of roofs, slabs, meshes, morphs, curtain walls, beams, columns, stairs and interior elevations, the tool defaults, the Favorites (with their sub-elements: a curtain wall's frame and panel classes, a stair's structures), the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Only then is the old attribute deleted. The new attribute has a new attribute id (Archicad does not keep a given id); its name, definition and attribute folder are the old ones. Elements on a hidden or locked layer cannot be changed, so their layers are shown and unlocked for the move and put back afterwards (in the current window, as Archicad keeps these flags per window). If an element still cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not moved. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed; their module file has to be reindexed on its own. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the old index (Archicad does not take them from ACAPI_Favorite_Change, so such Favorites are left as they are and named in the warnings). dryRun lists every reference without changing anything. The whole call is one undo step. Pens, layers (see ReindexLayers) and the other attribute types are not supported. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: attributeType, attributes, dryRun, maxPlaceholders.
- **DeleteAndReplaceAttributes** (since 2.0.0): Deletes fills, line types, surfaces or building materials and replaces each by another attribute of the same type wherever it was used, like Delete and Replace in the Attribute Manager. Every reference is rewritten to the replacement, the way ReindexAttributes rewrites them: the fields of the elements in the floor plan and in every view and layout, the parameters of library part based elements, their memo data, the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes that refer to it (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules. Elements on a hidden or locked layer are changed too: their layers are shown and unlocked for the change and put back afterwards (in the current window). If an element cannot be changed (it is locked itself, or not reserved in Teamwork), everything is put back and that attribute is not deleted. Elements from hotlinked modules cannot be changed and are listed. Indices typed into GDL scripts are not found, and the frame and panel classes of curtain wall Favorites and of the Curtain Wall tool default keep the deleted attribute (named in the warnings). If a tool default, Favorite, attribute or rule cannot be rewritten to the replacement, it keeps a copy of the deleted attribute with its name and a new attribute id, named in the warnings. The whole call is one undo step. With dryRun true nothing is changed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that passes the checks gets wouldDelete and lists every reference a real run would rewrite (elements, tool defaults, Favorites, other attributes, graphic override rules, elements from hotlinked modules). Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: attributeType, attributes, dryRun.
- **GetUnusedAttributes** (since 2.0.0): Lists the unused layers, fills, surfaces, building materials, composites, profiles, line types, pen tables and zone categories (index, id and name), for the given types or all of them. The Archicad API has no function that tells which attributes are unused (only how many per type), so every reference is collected: the elements of the floor plan and of every view and layout (hotlinked ones too), with their library part parameters and memo data, the tool defaults, the Favorites, the other attributes (composites, building materials, surfaces, profiles, MEP systems) and the graphic override rules, the way ReindexAttributes finds them; for layers the layer of each element, tool default and Favorite; for composites and profiles the walls, slabs, roofs, shells, column and beam segments whose structure type uses them; for pen tables the current pen table and the drawings set to a pen table of their own. An attribute that only an unused attribute refers to counts as used. Indices typed into GDL scripts and the pen tables saved with views are not found. Each type also reports Archicad's own count of the attributes in use (archicadUsedCount, see GetUsedAttributes), so a difference shows. Read only. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: types.
- **GetMissingAttributes** (since 2.0.0): Lists the references of placed elements to layers, fills, surfaces, building materials, composites, profiles, line types, pen tables and zone categories that do not exist in the project, for the given types or all of them, and of the tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options combinations and attributes: the structured counterpart of the missing attributes report of Archicad's GDL palette. Every element of the floor plan and of every view and layout (hotlinked ones too) is checked, and so is every tool default and Favorite (with its sub-elements): its layer, its attribute fields and memo data as ReindexAttributes finds them, its composite or profile when its structure type uses one, a drawing's own pen table, and its library part parameters of attribute types; of every graphic override rule the line type, fill and surface it overrides with; of every Model View Options combination the surfaces and line types of the stair and railing schemes and the library part settings' GDL parameters of attribute types; of every composite the building materials of its skins and the line types of its separators, of every building material its cut fill and cut surface, of every surface the fill of its vectorial hatching, of every MEP system its fill, center line type and surfaces, and of every profile the building material, surface or fill of each skin and its contour, cut end and edge line types. The sources input limits the check to elements, tool defaults, Favorites, graphic override rules, Model View Options or attributes. Each item names the source; for an element the element (and the element it is part of, for a curtain wall frame, a column segment, ...) and the story or view it sits on, for a tool default the tool, for a Favorite its name and tool, for a graphic override rule its guid and name, for a Model View Options combination its guid and name (and the library part option set), for an attribute its type, guid and name; then the attribute type, the missing index and the field or GDL parameter that holds it. Index 0 counts as no attribute. Read only. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: attributeTypes, sources.
- **CreateLayers** (since 1.0.3): Creates or overwrites Layer attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: layerDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateLayerCombinations** (since 1.2.4): Creates or overwrites Layer Combination attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: layerCombinationDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateLines** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Line attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: lineDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateFills** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Fill attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: fillDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateZoneCategories** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Zone Category attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: zoneCategoryDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateMEPSystems** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface) based on the given parameters. Parameters: mepSystemDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreatePenTables** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Pen Table attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: penTableDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **ModifyPens** (since 1.7.2): Changes the color, width and description of single pens of the Pen Table in effect for the model views (the default) or the layouts, keeping every other pen as it is. Only the given fields of a listed pen are changed. In a Teamwork project the PenTables lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet). Parameters: pens, target.
- **CreateProfiles** (since 1.5.4): Creates or overwrites Profile attributes as a copy of an existing Profile's geometry, based on the given parameters. Parameters: profileDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateBuildingMaterials** (since 1.0.1): Creates or overwrites Building Material attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: buildingMaterialDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateComposites** (since 1.0.2): Creates or overwrites Composite attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: compositeDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateSurfaces** (since 1.2.2): Creates or overwrites Surface attributes based on the given parameters. Parameters: surfaceDataArray, overwriteExisting.
- **GetBuildingMaterialPhysicalProperties** (since 0.1.3): Retrieves the physical properties of the given Building Materials. Parameters: attributeIds.
- **GetLayerCombinations** (since 1.2.4): Returns the details of layer combination attributes. Parameters: attributes.
- **GetCurrentLayerCombination** (since 1.7.3): Returns the layer combination in effect in the current window. No layer combination is returned when the current state of the layers matches none.
- **ActivateLayerCombination** (since 2.0.0): Activates the given layer combination in the current window, like choosing it in the Quick Layers palette. Saved views are not changed. Parameters: attributeId.
- **GetLayerOfElementDefaults** (since 2.0.0): Returns the layer of the tool defaults of the given element types: the layer new elements of that type are placed on. Parameters: elementTypes.
- **SetLayerOfElementDefaults** (since 2.0.0): Sets the layer of the tool defaults of the given element types, so new elements of that type are placed on it. Only the layer of the defaults is changed. Parameters: layersOfElementDefaults.
- **RenameAttributes** (since 2.0.0): Renames attributes of any type (layers, layer combinations, composites, surfaces, ...). Each attribute keeps its index, its id and its settings. A new name that another attribute of the same type already has is refused, and so is renaming the attributes Archicad does not allow to change (the built-in Archicad Layer, the Solid and Empty fills). Parameters: attributes.
- **GetLines** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Line attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetFills** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Fill attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetZoneCategories** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Zone Category attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetMEPSystems** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given MEP System attributes (domain, pens, fill, center line type, surface and insulation surface). Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetPenTables** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Pen Table attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetCurrentPenTable** (since 1.7.3): Returns the current Pen Table (its index, attribute identifier and name) and its number of pens. Pass the returned attributeId to GetPenTables to read the pens.
- **GetPens** (since 1.8.0): Returns the given pens, or all of them, in effect in the current window: index, color, width and description. It also works when the pens in effect are not a Pen Table attribute. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: indices.
- **SetPens** (since 2.0.0): Changes the color, width and description of the given pens in effect in the current window, the pens GetPens returns, in one undo step. Only the given fields of a listed pen are changed; each pen gets its own execution result. In a Teamwork project the PenTables lockable object set must be reserved first (see ReserveLockableObjectSet). Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: pens.
- **GetProfiles** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Profile attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetComposites** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Composite attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetSurfaces** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Surface attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetLayers** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Layer attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetBuildingMaterials** (since 1.5.4): Returns the details of the given Building Material attributes. Parameters: attributeIds, fields.
- **GetFontsByName** (since 1.7.3): Finds loaded fonts by name through Archicad's font search and returns their index (as Text and Label fields reference fonts in fontIndex) and name, or an error for a name no loaded font has. Parameters: fontNames.
