- **GetGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Gets all graphic override rules of the project, with their rule group, criterion and style. With includeCriterion the criterion also comes as structured conditions, which CreateGraphicOverrideRules and ModifyGraphicOverrideRules take back. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: includeCriterion.
- **GetGraphicOverrideRulesByName** (since 1.7.3): Gets graphic override rules by name, with their rule group, criterion and style. The rule group narrows the search; without it the rule is searched in every rule group. With includeCriterion the criterion also comes as structured conditions. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules, includeCriterion.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Creates graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. The rule group is created when no rule group has the given name. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules.
- **ModifyGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Modifies the name, criterion or style of graphic override rules. The criterion is given as Archicad's criterion XML or as structured conditions. A given style replaces the whole style of the rule. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules.
- **DeleteGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Deletes graphic override rules. They are also removed from the combinations that contain them. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRuleIds.
- **GetGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Gets all graphic override combinations of the project with the rules they contain. Available from Archicad 27.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Creates graphic override combinations from existing rules. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideCombinations.
- **ModifyGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the name and/or the rules of graphic override combinations. Omitted fields are kept. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideCombinations.
- **DeleteGraphicOverrideCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Deletes graphic override combinations. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideCombinationIds.
- **CreateGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.8.0): Creates empty graphic override rule groups. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroupNames.
- **GetGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.7.2): Gets all graphic override rule groups of the project with the rules they contain, empty groups included. Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetGraphicOverrideRuleOrder** (since 1.8.0): Sets the order of the rules in graphic override rule groups, found by name. The listed rules come first, in the given order; the other rules of the group keep their order after them. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRuleGroups.
- **RenameGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.7.3): Renames graphic override rule groups, found by name. Their rules are kept. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroups.
- **DeleteGraphicOverrideRuleGroups** (since 1.7.2): Deletes graphic override rule groups, found by name. A group that still contains rules is kept unless its rules are moved to another group or deleted with it. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroupNames, moveRulesToGroup, deleteRules.
- **SetGraphicOverrideRuleGroupOrder** (since 1.8.0): Sets the order of the graphic override rule groups, found by name. The groups not listed keep their order and follow the listed ones. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: ruleGroupNames.
- **MoveGraphicOverrideRules** (since 1.7.3): Moves graphic override rules to another rule group, or to another place in their own group. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: graphicOverrideRules.
- **GetUserDataOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Reads the key-value pairs stored on attributes by SetUserDataOfAttributes. An attribute without user data returns no pairs; one holding user data in another layout returns an error. Parameters: attributeIds.
- **SetUserDataOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Stores string values under keys in the user data of attributes, for scripts to keep their own state on an attribute. The given pairs are merged into what each attribute already holds: a key that exists gets the new value, other keys are left as they are, and the keys listed in keysToDelete are removed. Prefix the keys with the script's name so that scripts do not overwrite each other's data. User data in another layout is left unchanged and reported as an error. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it. Parameters: attributeIds, pairs, keysToDelete.
- **DeleteUserDataOfAttributes** (since 1.8.0): Removes the user data of attributes, every key at once. Archicad does not record this change as an undo step, so Undo does not revert it. With dryRun true nothing is removed: the response has dryRun set to true, and each attribute that exists gets wouldDelete. Parameters: attributeIds, dryRun.

## IFC Commands

- **IFCFileOperation** (since 1.2.6): Executes an IFC file operation: opens or merges an IFC file, or saves the project as an IFC file. A save can name the export translator to use, a merge the story the IFC file's first storey is placed on. With overwrite false a save refuses to replace an existing file. Parameters: method, ifcFilePath, overwrite, fileType, translatorName, elementsToExport, storyIndex.
- **GetIFCExportTranslators** (since 1.6.0): Lists the IFC export translators of the project in the order of Archicad's translator list. preview marks the first one, which the Archicad API documents as the preview translator; no API identifies the preview translator otherwise, and in some projects the IFC Translators dialog shows another one as preview. Pass one of the names to IFCFileOperation as translatorName.
- **GetElementsByIFCIds** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the elements by the given IFC identifiers. Accepts IFC GlobalIds in every Archicad version. Parameters: ifcIds.
- **GetIFCIdsOfElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the IFC identifiers of the given elements. Before Archicad 28 it also returns their IFC GlobalIds. Parameters: elements.
- **GetIFCTypeOfElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the IFC types of the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetIFCPropertiesOfElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the IFC properties of the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetIFCAttributesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, PredefinedType, LongName, ...) of the given elements, subelements included: the name, the IFC value type and the value of each attribute. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 storedOnly returns only the attributes stored on the elements. Parameters: elements, storedOnly.
- **SetIFCAttributesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Sets the values of IFC attributes (Name, Description, ObjectType, Tag, ...) of elements. The attribute must be one GetIFCAttributesOfElements returns for the element; its IFC value type is kept. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCAttributeValues.
- **SetIFCPropertiesOfElements** (since 1.7.0): Sets local IFC properties on elements by creating or modifying single value (IfcPropertySingleValue) properties in the given property sets. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCPropertyValues.
- **GetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Retrieves the IFC classification references of the given elements, subelements included: identification, name, location, description and sort (from Archicad 29), the name of the IfcRelAssociatesClassification (from Archicad 28), the referenced classification (name, source, edition, edition date, description and location) and whether the reference comes from the preview translator or is stored locally. On Archicad 25, 26 and 27 the source is not given and storedOnly returns only the references stored on the elements. Parameters: elements, storedOnly.
- **SetIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Stores IFC classification references (identification, name, location and the referenced classification with its name, edition, edition date, description and location) on elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. Parameters: elementIFCClassificationReferences.
- **RemoveIFCClassificationReferencesOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Removes IFC classification references stored on elements, given by the name of their classification and optionally their identification; without identification every stored reference of that classification is removed. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that has a matching stored reference gets wouldDelete. Parameters: elementIFCClassificationReferences, dryRun.
- **RemoveIFCPropertiesOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Removes local IFC properties, given by property set and property name, from elements. Available only in Archicad 25, 26 and 27 for now. With dryRun true nothing is removed and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and each element that has the local IFC property gets wouldDelete. Parameters: elementIFCProperties, dryRun.
- **GetIFCSpatialStructure** (since 2.0.0): Returns the IfcProject, IfcSite and IfcBuilding objects of the project's IFC model (hash value, IFC type and GlobalId), and for the given elements the index of the story they are assigned to in the IFC model. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetIFCAssignments** (since 2.0.0): Returns the IFC assignments of the project: the root IFC groups, and for each object the objects assigned to it (children) and the objects it is assigned to (parents). Each object is given by its hash value, its element where it belongs to one, its IFC type and its GlobalId. Available from Archicad 28.

## Library Commands

- **GetLibraries** (since 1.0.1): Gets the list of loaded libraries. From Archicad 28 a library package also gets its package information (ID, versions, minimum Archicad version and dependencies).
- **ReloadLibraries** (since 1.0.0): Executes the reload libraries command.
- **AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary** (since 1.2.2): Adds the given files into the embedded library. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on an outputPath is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer). Parameters: files, overwriteExisting.
- **DeleteEmbeddedLibraryItems** (since 1.6.0): Deletes the given items from the embedded library. The path of an item is the same relative path that AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary takes as outputPath. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: embeddedLibraryItems.
- **CreateLibraryParts** (since 1.8.0): Creates GDL library parts in the embedded library from their scripts (master, 2D, 3D, parameter, interface, properties) and parameter definitions, under the given parent subtype. The new parts are placeable right away, e.g. with CreateObjects. With the overwriteExisting flag an embedded library item already existing on the path of a new part is replaced (Archicad 27 or newer). Parameters: libraryParts, overwriteExisting.
- **CreateFolderInEmbeddedLibrary** (since 1.7.3): Creates a folder, with any missing parent folders, inside the embedded library. The folderPath is relative to the embedded library, like the outputPath of AddFilesToEmbeddedLibrary. Parameters: folderPath.
- **CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary** (since 1.7.3): Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced. Parameters: files, targetFolder, overwriteIfExists.
- **SetLibraries** (since 1.5.9): Makes the given folders the project's local libraries; built-in, embedded, server and web libraries are kept. Set the libraries before opening a file that needs them and the missing-library dialog does not appear. Parameters: libraries.
- **AddLibraries** (since 1.5.9): Adds the given folders to the project's local libraries, skipping any already loaded. Parameters: libraries.
- **GetAvailableLibraryParts** (since 1.5.0): Lists library parts currently available to the project. Filter by typeId (e.g. 'Door', 'Window', 'Object', 'Lamp'). Parameters: filterByTypeId.
- **GetLibraryPartSections** (since 2.0.0): Lists the sections of library parts given by index: their four-character type code, sub-identifier, size and whether they are text (scripts, comments) or binary (previews). Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetLibraryPartSection** (since 2.0.0): Reads the text of a text section (a script or the comment) of a library part given by index, without opening it in the GDL editor. Takes the password of a protected library part. Parameters: index, sectionType, subIdent, password.
- **GetLibrariesOfLibParts** (since 2.0.0): Gets the library of each given library part (by file name or guid): display name, location, embedded/built-in/package/local/missing flags and the Library Manager tree path. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetLibraryPartTypeDetails** (since 2.0.0): Returns the type details of the given library parts (ACAPI_LibraryPart_GetDetails): full unique ID and its direct parent's, type, the detail flags of objects, lamps, labels and zones, the frame and orientation settings of doors and windows, and the element type and variation of the tool that places the library part. For their path, library, GUID, license and scripts see GetLibraryPartDetails. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **IsLibraryPartSubtypeOf** (since 2.0.0): Checks for each of the given library parts whether the given ancestor is anywhere up its subtype hierarchy (e.g. whether a part is a kind of furniture), independent of its name. A library part is not a subtype of itself. With matchAncestorByMainId any revision of the ancestor matches. Parameters: libraryParts, ancestor, matchAncestorByMainId.
- **GetGDLParametersOfLibraryParts** (since 2.0.0): Gets the default GDL parameters (name, display name, type, array dimensions, value, flags) of the given library parts by name, read from the library part without placing it or changing any defaults. The output is in the format of GetGDLParametersOfElements, without isLocked and possibleValues, which need a placed element. To read a part by its file name, as SetLibraryPartParameters writes it, use GetLibraryPartParameterValues. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetMissingLibPartNames** (since 2.0.0): Gets the library part name of the given placed Object, Lamp, Window or Door elements, even if the library containing the part is not loaded. Use it to find the parts of elements that are shown as dots because their library part is missing. Parameters: elements.
- **GetUnusedLibraryParts** (since 2.0.0): Lists the loaded library parts that no element of the project is placed from. Read only. The Archicad API does not tell which library parts are used, so every element of the floor plan and of every view and layout is checked: objects, lamps, doors, windows, skylights, zone stamps, symbol labels, drawing titles, curtain wall parts, and the markers of doors, windows, skylights, sections, elevations, details and worksheets. A library part used only in another way (called as a macro, linked as a property object, as an interior elevation marker, in stairs and railings, in the tool defaults or in Favorites) is listed as unused. Library parts that cannot be placed (e.g. macros) are only listed with includeNotPlaceable. Parameters: filterByTypeId, includeNotPlaceable.
- **FindLibraryParts** (since 2.0.0): Finds loaded library parts with the Library Manager: all of them, GDL objects, images or text files, optionally only those whose name contains a text. Returns the name, path and index of each. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: kind, nameContains, firstOnly.
- **GetLibraryPartDetails** (since 2.0.0): Gets the details of loaded library parts, by name or index: path, library tree path, containing library, and for GDL objects the GUID, subtype, license, UI default flag, which scripts and pictures they have, and optionally the interface and migration scripts. Can also tell whether each one is in the subtype of another library part. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts, subTypeOf, includeScripts.
- **ModifyLibraryList** (since 2.0.0): Adds libraries by path and removes loaded libraries by name or path, in one change of the library list. Returns the result of each addition and removal. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: add, remove.
- **GetLibraryPartMetadata** (since 2.0.0): Returns the description, keywords, author and placeable, password protected and hierarchical pages flags of loaded library parts, given by file name. Use it to search library parts by description or keywords and to tell placeable parts from macros. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetLibraryPartOriginalLocations** (since 1.8.0): Gets the original location of the given library parts, the file they came from, e.g. before they were embedded into the project. The library parts are given by the index GetAvailableLibraryParts returns. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **IsUsableGDLString** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether each of the given strings is usable in GDL, e.g. before writing it into a GDL parameter or script. Returns one boolean for each string. Parameters: strings.
- **GetGDLDate** (since 2.0.0): Gets the date GDL scripts see: year, month, day, hour, minute and second.
- **SetGDLDate** (since 2.0.0): Sets the date GDL scripts see: year, month, day, hour, minute and second, as GetGDLDate returns them. Useful to test date-dependent library parts; set the value read with GetGDLDate back to restore it. Parameters: date.
- **CheckLibraries** (since 1.8.0): Checks the loaded libraries with the Archicad API's library check. Returns the error the API reports, if any.
- **ResetLibraries** (since 1.8.0): Resets the loaded libraries with the Archicad API's library reset.
- **SetLibraryPartScripts** (since 1.7.3): Sets and deletes the master, parameter, 2D, 3D, properties, interface and forward and backward migration scripts of loaded library parts. Only the given scripts are changed; an empty script makes the section empty, deleteScripts removes it. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **SetLibraryPartMetadata** (since 1.8.0): Sets the author, keywords, license, license version, password and the placeable, UI default, subtype and hierarchical pages flags of loaded library parts. Only the given fields are changed. A library part that is not editable (e.g. a part of a library package or a read-only library) is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetLibraryPartPictures** (since 1.8.0): Gets the preview picture and the GDL pictures of a loaded library part as base64 encoded PNGs, and from Archicad 29 also their dark user interface variants. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name.
- **SetLibraryPartPictures** (since 1.8.0): Deletes the preview picture, the GDL pictures (and from Archicad 29 their dark variants) or the 2D symbol of a loaded library part, or copies the 2D symbol from another library part. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name, deletePreviewPicture, deleteDarkPreviewPicture, deleteGdlPictures, deleteDarkGdlPictures, copy2DSymbolFrom, delete2DSymbol.
- **GetLibraryPartCustomSection** (since 1.8.0): Gets a custom section of a loaded library part by its section identifier and index: whether it exists, its data version and its content as base64. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name, sectionId, index.
- **SetLibraryPartCustomSection** (since 1.8.0): Creates, replaces or deletes a custom section of a loaded library part. The content is given as base64. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name, sectionId, index, dataVersion, data, delete.
- **CreateLibraryPart** (since 1.8.0): Creates a new library part file (.gsm) of the given loaded subtype, inheriting its parameters, and reports whether it is loaded with its index and names. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: path, ancestorSubtype.
- **GetLibraryPartParameterValues** (since 2.0.0): Returns the parameters of loaded library parts, given by their file name as GetAvailableLibraryParts returns it, with their default values and descriptions, in the format of GetGDLParametersOfElements: the read counterpart of SetLibraryPartParameters. Unlike GetGDLParametersOfLibraryParts, which finds a part by its name and also returns the index, flags and value descriptions of each parameter, it reads through the Library Manager. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **UpdateLibraryPartSections** (since 2.0.0): Replaces the text of existing sections (scripts, comment, keywords, copyright) of a loaded library part, found by its name. Each section is read back after the update, and the output has one execution result per section. Parameters: name, sections.
- **GetLibraryPart2DPrimitives** (since 2.0.0): Gets the lines, arcs and polygons (with their holes, and whether they are fills) of the 2D symbol of a loaded library part, drawn with its default parameters or with the parameters of a placed instance. Parameters: name, elementId, gdlContext.
- **SetLibraryPartPictureImages** (since 2.0.0): Sets the preview picture and the GDL pictures of a loaded library part from base64 encoded PNGs, and from Archicad 29 also their dark user interface variants. All pictures are set in one step; an invalid picture changes nothing. A library part that is not editable is refused and left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: name, previewPicture, gdlPictures, darkPreviewPicture, darkGdlPictures.
- **SetLibraryPartParameters** (since 2.0.0): Sets the parameter values, and optionally the parameter descriptions, of loaded library parts, in the format of SetGDLParametersOfElements. Only the given parameters are changed; with merge, the changed list is merged into the parameters of the part instead of replacing them. A library part that is not editable, or with an invalid value given, is left unchanged. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetLibraryPartScripts** (since 2.0.0): Gets the master, parameter, 2D, 3D and properties scripts of loaded library parts, given by name or by an element placed from them, with the unique ID of each part. A script section the part does not have is reported as not present. Password protected parts need their password. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts, scripts, password.
- **GetLibraryPartFileInfo** (since 2.0.0): Reads library part files (.gsm) without loading them into the libraries of the project: the unique ID of the part, the unique ID of its subtype and its master, parameter, 2D, 3D and properties scripts. Password protected parts need their password. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: files, scripts, password.
- **CopyLibraryParts** (since 2.0.0): Copies loaded library parts, given by name or by an element placed from them, under a new file name into a folder, by default the embedded library. The copy gets a new unique ID unless the main GUID is kept. An existing file is never overwritten. The libraries are reloaded once afterwards, so the copies can be found by name. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **GetLibraryPartIdentities** (since 2.0.0): Gets the unique ID (main and revision GUID), the reference GUID and the Teamwork lock status of library parts given by index or file path, and whether they are in a server library. Parameters: libraryParts.
- **CompareLibraryPartUnIds** (since 2.0.0): Compares two library part unique IDs with Archicad's own comparison and tells whether their main and revision GUIDs are the same. Parameters: unId1, unId2.
- **GetLastValidEmbeddedLibraryPartName** (since 2.0.0): Gets the name and file path of the last valid library part of the embedded library.
- **SearchLibraryParts** (since 2.0.0): Finds the loaded library parts derived from an ancestor library part (by its unique ID) whose name matches a pattern with * wildcards. Archicad returns at most 50 of them. Parameters: ancestorUnId, pattern.
- **OpenLibraryPartInEditor** (since 1.8.0): Opens a loaded library part, given by its fileName or documentName as returned by GetAvailableLibraryParts, in Archicad's library part editor. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: name.
- **CreateLibraryPartFromElements** (since 2.0.0): Creates a library part in the embedded library (or in a given local library folder, which is added to the loaded libraries when needed) whose 2D symbol is a copy of the given 2D drawing elements (lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines, fills, texts and hotspots), under the given parent subtype, with optional master, 2D, 3D and parameter scripts, comment and keywords. A and B are taken from the extent of the symbol. The elements themselves are not changed. Parameters: name, elements, parentId, parentName, folder, libraryFolder, overwrite, placeable, scripts, comment, keywords.
- **InterpretGDLScript3D** (since 2.0.0): Runs a GDL 3D script, given as text or as the master and 3D scripts of a loaded library part with its default parameters, with the settings of the GDL editor, and returns whether it ran without a GDL error, how many 3D model elements it generated and their bounding box. The API returns no GDL error message or line number. Parameters: script, libraryPartName.
- **GetGDLUserGlobals** (since 2.0.0): Returns the current GDL global variables the GDL interpreter gets, with their names, types and values. Available from Archicad 28.

## Teamwork Commands

- **TeamworkSend** (since 0.1.0): Performs a send operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.
- **TeamworkReceive** (since 0.1.0): Performs a receive operation on the currently opened Teamwork project.
- **GetTeamworkProjectInfo** (since 1.8.0): Tells whether the opened project is a Teamwork project and whether it is online, and returns its BIMcloud server, project name and the current user (id and name).
- **ReserveElements** (since 1.1.4): Reserves elements in Teamwork mode. GUIDs that are not elements (navigator items, layouts, databases) cannot be reserved with it: they are returned in notElements and the execution result fails. Parameters: elements.
- **ReleaseElements** (since 1.1.4): Releases elements in Teamwork mode. Fails, naming them, when any of the given GUIDs is not an element; the other elements are released. Parameters: elements.
- **GetReservationStatusOfElements** (since 1.7.3): Returns the Teamwork reservation status of elements without reserving them: whether each element is free, reserved by the current user or reserved by another user, with the reserving user. New elements stay reserved by the user who created them until they are released. Parameters: elements.
- **GrantElements** (since 1.7.3): Hands over the reservation of elements to another Teamwork user, given by user id, without a dialog. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements, userId.
- **ReserveLockableObjectSet** (since 1.7.1): Reserves a non-element lockable object set (attributes, favorites, project info, project preferences, etc.) in Teamwork mode. The object set is given by its Archicad API name, e.g. 'Composites', 'LayerSettingsDialog' or 'ProjectInfo'. Parameters: objectSetName.
- **ReleaseLockableObjectSet** (since 1.7.1): Releases a non-element lockable object set reserved with ReserveLockableObjectSet in Teamwork mode. Parameters: objectSetName.
- **GetLockableObjectSetStatus** (since 1.7.1): Returns the Teamwork reservation status of a non-element lockable object set and the users who hold it. Parameters: objectSetName.
- **ReserveHotlinkCacheManagement** (since 1.7.1): Reserves the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode, which is needed before changing hotlink nodes.
- **ReleaseHotlinkCacheManagement** (since 1.7.1): Releases the Hotlink and XRef management in Teamwork mode.
- **GetTeamworkStatus** (since 1.7.3): Returns whether the opened project is a Teamwork project and is online, the members of the shared project and who has reserved the Hotlink and XRef management. Works in a solo project too, then isShared and isOnline are false.
- **GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases** (since 1.8.0): Returns the Teamwork owner (user id and name) of each given database, e.g. of a layout or a view database. The user id is 0 when nobody owns the database. Parameters: databases.
- **UploadLibrariesToBIMcloud** (since 1.8.0): Uploads local library folders or container files (.lcf) to a folder of a BIMcloud or Teamwork server, as BIMcloud libraries. Returns a result per library. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: libraryPaths, serverUrl, parentPath.
- **RemoveLibrariesFromBIMcloud** (since 1.8.0): Removes libraries, given by name, from a folder of a BIMcloud or Teamwork server. Returns a result per library. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: libraryNames, serverUrl, parentPath.
- **GetTeamworkRightsOfObjects** (since 2.0.0): Returns for each given object, for example an element, whether the current Teamwork user has the right to create objects of its kind and to delete or modify it. Parameters: objectIds.
- **GetTeamworkAccessRights** (since 2.0.0): Returns whether the role of the current user has the given Teamwork access rights (API_TWAccessRights names without the API prefix, e.g. LayersCreate), all of them when no names are given. Parameters: accessRights.

## Navigator Commands

- **PublishPublisherSet** (since 0.1.0): Performs a publish operation on the currently opened project. Only the given publisher set will be published. Parameters: publisherSetName, outputPath, selectedNavigatorItemIds.
- **GetPublisherSets** (since 2.0.0): Returns the publisher sets of the project with their saved output: the local or LAN path, the Teamwork file server path, or the Internet host and directory name.
- **UpdateDrawings** (since 1.1.4): Performs a drawing update on the given elements. Parameters: elements.
- **GetDrawingContentBoxes** (since 1.7.3): Returns the full content box of the given Drawing elements, independent of their frames, as ACAPI_Drawing_GetFullDrawingContentBox reports it. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements.
- **GetDatabaseIdFromNavigatorItemId** (since 1.1.4): Gets the ID of the database associated with the supplied navigator item id Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **GetDatabases** (since 1.7.3): Lists every database of the given types (sections, elevations, interior elevations, details, worksheets, 3D documents, layouts, master layouts) with its database ID, name and reference ID, without walking the navigator trees. Parameters: types.
- **CreateDetails** (since 1.4.0): Creates independent Detail databases. Returns the databaseId and the Project Map navigatorItemId of each new detail. Parameters: detailsData.
- **CreateWorksheets** (since 1.4.0): Creates independent Worksheet databases. Returns the databaseId and the Project Map navigatorItemId of each new worksheet. Parameters: worksheetsData.
- **CreateDetailMarkers** (since 2.0.0): Places Detail markers with their clip polygon in the current floor plan, section or elevation, each with a new Detail viewpoint, like the Detail tool. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back. Parameters: detailMarkersData.
- **CreateWorksheetMarkers** (since 2.0.0): Places Worksheet markers with their clip polygon in the current floor plan, section or elevation, each with a new Worksheet viewpoint, like the Worksheet tool. GetDetailsOfElements reads them back. Parameters: worksheetMarkersData.
- **ModifyDetailMarkers** (since 2.0.0): Changes the name, the reference ID, the clip polygon, the boundary's pen and line type, the marker symbol's angle, always-horizontal setting and pen of Detail and Worksheet markers. Not written: the base point (Archicad places it at the center of the clip polygon's bounding box when the marker is created), the viewpoint the marker refers to, and the marker symbol's other settings, which are parameters of the library part placed as the marker (markerId in GetDetailsOfElements). A value Archicad did not apply gets a failed execution result. Parameters: detailMarkersWithDetails.
- **CreateLayout** (since 1.4.0): Creates Layouts and their backing master layouts. Archicad inserts a new layout at the first place of its subset, renumbering the sheets after it; previousNavigatorItemId or position 'last' places it after an existing sheet or at the end instead. A custom layout number does not leave the layout out of the numbering; layoutParameters.doNotIncludeInNumbering does. A layout that was created but could not be placed is returned with both its databaseId and the error. Parameters: layoutsData.
- **CreateLayoutSubset** (since 1.4.0): Creates Layout Book subsets. Parameters: subsetsData.
- **GetLayoutSubsetSettings** (since 1.7.3): Gets the settings of existing Layout Book subsets: the same fields CreateLayoutSubset accepts (name, ID prefix, numbering style, ...). Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **CreateDrawings** (since 1.4.0): Creates Drawing elements on the specified or active layout from navigator items. Parameters: drawingsData.
- **ChangeDrawingLink** (since 1.5.7): Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored. Parameters: drawingsWithNewLinks.
- **GetLayoutSettings** (since 1.1.7): Gets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields. Parameters: layoutDatabaseIds.
- **SetLayoutSettings** (since 1.1.7): Sets settings of layouts, including their master layout and Layout Info Panel custom data fields. In Teamwork the layout settings must be reserved first in Archicad (Layout Book > Reserve Layout Settings); the Archicad API cannot reserve them, and ReserveElements does not. GetTeamworkOwnersOfDatabases shows who holds a layout. Parameters: layoutsData.
- **GetLayoutCustomScheme** (since 1.1.7): Gets the Layout Info Panel custom field definitions (name and key) from Book Settings.
- **GetDrawingNumberingGridLines** (since 1.8.0): Gets the lines of the grid of the grid-based drawing numbering of the current layout (start and end point, pen index, line type index), for example to find which grid cell a drawing on the layout sits in. The current window must be a layout (see ChangeWindow), and only a layout that uses grid-based drawing numbering has such a grid.
- **GetModelViewOptions** (since 1.1.4): Gets all model view options
- **FindModelViewOption** (since 1.8.0): Finds a model view option combination by id or by name and returns its index, id, name and flags. The index is the one SetViewOptions takes to switch the model view options of a window to the combination. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: modelViewOptionId, name.
- **GetModelViewOptionDetails** (since 2.0.0): Gets the settings stored in model view option combinations (Document > Model View > Model View Options), all of them or the ones given by id or by name: the model view options in the fields of GetViewOptions, and the options library parts add to the combination (gdlOptions) with their GDL parameter values. Read-only: the Archicad API has no function to change, rename or create a stored combination; SetViewOptions changes the options of the current window. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: modelViewOptions.
- **GetViewOptions** (since 1.8.0): Gets the model view options and on-screen view options of the current plan window, and the index and name of the model view option combination it applies.
- **SetViewOptions** (since 1.8.0): Switches the current plan window to a model view option combination by index, and/or changes the given model view options and on-screen view options. With an index, the model view options stored in the combination apply. Parameters: modelViewOptionIndex, viewOptions.
- **GetViewSettings** (since 1.1.4): Gets the view settings of navigator items Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **SetViewSettings** (since 1.1.4): Sets the view settings of navigator items Parameters: navigatorItemIdsWithViewSettings.
- **GetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination** (since 1.7.2): Gets the graphic override combination applied to the current window, with its id and name. The response is empty when no combination is applied. This is the combination of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 30.
- **SetActiveGraphicalOverrideCombination** (since 1.7.2): Applies a graphic override combination, given by id or by name, to the current window. The current window must be a model window (floor plan, section, elevation, 3D, ...). To remove the overrides, apply the project's 'No Overrides' combination. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: combinationId, name.
- **GetRenovationFilters** (since 1.8.0): Gets the renovation filters of the project, and the one the current window uses (Document > Renovation > Renovation Filter). A renovationFilterId has the same shape as the renovationFilterGuid of GetViewSettings and SetViewSettings, so a filter listed here can be set on saved views too.
- **SetActiveRenovationFilter** (since 1.8.0): Sets the renovation filter of the current window (Document > Renovation > Renovation Filter), given by its renovationFilterId from GetRenovationFilters or by its name. Saved views keep their own filter: change that with SetViewSettings. Parameters: renovationFilterId, name.
- **GetGhostStorySettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the Trace & Reference ghost story settings of the floor plan: whether it is on, whether one story, the story above or the one below is shown, which story, its color and the element types shown in it.
- **SetGhostStorySettings** (since 1.8.0): Sets the Trace & Reference ghost story settings of the floor plan through its ghost record, which is created when the floor plan has none. Every field is optional; the ones left out keep their value, and without a story choice the current reference is kept. Parameters: on, showOne, showAbove, showBelow, storyIndex, ghostColor, filter.
- **GetStructureDisplay** (since 1.7.3): Gets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, and whether it is the 3D window. This is the setting of the window itself, not the one stored in a saved view (see GetViewSettings). Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetStructureDisplay** (since 1.7.3): Sets the Partial Structure Display (EntireStructure, CoreOnly, WithoutFinishes or StructureOnly) of the current window, e.g. the floor plan, a section or the 3D window. The change cannot be undone. The saved view is not changed (see SetViewSettings for that). Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: structureDisplay.
- **GetView2DTransformations** (since 1.1.7): Get zoom and rotation of 2D views Parameters: navigatorItemIds, databases.
- **SetViewRotation** (since 1.1.7): Set the rotation angle of 2D views via their floor plan database. Parameters: navigatorItemIdsWithRotation.
- **CloneProjectMapItemToViewMap** (since 1.1.7): Clones Project Map viewpoints into a specified View Map folder. Parameters: viewsData.
- **CreateViewsInViewMap** (since 1.1.7): Creates independent (non-clone) navigator views in a specified View Map folder, by copying database and settings from source items. Parameters: viewsData.
- **CreateViewMapFolder** (since 1.1.7): Creates a new folder in the View Map. Parameters: folderName, parentNavigatorItemId.
- **Set3DCutPlanes** (since 1.3.1): Sets the 3D cut planes. An empty cutPlanes array switches the 3D cut off. Parameters: cutPlanes.
- **Get3DCutPlanes** (since 1.7.3): Gets whether the 3D cut planes are on and the cut planes (pa, pb, pc, pd) of the 3D window, in the form accepted by Set3DCutPlanes.
- **Get3DStyleDetails** (since 1.7.3): Gets the settings of 3D styles by name (an empty name or no names means the current 3D style): rendering engine, model type, monochrome and background colors, contours, shadows and hatching. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: names.
- **Create3DStyles** (since 1.7.3): Creates 3D styles. Each new style starts from the current 3D style and differs from it only in the given fields. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: styles.
- **Change3DStyles** (since 1.7.3): Changes the given fields of existing 3D styles, identified by name. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: styles.
- **Get3DProjectionSettings** (since 1.7.2): Gets the 3D projection settings of the 3D window: whether it is perspective or axonometric, the camera and target position, view cone, roll angle, distance and azimuth of a perspective, or the projection type, azimuth and transformation matrix of an axonometry, and the sun position of either (date and time or azimuth and altitude).
- **Set3DProjectionSettings** (since 1.7.2): Sets a perspective or an axonometric projection for the 3D window. Every perspective parameter but sun is required: read a known good set with Get3DProjectionSettings and pass it back, with the values to change replaced. An axonometry changes only the values given: the projection type, the azimuth, the transformation matrix and the sun. The sun of either changes only the values given in it and is kept when sun is missing. The 3D window shows the change after a rebuild (RebuildView), e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage. Parameters: perspective, axonometry.
- **GetCameras** (since 2.0.0): Gets the Camera Sets (camera paths) of the project with their name, whether the set is the active one, its current camera, and its cameras in path order. Each camera has its element id, whether it is active in the path, and its perspective: camera and target position, distance, azimuth, view cone, roll angle, two-point perspective and sun, in the shape Set3DProjectionSettings accepts, so passing a camera's perspective there shows its view in the 3D window. Archicad cameras are always perspective; they have no name of their own.
- **Get3DStyles** (since 2.0.0): Gets the names of the 3D styles of the project and the name of the current one, which the 3D window uses.
- **SetCurrent3DStyle** (since 2.0.0): Meant to make the given 3D style, one of the names Get3DStyles returns, the current one. Not available yet: it checks the name, then refuses, because Archicad's API function for it crashes Archicad. Parameters: styleName.
- **StoreViewSettings** (since 2.0.0): Stores the current view settings (action Store) and puts them back later (action Restore), for example before and after a script that changes the view. The two must be called in pairs and cannot be stacked. Restoring may rebuild the view. Parameters: action.
- **ShowElementsIn3D** (since 2.0.0): Opens the 3D window on the given elements, as Show Selection in 3D does: they become the selection and only they are shown. Without elements it shows every element, as Show All in 3D does. Parameters: elements.
- **GetDocumentFrom3DDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Gets the defaults a newly created 3D Document starts with: name, reference ID, vectorial hatching and sun shadows, transparency, connection to the model, surfaces, boundary contours and the uniform cut, uncut, shadow and hidden edge attributes.
- **SetDocumentFrom3DDefaults** (since 1.8.0): Sets the defaults a newly created 3D Document starts with. Only the given fields are changed; existing 3D Documents are not affected. The fields are the ones returned by GetDocumentFrom3DDefaults. Parameters: name, refId, vect3DHatching, vectSunShadow, mustBeTransparent, intPlanConn, materialFrom3D, contureOff, cMater, boundaryDisplay, boundaryPen, boundaryLineType, attributeOptions.
- **Get3DWindowSettings** (since 1.7.3): Gets the 3D window settings: the pixel size of the 3D window and the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection.
- **Set3DWindowSettings** (since 1.7.3): Changes the pixel size of the 3D window and/or the zoom (scale and displacement) of its projection; the values not given are kept. Returns the settings read back after the change. Archicad may need a rebuild of the 3D window (RebuildView) before it shows the change, e.g. before SaveCurrentWindowAsImage. Parameters: hSize, vSize, zoomScaleX, zoomScaleY, zoomDispX, zoomDispY.
- **Get3DDocumentSettings** (since 2.0.0): Gets the settings of a 3D Document, given by its navigator item: the element and story filter, the 3D cut, the projection, the window and zoom, the uniform cut and uncut surface attributes, the source and the boundary contours, with the field names of API_DocumentFrom3DType. Parameters: navigatorItemId.
- **Set3DDocumentSettings** (since 2.0.0): Changes the given settings of a 3D Document, given by its navigator item, in the form Get3DDocumentSettings returns; the settings not given are kept. Returns the settings read back after the change. Parameters: navigatorItemId, settings.
- **Get3DFilterAndCutSettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the 'Filter and Cut Elements in 3D' settings of the 3D window: the stories shown, the filter mode and which element types are shown. Available from Archicad 27.
- **Set3DFilterAndCutSettings** (since 1.8.0): Changes the 'Filter and Cut Elements in 3D' settings of the 3D window; only the given fields and the listed element types change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: settings, rebuild.
- **GetGridSettings** (since 1.8.0): Gets the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window, and which database that is. Each database has its own grid settings. Available from Archicad 27.
- **SetGridSettings** (since 1.8.0): Changes the grid and snap grid settings of the database of the current window; only the given fields change. Returns the settings read back after the change. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: settings.
- **FitInWindow** (since 1.3.1): Zooms to the given elements or fits everything in the window. Parameters: elements.
- **ZoomToElements** (since 1.8.0): Zooms the current window, 2D or 3D, to the given elements: selects them, zooms to the selection and restores the previous selection unless keepSelection is false. Fails when none of the elements could be selected, e.g. all of them are on another story or on a hidden layer. Parameters: elements, keepSelection.
- **SetZoom** (since 1.7.3): Zooms the current 2D window to the given box in model coordinates. Parameters: zoomBox.
- **ResetZoom** (since 1.7.3): Steps back in the zoom history of the current window, like Archicad's Zoom Back. Parameters: numberOfStepsBack.
- **CreateSections** (since 1.5.0): Creates Section elements on the floor plan. A section looks to the left of its start to end direction, with its depth line that far on that side. GetDetailsOfElements reads the geometry of existing sections back. The floor plan must be the active window: creation fails while a Section or Elevation window is active. Parameters: sectionsData.
- **ModifySections** (since 2.0.0): Changes the name and the reference ID of Section and Elevation elements, which the Project Map and the markers show. GetDetailsOfElements reads those of a Section back as name and idStr. Parameters: sectionsWithDetails.
- **CreateInteriorElevations** (since 1.5.8): Creates Interior Elevation elements on the floor plan. Every consecutive pair of the given points becomes one segment, each with its own viewpoint - feed it the corner points of a room to get an interior elevation of that room. Parameters: interiorElevationsData.
- **CreateElevations** (since 2.0.0): Creates Elevation elements on the floor plan. The floor plan must be the active window: creation fails while a Section or Elevation window is active. Parameters: elevationsData.
- **GetSectionsAndElevationsDetails** (since 2.0.0): Gets every configurable setting of the given Section and Elevation elements, with their name and reference ID. Parameters: elements.
- **SetSectionsAndElevationsDetails** (since 2.0.0): Sets settings of the given Section and Elevation elements: pens, line types, horizontal and vertical range, model effects, story handles and markers. The name and the reference ID are changed with ModifySections. Parameters: elementsWithDetails.
- **MoveNavigatorItem** (since 1.1.7): Moves a navigator item to a new parent in the navigator tree, or to a new position within its current parent. Fails when Archicad does not put the item where it was asked to. Parameters: navigatorItemIdToMove, parentNavigatorItemId, previousNavigatorItemId.
- **RenameNavigatorItem** (since 1.1.7): Renames a navigator item or changes its ID. Renaming the Layout Book item of a placed Drawing also sets the custom name of the Drawing. newId sets the custom layout number of a layout and the custom ID of any other item. For a Project Map section, elevation, detail or worksheet the name and ID of the element behind the viewpoint are changed, for an interior elevation those of the segment the item stands for; the change is undone when the item does not show the new name. The name and ID of other Project Map items (stories, schedules, ...) cannot be changed. Fails when Archicad refuses the change or does not apply the new name or ID. With customName false the item drops its custom name and follows its Project Map source again. Parameters: navigatorItemId, newName, newId, customName.
- **DeleteNavigatorItems** (since 1.1.7): Deletes navigator items from the navigator tree: views and folders of the View Map, layouts and master layouts of the Layout Book, and independent worksheets and details of the Project Map. Layout subsets, View Map folders that are not empty, the other Project Map items and marker-linked worksheets and details cannot be deleted; the failed execution result says which case applies. An item that Archicad refuses to delete (in a Teamwork project: it is not reserved or the user has no right to delete it) is reported as a failed execution result. dryRun reports the result of the checks made before deleting (item not found, layout subset, View Map folder that is not empty) without deleting anything. Parameters: navigatorItemIds, dryRun.
- **GetNavigatorItemTree** (since 1.1.7): Returns the full navigator item tree for the specified map. With includeChildCount true every item also reports the number of its direct children. Parameters: navigatorMapId, publisherSetName, includeChildCount.
- **GetSchedules** (since 2.0.0): Returns the Interactive Schedules of the Project Map: navigator item id, name, ID and the folders they are in. Archicad's API does not give the rows of a schedule nor export it; to export one, put it in a publisher set with a spreadsheet format in Archicad and run PublishPublisherSet.
- **GetNavigatorParentItems** (since 1.7.3): Returns the parent of each given navigator item: the folder, subset or layout book item it is in. The root of a map has no parent and gets an error. Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **SetMasterLayoutContext** (since 1.8.0): Sets which layout's context the master layout of the current window is drawn in: its autotexts then show the values of the given layout. The current window must be a master layout, otherwise an error is returned. It does not assign a master layout to a layout. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: layoutDatabaseId.
- **GetAddOnViewpointRoots** (since 1.8.0): Returns the roots of the add-on viewpoints: the Project Map items created through the Archicad API by an add-on, as Archicad lists them to Tapir. Available from Archicad 27.
- **GetAddOnViewpointChildren** (since 1.8.0): Returns the direct children of an add-on viewpoint root or group. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpointId.
- **GetAddOnViewpoints** (since 1.8.0): Returns the details of the given add-on viewpoint items: their parent, type (Root, Group or Leaf), ID, name, view settings flags and attached data (base64 encoded). The output is aligned with the input array; an item that cannot be read gets an error. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpointIds.
- **CreateAddOnViewpoints** (since 1.8.0): Creates add-on viewpoint roots, groups and leaf nodes in the Project Map, with their ID, name, view settings flags (leaf nodes only) and attached data (base64 encoded). A group or a leaf node is created in the given parent root or group. Returns the identifier of each new item, or an error for an item that could not be created. Roots and groups can't be created in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpoints.
- **ChangeAddOnViewpoints** (since 1.8.0): Changes the ID, name, view settings flags or attached data (base64 encoded) of the given add-on viewpoint items; only the given fields are changed. Roots and groups can't be changed in a Teamwork project. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: viewpoints.
- **ReorderNavigatorItems** (since 2.0.0): Reorders the children of a navigator item to match the given order. Works around MoveNavigatorItem being unable to reposition an item within its current parent, by bouncing it through a sibling. Parameters: parentNavigatorItemId, orderedNavigatorItemIds.

## Graphic Override Commands

- **CreateGraphicalOverrideRule** (since 1.7.2): Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: name, ruleGroupName, criterionXML, surfaceRGB, linePenIndex, overrideContours.
- **GetGraphicalOverrideRules** (since 1.7.2): Returns every graphic override rule with its criterion XML. Needs Archicad 27 or later.
- **CreateGraphicalOverrideCombination** (since 1.7.2): Creates a graphic override combination from rule names, or replaces the rules of an existing one. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: name, ruleNames.
- **GetGraphicalOverrideStyleOfElements** (since 1.8.0): Returns the graphic override style each element is drawn with in the current window: for every overridable member (line type, pens, fill types, surfaces, ...) whether the active graphic override combination replaces it, and with what. Needs Archicad 27 or later. Parameters: elements.

## Issue Management Commands

- **CreateIssue** (since 1.0.2): Creates a new issue. Parameters: name, parentIssueId, tagText.
- **DeleteIssue** (since 1.0.2): Deletes the specified issue. With dryRun true nothing is deleted and no undo step is created: the response has dryRun set to true, and wouldDelete when the issue exists. Parameters: issueId, acceptAllElements, dryRun.
- **GetIssues** (since 1.0.2): Retrieves information about existing issues.
- **AddCommentToIssue** (since 1.0.6): Adds a new comment to the specified issue. Parameters: issueId, author, status, text.
- **GetCommentsFromIssue** (since 1.0.6): Retrieves comments information from the specified issue. Parameters: issueId.
- **AttachElementsToIssue** (since 1.0.6): Attaches elements to the specified issue. Parameters: issueId, elements, type.
- **DetachElementsFromIssue** (since 1.0.6): Detaches elements from the specified issue. Parameters: issueId, elements.
- **GetElementsAttachedToIssue** (since 1.0.6): Retrieves attached elements of the specified issue, filtered by attachment type. Parameters: issueId, type.
- **ExportIssuesToBCF** (since 1.0.6): Exports specified issues to a BCF file. With overwrite false it refuses to replace an existing file. Parameters: issues, exportPath, overwrite, useExternalId, alignBySurveyPoint.
- **ImportIssuesFromBCF** (since 1.0.6): Imports issues from the specified BCF file. Parameters: importPath, alignBySurveyPoint.
- **ImportMarkupsFromPDF** (since 1.7.3): Imports the markups of the specified PDF file as issues, like Issue Manager > Import PDF markups, without any dialog and without opening the Issue Manager palette, and reports the issues it created. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: pdfFilePath.

## Revision Management Commands

- **GetRevisionIssues** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all issues.
- **ModifyRevisionIssues** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the ID, the short description and the custom scheme data of the given revision issues. Only the given fields are changed. Issued revision issues may refuse the change. Parameters: revisionIssues.
- **GetRevisionChanges** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all changes.
- **GetRevisionChangeCustomScheme** (since 1.7.3): Retrieves the custom fields of changes (the change custom scheme): the key and the name of each field. The keys are the customSchemeKey values in the customSchemeData of changes.
- **GetDocumentRevisions** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all document revisions.
- **GetCurrentRevisionChangesOfLayouts** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves all changes belong to the last revision of the given layouts. Parameters: layoutDatabaseIds.
- **GetRevisionChangesOfElements** (since 1.1.9): Retrieves the changes belong to the given elements. Parameters: elements.

## Design Options Commands

- **GetDesignOptions** (since 1.2.9): Retrieves information about existing design options. Available from Archicad 29.
- **GetDesignOptionSets** (since 1.2.9): Retrieves information about existing design option sets, and in Teamwork projects the Teamwork identifier of the design options. Available from Archicad 29.
- **GetDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.2.9): Retrieves information about existing design option combinations.
- **GetElementsOfDesignOptions** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the elements associated with the given design options. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **GetDesignOptionForElements** (since 1.5.1): Retrieves the design option association for the specified elements. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **CreateDesignOptionSets** (since 1.5.1): Creates new design option sets with the given names. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **CreateDesignOptions** (since 1.5.1): Creates new design options with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **CreateDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.5.1): Creates new design option combinations with the given parameters. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **SetActiveDesignOptionsInCombinations** (since 1.5.1): Sets active design options in the given combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: activeDesignOptionsInCombinations.
- **ActivateDesignOptionsInCombinations** (since 1.8.0): Activates one design option in each of the given combinations, without listing all active design options of the combination. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionsToActivate.
- **DeactivateDesignOptionsInCombinations** (since 1.7.3): Turns off the given design options in the given combinations, leaving their other options as they are. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: deactivatedDesignOptionsInCombinations.
- **MoveElementsToDesignOptions** (since 1.5.1): Moves the given elements into the given design options. Use NULLGuid for design option to remove the element from any design options and move it to the main model. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elementDesignOptionPairs.
- **MoveDesignOptionsToAnotherSet** (since 1.5.1): Moves the given design options to another sets. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionAndSetPairs.
- **RenameDesignOptions** (since 1.7.2): Changes the name and/or the string id of the given design options. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **RenameDesignOptionSets** (since 1.7.2): Changes the name of the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **RenameDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Changes the name of the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **DeleteDesignOptions** (since 1.7.2): Deletes the given design options. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **DeleteDesignOptionSets** (since 1.7.2): Deletes the given design option sets. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **DeleteDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.7.2): Deletes the given design option combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **GetHotlinkDesignOptionTables** (since 2.0.0): Retrieves the design option table of the given hotlink nodes and placed hotlink instances: the filter mode (main model only, by options or by combination), the design option sets, options and combinations of the hotlinked module and which of them are active. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: hotlinks.
- **SetHotlinkDesignOptionTables** (since 2.0.0): Sets the filter mode, the active combination and the active option of sets in the design option table of the given placed hotlink instances. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: hotlinkInstances.
- **SetDefaultDesignOption** (since 1.8.0): Sets the given design option as the default, or the Main Model when no design option is given. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionId.
- **ReorderDesignOptionSets** (since 1.8.0): Moves the given design option sets before another set or to the end of the list. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionSets.
- **ReorderDesignOptionsInSet** (since 1.8.0): Moves the given design options before another design option of the same set or to the end of their set. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptions.
- **CanMoveElementsToDesignOptions** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether the given elements can be moved to another design option or to the main model, with the reason when they cannot. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **DuplicateDesignOptionCombinations** (since 1.7.3): Duplicates the given design option combinations and returns the identifiers of the new combinations. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: designOptionCombinations.
- **GetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews** (since 2.0.0): Retrieves which design option combination the given views show: only the main model, a combination, a custom set of design options or a deleted combination. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: navigatorItemIds.
- **SetDesignOptionCombinationOfViews** (since 2.0.0): Sets the design option combination the given views show, or makes them show only the main model. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: navigatorItemIdsWithCombination.
- **GetHotlinkDesignOptionTableDetails** (since 1.8.0): Reads the design option table of hotlink nodes: the design option sets, options and combinations of the hotlinked source file, and which of them the node shows. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: hotlinkNodes.

## Keynote Commands

- **GetKeynoteTree** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the whole keynote folder and item hierarchy. The technical root folder is not included in the output; the top-level folders and items are returned directly. Available from Archicad 28.
- **GetKeynoteAutoTexts** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the autotext tokens of the given keynote items. The tokens can be used as label text content to reference the fields of a keynote item. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: keynoteItems.
- **CreateKeynoteFolders** (since 1.5.6): Creates keynote folders under the given parent folders (or under the root folder). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: foldersData.
- **CreateKeynoteItems** (since 1.5.6): Creates keynote items in the given parent folders (or in the root folder). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: itemsData.
- **ModifyKeynoteFolders** (since 1.5.6): Modifies the key, title or reference of the given keynote folders. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: foldersData.
- **ModifyKeynoteItems** (since 1.5.6): Modifies the key, title, description or reference of the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: itemsData.
- **DeleteKeynoteFolders** (since 1.5.6): Deletes the given keynote folders including their content. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: keynoteFolderIds.
- **DeleteKeynoteItems** (since 1.5.6): Deletes the given keynote items. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: keynoteItemIds.
- **CreateKeynoteLabels** (since 1.5.6): Creates Label elements that reference the given keynote items via autotext. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: labelsData.

## Project Data Commands

- **GetProjectDataKeys** (since 1.7.3): Lists the project data stored by Tapir in the project: the names, the identifiers of the add-on objects that store them, whether they are kept on this client only and the Teamwork user who has reserved them. Project data is text (for example JSON) saved in the project file by scripts and Grasshopper definitions, such as their settings or the mapping of elements to an external system.
- **GetProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Gets the content of the project data with the given names. Parameters: names.
- **SetProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Creates or overwrites project data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name. New project data can be kept on this client only, or created as unique so that in Teamwork only one can exist with its name. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data. Parameters: values.
- **DeleteProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Deletes the project data with the given names. Parameters: names.
- **ReserveProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Reserves the project data with the given names in Teamwork, so that other users cannot change it. Returns the users who have already reserved some of it. Parameters: names.
- **ReleaseProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Releases the project data with the given names in Teamwork. Parameters: names.
- **RequestProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Requests the project data with the given names in Teamwork from the users who have reserved it, with an optional message. Parameters: names, mailText.
- **GrantProjectData** (since 1.7.3): Grants the project data with the given names, reserved by the current user, to another Teamwork user. Parameters: names, toUserId.
- **GetModulData** (since 2.0.0): Gets the module data Tapir stored in the project with StoreModulData: the given names, or all of them, with their data version and, unless includeContent is false, their content. Module data are the custom data sections of Archicad's ModulData Manager: text saved in the project file under a name, kept apart from project data (SetProjectData). Parameters: names, includeContent.
- **StoreModulData** (since 2.0.0): Creates or overwrites module data: text (for example JSON) saved in the project under a name, with an optional data version. Prefix the names with the name of your tool (for example 'my-tool/settings') so scripts do not overwrite each other's data. Storing module data is not an undoable step. Parameters: modulData.
- **DeleteModulData** (since 2.0.0): Deletes the module data with the given names. Deleting module data is not an undoable step. Parameters: names.

## MEP Commands

- **GetMEPElements** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the MEP (Mechanical, Electrical, Plumbing) elements of the project (every element the MEP API lists, and from Archicad 30 the electrical panels and devices), optionally filtered by type and domain. MEP elements are ordinary elements, so the generic element commands work on them as well (for example they can be deleted with the DeleteElements command). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elementTypes, domains.
- **GetMEPRoutingElements** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the details of the given MEP routing elements: domain, MEP system, offset from the home story, branch preference table, the ports logically connected at the route's beginning and end, the floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), route polyline, segments with cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), begin and end nodes, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style, insulation thickness and rigid segments, and nodes with their incoming and outgoing segments, preferred transition placement, elbows and transitions. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetMEPPorts** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the ports of the given MEP elements including position, shape, size, connection status (Archicad 27: whether the port is connected, from Archicad 28: whether it is physically connected) and connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports (from Archicad 28), the nominal size of piping ports (from Archicad 30), and the outer diameter, wall thickness and flange size (Archicad 30) of piping and ventilation ports. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements.
- **GetMEPDistributionSystems** (since 1.5.6): Retrieves the MEP distribution systems of the project with their domain, MEP system attribute, member elements, physical systems (from Archicad 29) and optionally their tree: the elements from the root element on, each with its previous and next elements and the connecting ports. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: includeTree.
- **CreateMEPRoutingElements** (since 1.5.6): Creates MEP routing elements (duct, pipe or cable carrier routes) along the given polylines with optional cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), MEP system and layer (also set on the segments, elbows and transitions), and optional elbow and transition defaults (preference tables and elbow radius factor, from Archicad 29) that apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: routingElementsData.
- **CreateMEPElements** (since 1.5.6): Creates MEP elements (Terminal, Accessory, Equipment or Fitting) at the given positions, optionally with another library part, size (from Archicad 30), MEP system, port sizes and shapes and a changed insulation, which apply only to what is placed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elementsData.
- **ModifyMEPRoutingElements** (since 1.5.6): Modifies the given MEP routing elements: MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings (cut plane position, floor plan display option, show projection and on-story visibility, from Archicad 29), cross section data (shape, size, preference table and reference id), anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size and connection style of all segments, preferred transition placement of all nodes, insulation thickness of the whole route (segments, elbows and transitions), and node positions. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: routingElementsData.
- **ModifyMEPPorts** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the given MEP ports (as returned by GetMEPPorts): shape, connection style (from Archicad 30), the flow direction of piping and ventilation ports, and the outer diameter and nominal size (from Archicad 30) of piping ports. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: portsData.
- **ConnectMEPElements** (since 1.5.6): Connects MEP routing elements to other MEP elements or routes. Merges routes, splits routes or creates branch elements as needed. The first or last node of the 'connectToId' route must lie exactly on the 'routingElementId' route, so for a tee pass the main route as 'routingElementId' and the branch as 'connectToId'. A failed connection says which condition is not met. Archicad 27 does not report the merged, split or created elements. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: connectionsData.
- **CheckMEPPortConnectability** (since 1.8.0): Checks whether MEP ports can be connected to other ports, for the given pairs of ports. Archicad 28 and later check the physical connection. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: portPairs.
- **GetMEPPreferenceTables** (since 1.5.7): Gets the circular cross section preference tables (referenceId, diameter, wall thickness, description) and the reference set of the Piping or Ventilation domain, optionally with the elbow, branch and transition preference tables, plus the rectangular duct tables of the Ventilation domain or the segment tables of the CableCarrier domain. Each table has its name and whether it is editable; the segment tables also have their segmentation lengths from Archicad 29. The rows of the circular, elbow, branch and transition tables say whether they are valid, and the reference set and the angle set say which of their reference ids and angles are defined. The angle set and the transition tables are available from Archicad 29. Every row has its index in the table, as ModifyMEPPreferenceTables expects it. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: domain, includeFittingTables.
- **ModifyMEPPreferenceTables** (since 1.8.0): Modifies the MEP preference tables of a domain, in the shape GetMEPPreferenceTables returns them: adds tables, changes their names, segmentation lengths (from Archicad 29) and row values and descriptions, deletes or empties rows, adds rows to the rectangular duct and cable carrier tables, deletes tables, deletes reference ids from the reference set, and adds and deletes angles of the angle set (from Archicad 29). Each table is changed in one undoable step. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: domain, tablesToAdd, tables, tablesToDelete, referenceIdsToDelete, anglesToAdd, anglesToDelete.
- **GetMEPSystemGroups** (since 1.7.2): Gets the MEP system groups of the project with their physical systems: name, editable flag, root element and MEP system. Available from Archicad 29.
- **CreateMEPSystemGroups** (since 1.7.2): Creates MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: systemGroupsData.
- **CreateMEPPhysicalSystems** (since 1.7.2): Creates physical systems in MEP system groups, optionally with a root element and an MEP system as their category. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: physicalSystemsData.
- **ModifyMEPSystemGroups** (since 1.7.3): Renames MEP system groups. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: systemGroupsData.
- **ModifyMEPPhysicalSystems** (since 1.7.3): Modifies MEP physical systems: name, root element and the MEP system used as their category. Only the given fields are changed. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: physicalSystemsData.
- **DeleteMEPPhysicalSystems** (since 1.7.3): Removes MEP physical systems from their system groups. Their member elements are not deleted. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: physicalSystems.
- **GetMEPToolDefaults** (since 2.0.0): Retrieves the current settings of the MEP tools per domain, without changing them: the routing tool (MEP system, branch preference table, floor plan display settings from Archicad 29, and its segment, node, elbow (Archicad 27 and from Archicad 29) and transition defaults), its rigid segment and branch defaults, the flexible segment tool, the library part, insulation and port settings of the terminal, accessory, fitting and equipment tools, and from Archicad 30 the electrical panel tool with its number of circuit defaults. Archicad 27 gives fewer settings, and only the shape of the ports. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: domains.
- **TransferMEPSettings** (since 2.0.0): Picks up the settings of an MEP element and injects them into other MEP elements of the same type and domain, like Archicad's pick up and inject parameters. Works for routing elements, terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings, flexible segments, branches, take-offs and (from Archicad 30) electrical panels and devices. Each target is changed in its own undoable step. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: sourceElementId, targetElements.
- **GetMEPPhysicalSystemsOfElements** (since 2.0.0): Returns the physical systems each of the given MEP elements is part of. Available from Archicad 29. Parameters: elements.
- **CreateMEPFlexibleSegments** (since 2.0.0): Creates MEP flexible segments through the given control points, or along a polyline of alternating line and spline parts (Piping), with the current settings of the Flexible Segment tool of their domain, optionally with the orientation (control points) or direction (polyline) at both ends. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: flexibleSegmentsData.
- **CreateMEPTakeOffs** (since 2.0.0): Creates MEP take-offs on the given routing segments, at a distance from the beginning of the segment (not more than its length) and optionally rotated around its axis by a multiple of 90 degrees, with the current settings of the Take-Off tool of their domain (by default the domain of the segment's routing element), optionally with their length and without insulation, which apply only to what is created. Archicad only has Ventilation take-offs. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: takeOffsData.
- **ModifyMEPElements** (since 2.0.0): Modifies placed MEP elements: the anchor point, orientation and library part of terminals, accessories, equipment, fittings and flexible segments, the control points, polyline (Piping, from Archicad 28), and width and height of flexible segments. Only the given fields are changed, in one undo step with one execution result per element; an item with a field that does not fit its element changes nothing. Archicad reports a 'libraryPartId' it does not find only after the item's other changes were made, so that item's error says which changes stayed. Available from Archicad 27. Parameters: elements.
- **GetMEPRoutingParameters** (since 1.8.0): Gets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: of a routing element its routing node parameters (preferred transition placement, elbow from Archicad 29, transition) and routing segment parameters (cross section, preference table, anchor, reference line offsets, wall thickness, flange size, connection style); of a routing node its elbow (from Archicad 29) and transition parameters; of a routing segment its rigid segment parameters (Archicad 28 only). Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **SetMEPRoutingParameters** (since 1.8.0): Sets the routing parameters of placed MEP elements: the routing segment parameters (cross section and preference table) and, from Archicad 29, the routing node parameters (elbow radius factor and preference table, transition preference table) of routing elements, and the elbow and transition parameters of routing nodes (from Archicad 29). Only the given keys are changed, with one execution result per element. A changed preference table is also set on each of the route's segments and nodes and injected into them, because Archicad 29 can otherwise keep the old one; the item fails if they still report the old table. Available from Archicad 28. Parameters: elements.
- **GetElectricalPanels** (since 1.7.2): Gets the electrical panels (distribution boards) of the project or the given ones: name, circuit naming, circuits, parent circuit, placement and the connected and demand loads in total and per phase. Available from Archicad 30. Parameters: elements.
